## Client language from the OS (os-language, branch poc/os-language, 2026-10-31)

Owner decision (owner-review question 14): the client picks its language from the real OS language on Windows, macOS and Linux, with no conversion table to maintain and no new library.

- **Algorithm** (`src/ClassicUO.Client/OsLanguage.cs`, pure function `OsLanguage.Choose`): (1) a language in settings.json that is available wins (`IVL`/`ZZZ` placeholders are ignored); (2) otherwise each OS preferred locale in order: its language subtag (exactly 2 letters; `fil` and the like are skipped) against the first two letters of the available cliloc codes; one hit is used; several are broken by the exact Windows code (`GetLocaleInfoEx(LOCALE_SABBREVLANGNAME)`, used only if it is one of the hits, so `es-ES` = `ESN` still gives UO's `ESP`), else Chinese by Traditional (script `Hant`, or TW/HK/MO) -> `CHT` else `CHS`, else English -> `ENU`, else the alphabetically first; (3) nothing matched, or an empty list: `ENU`. The output is the available code upper-cased (the packet and settings get `DEU`, as the real client sends). One Info line: `language: <code> - <why> (OS preferred: ...; available: ...)`, and `language packet: sending '<code>'` when the 0xBF language packet goes out.
- **Deviation from the spec text:** "the first two letters are the ISO-639 language" is false for two stock codes: Japanese is `JPN` (ISO `ja`) and Chinese is `CHT`/`CHS` (ISO `zh`). `CodePrefix` maps `ja` -> `jp` and `zh` -> `ch`; every other stock code (ENU FRA DEU ESP ITA KOR RUS PTB) already starts with its ISO code, as do the other Windows names (Czech CSY, Swedish SVE, Dutch NLD, ...).
- **Where it runs:** not in `Main`. The available languages are only known once the pack is open, which happens in `UltimaOnline.LoadUOFiles` (`Client.cs`), so the selection moved there: right after `PackAssets.Open` / `UOFileManager` is created and before `FileManager.Load(lang)` (before any text loads) and long before the language packet (sent at world entry, `PacketHandlers`). `SDL_GetPreferredLocales` needs no `SDL_Init` (and the code runs after FNA's init anyway); `SDL_PREFERRED_LOCALES` (the env name of `SDL_HINT_PREFERRED_LOCALES`) overrides it. `Main` now only clears a saved `IVL`/`ZZZ`. `ClilocLoader.AvailableLanguages()` lists the pack's cliloc language records when the pack can serve the text (it has `enu`), else the `Cliloc.*` files named in the client folder or in `files_override` whose resolved path exists; only three-letter codes in both cases (case-insensitive, names only: no table is read, so startup does not pay for it).
- **Not persisted:** `Settings.Language` is the effective language of the run; the configured one (settings.json or `-language`) is kept in `Settings.ConfiguredLanguage` and `Save` writes that unchanged. A language chosen from the OS is therefore never written (otherwise the first run would freeze it as a "profile language" and later OS changes would be ignored), and a configured language that is unavailable this run is kept for the next. An explicit `lang` in settings.json, or `-language`, still wins when available.
- **Tests:** `tests/ClassicUO.UnitTests/OsLanguageTests.cs`, 25 cases of the pure matcher (every case in the spec plus the Windows-exact tie-break, English variants, 3-letter languages, case and `-`/`_` splitting, no-enu sets). Suite 812 (787 at the base).
- **Windows client job (bench-000025):** each locale run with `SDL_PREFERRED_LOCALES`, JIT build, logged in to the local shard. All six pass: the language chosen, the cliloc loaded from the pack, and the language packet sent all match.

  | OS locale | Chosen | Rule | Cliloc (pack) | Packet |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | unset (en_US) | ENU | only match | enu, 117,725 strings, 8.8 ms | ENU |
  | de_DE | DEU | only match | deu, 18,622 over English, 10.6 ms | DEU |
  | ja_JP | JPN | only match (jp prefix) | jpn, 59,707 over English, 10.7 ms | JPN |
  | zh_TW | CHT | exact OS code | cht, 42,162 over English, 9.7 ms | CHT |
  | es_ES | ESP | only match (not Windows' ESN) | esp, 18,241 over English, 8.5 ms | ESP |
  | zh_CN | CHS | exact OS code | chs, 453 over English, 8.4 ms | CHS |

  Available languages were discovered from the pack: enu, chs, cht, deu, esp, fra, jpn, kor. Cliloc load times here are JIT, first call.
- **macOS and Linux were not run here** (no machine). They use the same SDL3 call and the Chinese rule; only the Windows-exact tie-break is skipped. A desktop whose language is Swedish with no `sve` cliloc, for example, falls back to the next preferred language, then ENU.
- **Memory cost:** none (a list of a few strings, one record directory read).

### Codex audit (coordinator scratchpad `astra-oslang/out.md`) (2026-10-31)

Six P2 findings; 1-5 fixed, 6 deferred. Each fix has a unit test on the production path. Unit tests 829 pass (812 before); both client builds (default and `CuoDevTools=false`) 0 errors. No client rerun: none of the fixes changes what bench-000025 showed (same pack, same six choices, same log lines).

1. **An unavailable saved preference was erased on save** (saved `RUS`, no Russian cliloc, German OS: the run used `DEU` and the next save wrote `lang: ""`). Fixed: `Settings.ApplyLanguage` keeps the configured language in `Settings.ConfiguredLanguage` and sets `Language` to the effective one; `Save` writes the configured one unchanged (`AutoLanguage` is gone). Test `OsLanguageTests.SaveWritesTheConfiguredLanguageNotTheEffectiveOne` (real `Settings.Save` to a temp file: RUS stays RUS, unset stays unset, an available `fra` stays `fra`).
2. **CHS missing from the Unicode-font decision.** Fixed: one helper `OsLanguage.NeedsUnicodeFonts` (CHT, CHS, KOR, JPN) replaces the ten copies of the CHT/KOR/JPN test in Combobox (2), CharacterSelectionGump, LoadingGump, CreateCharAppearanceGump (2), CreateCharProfessionGump, CreateCharTradeGump and RaceChangeGump (2). The `-language` argument now also accepts `CHS` (it fell to ENU). Tests `NeedsUnicodeFontsCoversAllCjkLanguages`, `SimplifiedChineseFromTheOsUsesTheUnicodeFonts`.
3. **Discovery ignored `files_override`.** Fixed: the candidates are the folder's file names plus the override map's names (`UOFileManager.OverriddenFiles`), each kept only when `GetUOFilePath` (the path the loader opens) exists, so an override to a missing file hides the folder's file, as it does for loading. Test `TextPackAuditTests.AvailableLanguages_Includes_Files_Override_Targets_That_Exist` (also loads the overridden language).
4. **Pack codes could exceed the 3-character language packet** (`ptbr` would be selected as `PTBR` and sent as `PTB`). Fixed: only three ASCII letters are selectable (`ClilocLoader.IsLanguageCode`), in pack and files discovery alike; longer pack identifiers are skipped with one Warn line per discovery, and `OsLanguage.Choose` applies the same rule to whatever it is given. Tests `AvailableLanguages_Lists_Only_Three_Letter_Codes_From_Pack_And_Files`, `OsLanguageTests.CodesOtherThanThreeLettersAreNotSelectable`.
5. **An empty or overrides-only pack store hid the file languages.** Fixed: the pack's list is used only when it has `enu`, the condition under which the loader serves from the pack at all (without `enu` every language falls to the files); otherwise discovery lists the files. Test `AvailableLanguages_Falls_Through_To_Files_When_The_Pack_Has_No_Languages` (overrides-only and empty stores; the loader then serves `Cliloc.deu`).
6. **Concurrent settings/profile access (pre-existing).** Deferred to the separate multi-instance audit: `ConfigurationResolver.Save` truncates and writes in place and loads read without coordination, for settings.json and profiles alike. The language selection adds no writes.

#### Codex audit round 2 (coordinator scratchpad `astra-oslang/out2.md`) (2026-10-31)

Two findings fixed, one deferred. Unit tests 832 pass (829 before); both client builds 0 errors.

1. **An unused malformed override aborted startup.** On Linux/macOS an override `cliloc.rus=` (empty target) made `GetUOFilePath` throw in `new FileInfo("")` during discovery. Fixed twice over: the alternative-casing lookup in `UOFileManager.GetUOFilePath` catches invalid-path and I/O/access failures and returns the path unresolved, and `AvailableLanguages` checks each candidate in its own try/catch (one Warn line, that language skipped, the rest continue). Test `AvailableLanguages_Skips_A_Malformed_Override_Target_And_Continues` (empty and NUL-containing target). The lookup is switchable (`UOFileManager.CaseInsensitiveFallback`, internal, default off on Windows), so the test runs the Linux path on Windows; the empty target threw `ArgumentException` there before the fix.
2. **Relative UO directory on a case-sensitive filesystem.** The fallback compared absolute directory entries with the relative probe path. The candidate is now `Path.GetFullPath`-normalised before the comparison (in `GetUOFilePath`, so loading benefits too). Test `GetUOFilePath_Resolves_Alternative_Casing_Under_A_Relative_Base` (relative base, `CLILOC.ENU` / `Cliloc.DEU`, resolves, lists and loads `deu`). Limit: on Windows `File.Exists` already finds a differently-cased file, so the fallback is not entered there and this test only fully proves the fix on Linux/macOS.
3. **Concurrent settings/profile access.** Still deferred to the multi-instance audit.
## T1 slice 1: the mutation funnel API, CUO_FUNNEL_CHECK, world items (2026-10-30, `bg/ecs-t1-funnel`)

Base `poc/modern-client` a9700dab7; code commit 566eff92a. Plan: ecs-transition-plan.md, T1.

- **API.** `WorldWriter` (`Game/Ecs/WorldWriter.cs`, `World.Writer`): `InScope`, `Enter()` returning an allocation-free `ref struct Scope` (nests), `UpsertWorldItem` (the item branch of `UpdateGameObject`, 0x1A/0xF3: create or take out of the container, the fields in the old order, `CheckGraphicChange`, `SetInWorldTile`, one ECS commit) and `RemoveWorldItem` (0x1D item branch: house, parent child list, `World.RemoveItem`). The GameObject properties keep their public setters; "the internal-setter path" is the scope: a write inside an operation is a funnel write, anything else is counted by the check. Making the setters `internal` is the compile-time version of the same guard and fits T4, once the remaining 313 sites are gone.
- **The fold.** While `UpsertWorldItem` runs, `WorldEcs.Sync` of its own item returns at once (`BeginFold`/`EndFold`), and the operation calls `WorldEcs.Commit` once where the old path's last Sync ran (AddToTile). The hooks it folds: `GetOrCreateItem`, `RemoveItemFromContainer`, the `Direction` setter, AddToTile. Same final components, same entity ids, same `EquipmentDirty` marks (the old wearer is read from the mirror before the operation in both paths), same corpse queue order (nothing else is queued between). `RemoveWorldItem` does not fold: the removal's own Sync of a corpse queues it in the active-items list, and the list's swap-remove order is observable.
- **Order changes (UI only).** In `UpdateGameObject`, the new-corpse `SingleClick` and the `ItemHold` clear now run after the tile placement instead of before; in `DeleteObject`, the paperdoll and minimap refreshes run after the removal (they only set a flag; `Layer`/`IsMulti` are read before). No world-state write moved.
- **`CUO_FUNNEL_CHECK=1`.** All 43 class-A properties (the `FunnelField` enum, including `Offset`, `OffsetX/Y/Z`) call `FunnelCheck.Write`, a `[Conditional("CUO_DEVTOOLS")]` method: absent from `-p:CuoDevTools=false` builds; in dev builds with the check off, one static load and a branch. On: writes to an entity its World holds (not detached objects, not stale instances, not Land/Static/Multi/effects) outside a scope are counted per field; the first 64 of each field, then 1 in 1024, resolve their caller by a stack walk and log `[funnel] direct write <field> at <caller>` once per (field, caller); `[funnel] direct writes N: <field> <count>, ...` every 5 s. Auto-properties became properties with backing fields (`_graphic`, `_x`, ...; none of these names is in the write-site scanner's field list).
- **Write-site budget.** `WorldWriter.cs` is exempt (the funnel; a test pins the exemption to that one file). `PacketHandlers.cs` 326 → 313: Graphic 14→12, Amount 6→5, Direction 7→6, Flags 11→10, Layer 5→4, X/Y/Z 6→5, IsMulti 2→0, IsDamageable 1→0, LightID 1→0.
- **Tests.** 759 pass in both `CuoDevTools` variants (720 at the base + 39). `WorldWriterTests` runs a copy of the old item branch and the funnel on two Worlds from five starting states (none, ground, in a bag, worn, corpse) × six packets (count 0, graphic inc, hue fix, damageable, corpse with and without the running bit, inc landing on 0x2006), plus resends and a sequence, and compares every item property, the mirror records, tags, entity ids, epoch, wearer `EquipmentDirty`, contents/equipment indexes and the active-items list. `RemoveWorldItem` has no unit test: `Entity.Destroy` needs a running client (`SendCloseStatus`); it makes the same calls in the same order. `FunnelCheckTests` (own collection, not parallel): counting per field, the caller, all four Offset setters, scopes and nesting, detached and stale objects, the operations make no direct writes, off counts nothing. Multis (type 2) are not unit-tested (CheckGraphicChange loads the multi from the files).
- **Bench and client runs:** the round-1 jobs (`bench-000007`/`bench-000008`, 566eff92a) were cancelled by the coordinator: round 2 superseded the code. The numbers for round 2 (b90d02c6d) are at the end of the "Codex audit round 1" subsection; round 3 in the "Codex audit round 2" subsection.

### Codex audit round 1 (audit of 566eff92a, gpt-6-astra), fixes in b90d02c6d

No P0/P1. Each finding re-checked against the code; dispositions:

1. **P2, the new-corpse `SingleClick` moved after placement: fixed.** It sends a packet, and plugin send hooks run synchronously, so the "UI only" note above was wrong. The upsert is split: `UpsertWorldItem` writes the values and the derived state, the handler runs `SingleClick` and the `ItemHold` clear, then `PlaceWorldItem` places the item, as before T1. Test: `The_Callback_Sees_The_Same_State_As_Before_T1` (the callback sees the same item and mirror state in the old and new paths, outside any scope). `DeleteObject`'s paperdoll/minimap flag refreshes stay after the removal (they only set a flag).
2. **P2, check coverage: fixed.** `FunnelField` gains `IsSAPoisoned` (`SetSAPoison`), `Steps` (`EnqueueStep`'s three `AddToBack`, `ClearSteps`, the step taken in `ProcessSteps`, `PlayerMobile.Walk`) and `AnimationState` (`SetAnimation`, `SetIdleAnimation`, `CalculateRandomIdleTime`, the timer write-back in `ProcessAnimation`). The `Serial` setter uses `FunnelCheck.WriteSerial(this, value)`: the object counts as world state when World holds it under the old or the new serial, which catches the 0xAF death re-key (dictionary moved first). The `ref Steps.Front()/Back()` sites were checked: all read. Tests: `The_Mutation_Methods_Are_Covered`, `A_ReKey_Serial_Write_Is_Counted`. The counters and the site table are not synchronised: they assume the single world-mutation thread (the game loop), like World itself.
3. **P2, scopes and the scanner: fixed.** `Enter()` is gone: the `Scope` type and `Open` are private to `WorldWriter`, so only an operation opens a scope. A scope owns its subject only (`WorldWriter.Owns(e)`; a removal owns its subtree, collected when the check is on), so a write to another object during an operation still counts. The scanner's exemption is structural: the bodies of `UpsertWorldItem`, `PlaceWorldItem` and `RemoveWorldItem` declared directly in class `WorldWriter` in `WorldWriter.cs` (brace matching); another method, a nested type or another class in that file counts (`The_Exemption_Is_The_Operation_Bodies_Not_The_File`). The 31 backing fields T0c/T1 introduced (`_graphic`, `_x`, `_amount`, ...) are A fields in the scanner; a write counts unless it is the field's own one-line checked setter (`set { FunnelCheck.Write(this, FunnelField.Graphic); _graphic = value; }`), and only in the declaring file (they are private; PlayerMobile's own `_amount` is another field). Test: `Backing_Field_Writes_Outside_Their_Checked_Setter_Are_Found`. Current count of such writes: 0. Budget 313 → 312 (Item.cs `UsedLayer` 2 → 1: `CheckGraphicChange`'s two corpse writes became one).
4. **P2, tests: fixed where feasible.** The wearer's `EquipmentDirty` tag is cleared before every packet; the active-items list, every child list (wearer, bag, item, contents two levels deep) and the mirror's contents and equipment indexes are compared as ordered serial sequences; each operation's mirror writes are counted (`WorldEcs.ItemMirrorWrites`: exactly 1 per upsert, against 2 to 4 hook Syncs in the old path); `RemoveWorldItem` is compared old-vs-new from four starting states (`GameActions.SendCloseStatus` now tests `world.InGame` before `Client.Game.UO.Version`, two plain reads, so a World without a client can destroy items); rejection, placement-pairing, fold and mobile-serial cases added. **Still untested in unit tests:** real tile placement (insertion order among equal priorities, parking): the test Worlds have no Map, and `Map` needs the UO map files; covered by the client runs (`-ecscheck`, `CUO_ECS_PARITY`). Multis (type 2) likewise (the multi load reads the files).
5. **P2 design, write-then-read-back: fixed (the pattern every later group copies).** An operation now: (1) resolves its object and rejects a foreign or stale one; (2) computes the authoritative values into an `ItemState` (serial, graphic, hue, x, y, z, direction, flags, amount, container, layer, multi) from the packet and the previous state, with pure helpers (`Entity.FixedHue`, `Item.CorpseState`), every read of the previous state before the first write; (3) writes the ECS from those values (`WorldEcs.CommitItem(item, in ItemState)`, no getter reads) and then the GameObject cache from the same values, in the old order; (4) only then runs the helpers that read world state (`Item.RefreshGraphicState`, the non-writing half of `CheckGraphicChange`: drawability and the multi load), which see the same values through either source, so the order holds when T4 moves the getters to the ECS; (5) placement as its own operation where the handler has callbacks in between. `CheckGraphicChange` keeps its behaviour for its other callers (it now uses `CorpseState` + `RefreshGraphicState`). Same tests pass unchanged in meaning (the old-path copy still uses the old code).
6. **P3, nesting: fixed.** The fold matches the instance, not the serial (`BeginFold(Item)`), and a second `BeginFold` throws; a second operation while one is open throws before any side effect; `Scope.Dispose` is idempotent and keyed by a scope id, so a copied or repeated Dispose does nothing. An exception mid-operation still leaves partial cache writes without rollback (as the old code did); the ECS is written before the cache, so the mirror holds the computed values.
7. **P3, foreign/stale arguments: fixed.** `UpsertWorldItem` takes no object any more: it resolves `World.Get(serial)` itself (the handler's own lookup) and throws on a live mobile. `RemoveWorldItem(item, out parent)` throws unless `item` is the instance this World holds for its serial (a destroyed one World still holds goes through, as `DeleteObject` did), derives the parent itself, and removes by serial only while World still holds that instance.

Tests: 774 pass in both `CuoDevTools` variants; both client builds succeed.

### Codex audit round 2 (audit of b90d02c6d, gpt-6-astra), fixes in 345fc7223

No P0/P1; five findings, each re-checked against the code. Also the coordinator's answer on violations.

0. **Violations in release builds (coordinator answer 1; also audit #4's "exceptions escape packet dispatch in release"): done.** Nesting, a placement that is not outstanding, a removal of an item this World does not hold, and an item upsert of a live mobile are `WorldWriter.Violation`s. In CUO_DEVTOOLS builds they throw (`InvalidOperationException` for nesting, `ArgumentException` otherwise). With `-p:CuoDevTools=false` they log an Error once per kind and the packet takes the pre-T1 path: `UpsertPreT1` (the old item branch: `RemoveItemFromContainer`, the field writes, `FixHue`, `CheckGraphicChange`, hook Syncs, no fold), `PlacePreT1` (`if (OnGround) SetInWorldTile`), `RemovePreT1` (by serial from this World, as `DeleteObject` did); a live mobile's serial returns null (the handler returns). `WorldWriter.ThrowOnViolation` (per writer; default from the build) lets the tests run the release path in either build: `Release_A_Nested_Upsert_Takes_The_Pre_T1_Path` and `Release_A_Bad_Placement_Or_Removal_Takes_The_Pre_T1_Path` compare it with the old-path copy. The fallback's writes are direct writes and count in the budget: 312 → 325 (`WorldWriter.cs` Graphic 2, IsMulti 2, IsDamageable, X, Y, Z, LightID, Layer, Amount, Flags, Direction 1 each).
1. **P2, Container write-then-read-back: fixed.** `World.RemoveItemFromContainer` is split: `UnlinkFromContainer(item, containerSerial)` does the gump refresh, the parent's child list, the list links and the tile, and writes no state; `RemoveItemFromContainer` = unlink + `Container = 0xFFFFFFFF` + Sync, unchanged for its other callers. `UpsertWorldItem` captures the old parent before any change, computes `v.Container` (0xFFFFFFFF when it unlinks, else the old value), unlinks, commits the ECS from `v`, then writes the cache's Container from `v`. `WorldEcs.CommitObserver` (tests; one null check per commit) sees each commit while the getters still return the previous values, as T4's ECS-backed getters would: `The_Container_Is_Computed_Not_Read_Back` (in a bag and worn: the getter still says the old parent at the commit, the commit says none, the item ends on the ground in both stores and out of the parent's list) and `The_Commit_Takes_No_Value_From_The_Getters` (every committed field equals the packet and the pure helpers). **Listed for T4** (schema, not in reach here without a mirror layout change): `Layer` for ground and contained items (the mirror keeps it only in `EquippedOn`; a corpse's layer is in the cache only), and defined defaults for new items before their first commit. Today a new item has no mirror record at all until the operation's commit (`GetOrCreateItem(serial, out isNew)` skips the creation Sync), so nothing reads a half-made record; once the getters read the ECS, the record must be created with defaults or the getters must tolerate its absence.
2. **P2, scanner partial-class hole: fixed.** `CheckedBackingFields` maps each backing field to its declaring type, not a file; a write counts when it lies in any declaration body of that type (partial declarations in any file, and its nested types), unless it is the field's own one-line checked setter. Negative fixtures for `MobileAnimation.cs`, `Views/MobileView.cs`, `Views/ItemView.cs`, `Views/View.cs` and `Mobile.cs` (a direct write and a nested type's write each found); `PlayerMobile`'s own `_amount` stays excluded. The real partial files hold no such write (the budget did not change from this).
3. **P3, admission after mutation: fixed.** Every operation checks "no operation and no fold open" before its first side effect (`Admitted`), so a rejected upsert creates nothing, replaces no destroyed instance and touches no outstanding placement. Tests: `Admission_Is_Checked_Before_Any_Creation_Or_Placement_Change` (absent and destroyed serials, an earlier placement still placeable) and `An_Operation_Inside_An_Operation_Is_Rejected_Before_Any_Change` (a real nesting from inside a commit).
4. **P3, single pending-placement slot: fixed with tokens.** `UpsertWorldItem(..., out bool created, out WorldWriter.Placement placement)`; `PlaceWorldItem(in Placement)`. Each upsert issues its own token (item + id); `Upsert(A) → Upsert(B) → Place(B) → Place(A)` works. A token is consumed by its placement; cancelled when a later upsert of the same item supersedes it, when the item is removed (funnel or pre-T1 removal), or, abandoned (a callback threw so the handler never placed; before T1 the placement was skipped too), when `MaxOutstanding` (8) newer ones were issued. Using a consumed or cancelled token is a violation. Id 0 marks a pre-T1 upsert's token (release fallback): its placement is the old one, no violation. Tests: `Placement_Needs_An_Outstanding_Token_Of_This_Upsert`, `A_Placement_Survives_Upserts_And_Placements_Of_Other_Items_In_Between`, `A_Placement_Is_Cancelled_When_Superseded_Removed_Or_Abandoned`. Cost: a list of at most 8 structs per World, a scan of normally 0–1 entries per upsert and placement.
5. **P3, mutable `Steps`: fixed.** `Mobile.Steps` is now a read-only `Mobile.StepQueue` (`Count`, indexer by value, `ref readonly Front()/Back()`); the queue itself is private (`_walkSteps`), changed only by the checked one-line methods `AddStep`, `RemoveFirstStep`, `ReplaceStep` (single-step replacement) and `ClearStepQueue`. The read sites now take `ref readonly`. The scanner counts calls of those methods on a mobile like setter writes, and any `_walkSteps` mutation outside their own bodies (`The_Walk_Queue_Changes_Only_Through_The_Checked_Methods`); budget unchanged (Mobile.cs Steps 5, PlayerMobile.cs Steps 1).

Tests: 792 pass in both `CuoDevTools` variants (774 + 18); both client builds succeed. Round 3 touches the hot path (the commit's observer check, the token list), so the E2 bench re-runs base, r2 and the next head interleaved and the client gate re-runs: `bench-000019`/`bench-000020` (on 345fc7223) were withdrawn before they started and replaced by `bench-000022` (base, r2, 36b46ef54) and `bench-000024` (client gate on 36b46ef54), which cover round 3 and the containers group together.

### Containers group (36b46ef54): `WorldWriter.PlaceInContainer`

`AddItemToContainer` (0x25, each item of 0x3C, 0x27's deny path) keeps its UI half in the handler (the `ItemHold` clear before, the gumps, the bulletin-board request and the trading gump after) and its world-state half becomes one operation, on the round-3 pattern, preserving the points of the Codex round-2 container notes:
- **Old order kept.** Container (`World.Get`; null: nothing, the handler warns as before), the item (`Items.Get`), a mobile holding the serial removed (`RemoveMobile`, as before; mobiles are a later group), then destroy-vs-reuse.
- **Destroy-vs-reuse and the corpse equipment exception.** An item whose Container differs is destroyed with its contents and recreated, unless the target is a corpse and the item has a Layer (equipment moving onto a corpse is moved, not recreated). The destroy runs in its own scope (`RemoveForReplacement`: owns the removed subtree for the check, cancels the item's outstanding placement), so the new instance's operation folds only the new instance.
- **What `CheckGraphicChange` saw.** It ran right after the Graphic write, so it read the old Direction (the corpse branch), the old IsMulti, and for a multi the old position. The operation computes the corpse state from the old Direction with `Item.CorpseState`, keeps the old IsMulti, Flags and Layer, and runs `RefreshGraphicState` where `CheckGraphicChange` ran: after Graphic and the corpse fields, before Amount, Hue and X/Y/Z. (For a non-multi it reads Graphic only; a multi in a container would load at its old position, as before T1. When T4 moves the getters to the ECS that multi case reads the new position: noted for T4.)
- **Values and links.** Amount as given (0x25 and 0x3C already clamp it to ≥ 1), `FixedHue`, X, Y, Z = 0, Container = the target. One ECS commit; then the cache; then, if the container changed, `UnlinkFromContainer` (the old parent's gump and child list, the tile; no state) and the computed Container; then `PushToBack`, also when the item already was in that container (the re-push moves it to the end of the child list, as before).
- **0x3C** keeps its bulk clear (`ClearContainerAndRemoveItems`) before the first add, outside any operation; the adds are separate operations. The clear itself is not converted yet (its `RemoveItem` writes are counted as before).
- **Not done here, listed for later:** child-order stamps in the mirror (the contents index is the ECS component index of `ContainedIn`; a re-push into the same container moves the GameObject child to the end, but the mirror does not re-add a `ContainedIn` whose parent is unchanged, in the old path too, so the two orders can differ; old and new agree on both, which the tests compare) and parent invalidation on re-push; `ContainerGump.CheckItemControlPosition`'s X/Y clamp after the operation (census 9.3, a direct write as before); 0x27's other deny branches (paperdoll, terrain), `ClearContainerAndRemoveItems`, and the equip packet (0x2E) are the next groups.
- **Release fallback:** `PlaceInContainerPreT1` (the old function's world-state part). Write-site budget unchanged at 325: `PacketHandlers.cs` Graphic 12 → 11, Amount 5 → 4, X/Y/Z 5 → 4, Container 7 → 6; `WorldWriter.cs` (the fallback) Graphic 2 → 3, Amount 1 → 2, X/Y/Z 1 → 2, Container 0 → 1. `PlaceInContainer` is a funnel operation in the scanner (and its pinning test).
- **Tests** (`WorldWriterTests`, old-vs-new on two Worlds as for 0x1A): five starting states (none, ground, in a bag, worn, ground corpse) × five packets (into the bag, onto the mobile, into a corpse holding an item, a corpse graphic on an item whose direction has the running bit, a container nobody holds), each followed by a resend (the re-push; one mirror write per operation); the re-push ordering against a sibling; a sequence through all packets and a 0x1A in between; the computed Container at the commit (the getter still says the ground) and the cancelled ground placement; the release fallback. 821 tests pass in both `CuoDevTools` variants (792 + 29); both client builds succeed.

A tiered-JIT smoke run (not a measurement) gave 1.343 → 0.527 µs for the new item and 0.133 → 0.155 for the update. ### Codex audit round 3 (audit of 345fc7223..36b46ef54, gpt-6-astra), and the fallback exemption

No P0/P1; one P2 and two P3 findings, each re-checked against the code and fixed. Also the coordinator's round-3 answer 1.

0. **The release fallbacks are funnel code in the budget (coordinator answer 1): done.** `WriteSiteScanner.FunnelFallbacks` = `UpsertPreT1`, `PlacePreT1`, `RemovePreT1`, `PlaceInContainerPreT1`, exempt by exact method name in class `WorldWriter` like the operation bodies (`Only_The_Funnel_Operations_Are_Exempt` pins both lists, and the exemption fixture now has a fallback body). So they can't become a general bypass, `The_Fallbacks_Are_Called_Only_From_The_Violation_Paths` checks every use in `WorldWriter.cs`: each is a call (no method group, no lambda) inside an operation's body, in a block entered on a violation (its header tests `!Admitted(`, or it called `Reject(` before the call, or it is the `placement.Id == 0` branch for a pre-T1 upsert's token), and no other client file names them. Each of the four has at least one such call. `An_Unguarded_Fallback_Use_Is_Found` is its negative fixture (a call after a closed rejection block, an unguarded `if`, a lambda, a helper method, a method group, another class). Budget 325 → 306: `WorldWriter.cs` Graphic 3 → 0, Amount 2 → 0, IsMulti 2 → 0, X/Y/Z 2 → 0, Container, Direction, Flags, IsDamageable, Layer, LightID 1 → 0 each (the file has no counted writes left).
1. **P2, a fallback inside the fold of its own item: fixed.** A nesting violation means an operation (or a fold) is open; the release fallback's old writes rely on the hook Syncs, and `WorldEcs.Sync` skips the folded instance, so a fallback on the same item left the mirror on its previous values (cache and placement changed). Each `*PreT1` path now calls `WorldEcs.ReconcileFoldOnEnd()`, which marks an open fold; `EndFold` then Syncs its item from its cache once the fold closes (nothing when no fold is open; `BeginFold` clears the mark). The mirror ends equal to the cache whichever of the outer operation's and the fallback's writes came last; the outer operation's continuation overwriting the nested writes is what a pre-T1 handler's continuation did too. Deferring the nested writes until the outer closes would change the order the old code had, so it was not chosen. Tests: `Release_A_Fallback_Inside_The_Fold_Of_Its_Own_Item_Reaches_The_Mirror` (four start/packet pairs, folding the same instance, against the old path), `Release_A_PlaceInContainer_Inside_The_Fold_Of_Its_Own_Item_Reaches_The_Mirror` (same container, so the folded instance is reused), `Release_A_Nested_Upsert_Inside_A_Real_Operation_Leaves_The_Mirror_Equal_To_The_Cache` (an upsert of the same item from inside the outer upsert's commit: the outer values win, mirror = cache). With the mark disabled, the five same-instance cases fail. Cost: one bool per World, a `_foldReconcile = false` store per `BeginFold` and a test of it per `EndFold`. (Round 4 removed this mark again: a nesting is now rejected, so no fallback runs inside a fold; see "Codex audit round 4".)
2. **P3, scanner holes: fixed.** (a) Any access of `Mobile._walkSteps` outside its declaration, the read-only `new StepQueue(_walkSteps)` view and the checked one-line methods now counts as a Steps write (`_walkSteps.Front().Run = true`, `ref _walkSteps.Back()`, an alias, an index read); fixture lines added to `The_Walk_Queue_Changes_Only_Through_The_Checked_Methods`. (b) Bare-write discovery is no longer only by folder: `WriteSiteScanner.ScanFile` keeps the Game/GameObjects folder rule and, in any other file, treats the bodies of declared world-object types (`class GameObject|Entity|Item|Mobile|PlayerMobile`, partial ones too) as GameObject code, the rest of the file not (`A_Partial_World_Class_Outside_The_GameObjects_Folder_Is_GameObject_Code`). Neither change found a write in the tree today. Not done: `StepQueue`'s `ref readonly` can still be unwrapped with a deliberate `Unsafe.AsRef`; no such use exists, and returning steps by value would copy on every read in `ProcessSteps`, so it stays a documented limit.
3. **P3, the container oracle missed the mobile branch: fixed.** `OldAddToContainer` (the test's copy of the old handler) now removes a mobile holding the incoming serial (`RemoveMobile(serial, true)`), as the old handler, the operation and its fallback do. `PlaceInContainer_Of_A_Live_Mobile_Serial_Equals_The_Old_Path` puts the wearer's serial into the bag and into a corpse, and through the release fallback: the mobile, its worn item and that item's contents go, and items, mobiles, child lists, mirror records and indexes match the old path. `AssertSameWorld` now also compares the mobile count and the wearer's presence.

Codex's other notes (no change): the test oracles share today's helper implementations; packet-level 0x3C/deny, real tile order, multi loading, opened bank/spellbook/trade gumps, parent-arrival sequences and ECS-backed getters stay for the client gate and T4 (already listed above). Tests: 833 pass in both `CuoDevTools` variants (821 + 12); both client builds succeed with 0 errors. The hot path gains one bool store per `BeginFold` and one bool test per `EndFold`; the rest is violation paths and test code, so `bench-000022`/`bench-000024` (on 36b46ef54) still stand for this head.

### Codex audit round 4 (audit of 36b46ef54..bcc6a7534, gpt-6-astra)

No P0/P1; two P2 and three P3 findings, each re-checked against the code. Coordinator direction: first establish whether production code can re-enter `WorldWriter` during an operation; if it can't, forbid re-entry instead of building recovery continuations.

**Re-entry: production code cannot re-enter the writer.** The operations (`UpsertWorldItem`, `PlaceWorldItem`, `RemoveWorldItem`, `PlaceInContainer`) are called only by `PacketHandlers` (`UpdateGameObject`, `DeleteObject`, `AddItemToContainer`; reached from 0x1A, 0xF3, the 0x1D item branch, 0x25, each item of 0x3C, 0x27's deny path). Packet handlers run only from `PacketHandlers.ParsePackets`, whose one caller is `GameController.Update`'s `NetClient.Socket.Drain`. Between an operation's admission and its scope's end the code runs: the world lookups and creation, `UnlinkFromContainer` (gump refresh flags, child lists, tile), `CommitItem`, the setters, `RefreshGraphicState` (the multi load reads files), `World.RemoveItem`/`RemoveMobile` → `Destroy` (gump disposal, OPL, `SendCloseStatus`). The only callout to foreign code there is a socket send, whose plugin send hook runs synchronously; a plugin that injects a packet from it goes through `Plugin.OnPluginRecv(_new)` → `PacketHandlers.Handler.Append`, which only queues it for the next `Drain`. No event, UI callback or plugin hook in that window calls a handler or the writer, and nothing pumps messages or drains the socket there. The handler callbacks that do send packets (0x1A's new-corpse `SingleClick`, the `ItemHold` clear) run between `UpsertWorldItem` and `PlaceWorldItem`, outside any scope, which the placement tokens already cover. So Codex's two P2 scenarios exist only through the `CommitObserver` test seam.

1. **P2, a nested removal leaves a ghost mirror record: closed by forbidding re-entry.** A nested operation while one is open (an operation scope or a fold) is a `Violation.Nesting`: it throws in CUO_DEVTOOLS builds (as before) and, new, in a release build it logs once and is **rejected**: the nested call changes nothing (`UpsertWorldItem` and `PlaceInContainer` return null, `RemoveWorldItem` returns with no parent, `PlaceWorldItem` leaves its token outstanding). The outer operation then completes exactly as without the nested call, so no stale continuation can publish over a nested change. With no nested fallback left, `UpsertPreT1` and `PlaceInContainerPreT1` were unreachable and are removed, as is round 3's fold reconcile (`WorldEcs.ReconcileFoldOnEnd`, `_foldReconcile`: a fallback can no longer run inside a fold), and the zero-id "pre-T1 token" branch of `PlaceWorldItem` (a default token is simply not outstanding). `PlacePreT1` (a placement that is not outstanding) and `RemovePreT1` (a removal of an instance this World does not hold) stay: both run after admission, with nothing open. Tests: `A_Nested_Operation_During_A_Commit_Is_A_Violation_And_Changes_Nothing` (16 cases: throw and release × outer upsert or container placement × nested upsert, removal, container placement or placement, each started from the outer commit; the world equals the old path's run of the outer packet alone, mirror = cache, the bag lists the item iff it holds it), `Release_A_Nested_Upsert_Is_Rejected`, `Release_Any_Operation_Inside_The_Fold_Of_Its_Own_Item_Is_Rejected` (four start/packet pairs; the world stays as built). The round-3 tests of the nested fallbacks were replaced by these. The tests' `NewUpsert` now returns without placing when the upsert returns null, as the handler does.
2. **P2, stale container links after a nested world upsert: closed the same way.** Codex's case (an outer `PlaceInContainer`, a nested `UpsertWorldItem` from its commit) is the `(PlaceInContainer, Upsert)` case of the test above: the nested upsert is rejected, the outer one pushes the item into the bag, and the item's Container, the mirror and the bag's child list agree, as in the old path.
3. **P3, the fallback gate accepted general bypasses: fixed on syntax trees.** The test project references `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp` 4.11.0 (tests only). `WriteSiteScanner.UnguardedFallbackUses` now parses `WorldWriter.cs` and accepts a fallback reference only when it is a direct call that is the whole expression of its statement, in the body of an operation declared directly in class `WorldWriter`, with no lambda, anonymous method or local function around it, reached from the then-block of an `if` only through nested then-branches and blocks, where that then-block runs an unconditional `Reject(...)` statement before the statement holding the call. The `!Admitted(` and `.Id == 0` header rules are gone (neither guards a fallback any more). Negative fixtures in `An_Unguarded_Fallback_Use_Is_Found` (17 uses found): `if (fast || !Admitted(...))`, a conditional `Reject` before the call, a deferred lambda and an anonymous method in a guarded block, the zero-token and negated conditions, `Reject` after the call, an else branch, a loop, a call inside a larger expression, a call after a closed block, a local function, a helper method, a method group, an expression-bodied delegate property (`Action<Item> Bypass2 => PlacePreT1;`), a nested type and another class. Codex's false positives are accepted now: `Reject (` with whitespace and a braceless nested `if (item != null) PlacePreT1(item);`. `FunnelFallbacks` = `PlacePreT1`, `RemovePreT1`; each has its guarded call (`PlaceWorldItem` 1, `RemoveWorldItem` 1).
4. **P3, a whole-line `_walkSteps` exemption: fixed on syntax spans.** Each `_walkSteps` access is judged by its own syntax node (`WriteSiteScanner.IsAllowedWalkStepsAccess`): allowed only as the field's declarator, as the single argument of `new StepQueue(_walkSteps)`, or inside the second and last statement of `AddStep`/`RemoveFirstStep`/`ReplaceStep`/`ClearStepQueue` whose body is exactly `{ FunnelCheck.Write(this, FunnelField.Steps); <one statement> }` and not in a lambda there. Fixtures added to `The_Walk_Queue_Changes_Only_Through_The_Checked_Methods`: Codex's `get { _walkSteps.Clear(); return new StepQueue(_walkSteps); }`, an unchecked method on the same line as a checked one, a checked method with a third statement, a method of another name with the checked shape, a lambda in a checked statement, `new StepQueue(_walkSteps, _walkSteps)`. The real Mobile.cs accesses (declaration, view, four checked methods) are all allowed; the budget did not change.
5. **P3, the mobile-serial oracle skipped the replacement item's cache and the removed instances: fixed.** `AssertSameWorld` now compares every item either World holds (cache via `AssertSameItem`, mirror record and tags), not the four fixed serials, so the replacement item under serial `MOB` is compared. `PlaceInContainer_Of_A_Live_Mobile_Serial_Equals_The_Old_Path` keeps references to the mobile, its worn item and that item's contents before the packet and checks they are destroyed in both Worlds, compares the returned replacement items directly, and has a negative fixture (a hue flipped in the replacement's cache after the commit fails the comparison). Its release-fallback case went with the fallback.
6. **Cost note (round 3): corrected.** The round-3 reconcile also stored `_foldReconcile = false` per `BeginFold` (the note now says so); round 4 removed the field, the store and the test, so the fold costs what it did in round 2.

Write-site budget unchanged at 306 (the fallbacks were exempt by name; no counted write moved). Tests: 845 pass in both `CuoDevTools` variants (833 − 9 removed or replaced + 21 new); both client builds succeed with 0 errors. The hot path loses the round-3 fold bool and the operations lose nothing else, so `bench-000022`/`bench-000024` (36b46ef54) still stand for this head.
## Hues: one source of truth, hues.bin retired (2026-10-31)

Branch `poc/hues-single-source` from `poc/modern-client` 78f9d153e. Owner decision (2026-10-31): one source of truth per pack file. `hues.bin` (the RGBA8 LUT, 3000 × 32) duplicated `hues_raw.bin` (hues.mul's 5-bit colours), so it is removed from the format. Tools will be built around the pack files and keeping two files in sync is error-prone; space was not the reason.

**What changed.**
- `Uo.Pack.HueLut.Build(ReadOnlySpan<HueEntry>)` (in `PackTables.cs`, next to `HueRawFile`) is the one LUT builder: row i = hue i + 1, column = shade, `PackColor.ToRgb8` (bit replication `x<<3 | x>>2`, bit 15 ignored), alpha 0xFF. It is the converter's old `ArtConvert.Hues` loop, moved.
- `HueRawFile.Read` now treats the file as untrusted: count 0..65536 (hue ids are u16) and the entries must fit in the file, checked before allocating.
- Client: `HuesLoader.Load` builds `PackHues`/`PackHueCount` from the raw entries; `hues.bin` is no longer in `PackAssets`' required-file list. A pack that still has `hues.bin` (`classic-1.0`) loads as before; the file is ignored.
- poc: `PackSet` builds the LUT from `hues_raw.bin`; `Synthetic` writes `hues_raw.bin` (5-bit ramps) instead of `hues.bin`; the converter no longer writes `hues.bin` (`ArtConvert.Hues` removed; the `hues` stage writes `hues_raw.bin` and `radarcol.bin`, and deletes a stale `hues.bin` in its output, e.g. a hard link from CURRENT in an `--only hues` test pack; deleting the link leaves the source intact). `Verify` builds the LUT from the written `hues_raw.bin` and compares it with an expansion done by hand from HuesLoader's entries (no `PackColor` call).
- `HueFile` keeps only a legacy reader (for the test below); `PackConst.MagicHues` is marked retired.
- Docs: pack-format.md (layout, magic table, version notes, §Hues rewritten, converter and size tables). pack-format-v0.md is history and left as is.

**Pixel-neutral.** `HueLutTests.Built_Lut_Equals_Legacy_HuesBin_Byte_For_Byte`: the LUT built from `classic-1.0/hues_raw.bin` equals the payload of `classic-1.0/hues.bin` byte for byte (count 3000, 384,000 bytes); it skips when the pack is absent. Two more tests: the expansion edge cases (0, 0x7FFF, bit 15 set, R in the low byte) and `HueRawFile.Read` rejecting counts -1, 3001 (past the end of a 3000-entry file), 65537 and int.MaxValue.

**Load time.** Measured inside that test, 200 runs on the classic-1.0 file (dev machine, busy with other work; Release, tiered JIT): `HueLut.Build` for 3000 hues median 177 µs, p95 384 µs, max 658 µs (cold first run); read `hues_raw.bin` + build median 292 µs, p95 530 µs. With `DOTNET_TieredCompilation=0`: build median 142 µs, p95 336 µs; read + build median 261 µs. The old path read the 384 KB `hues.bin` instead. Memory: unchanged (the same 384 KB LUT array as before, now built instead of read).

**Verification.** Client builds Release and `-p:CuoDevTools=false`: 0 errors. `dotnet test tests/ClassicUO.UnitTests -c Release`: 793 passed, 0 failed (6 new). Uo.Converter, Uo.Render.App, Uo.Client (and with them Uo.Pack, Uo.Render) build with 0 errors. No converter run on client data and no client run (the byte-equality test covers rendering).

**Survey: other pack content rebuildable from another pack file (report only, nothing changed).**
1. **`tiledata.bin` (TLTD) duplicates `tiledata_ext.bin` (TLDX).** Its flags, texId, height and layer are copies of `tiledata_ext.bin`'s fields (same source arrays in the converter, entries parallel). The only extra is `packFlags` (NoDraw bits), which the converter computes from id, flags and name, plus the source client version for the easel rule (manifest `sourceClientVersion`). Rebuild: one pass over 0x4000 land + ~0x10000 statics with a case-insensitive `nodraw` name-prefix test, well under 1 ms (same order as the hue LUT); tiledata_ext must then be loaded by whoever needs it (the client already loads it; the poc renderer `PackSet` reads only tiledata.bin). The ClassicUO client does not read tiledata.bin at all today, so it is renderer-only. 0.94 MiB. Strongest candidate.
2. **`SpriteEntry.flags` bit 2 (partial hue) in `art/sprites.bin`** copies the static's `PartialHue` tiledata flag (0x00040000); bits 0/1 (land/texmap) follow from which table and index the entry is in. Rebuild: a lookup per entry at load, microseconds. A field, not a file; two sources can disagree if a tool edits tiledata without re-running art.
3. **Lower mip levels of B5G5R5A1 atlas pages** (art, tex) are derived from mip 0 (alpha-aware box filter, 5-bit rounding as specified). Rebuildable but not cheap: every page decode would run the filter (about a third more texels written, CPU work per page on the streaming path), so it is the same kind of duplicate but not a cheap one. Kept for decode/upload speed.
4. **`map/<facet>/facet.json`**: `blocksX/blocksY` = width/height ÷ 8, and the region grid follows from them and `regionBlocks`; each region file's `RegionHeader` repeats facet, rx, ry (also in its file name). Trivial to rebuild, tiny; a consistency risk only if a tool rewrites one and not the other.
5. **`manifest.json` sizes and sha256** are derived from the files by design (integrity and delta patching), not a duplicate to remove.
6. Experimental only: the Indexed8 mip sidecar `anim/mips_NNNN.bin` is derived from the anim page and its palettes (not shipped).
Not duplicates: `radarcol.bin`, `animdata.bin`, `lights.bin`, `multis.bin`, `tileart.bin`, `equipconv.bin`, `palettes.bin` (its per-frame palette id is not in `anim.bin`) and the text/gump stores each come from their own client file.

### Codex audit (coordinator scratchpad `astra-hues/out.md`) and fixes (2026-10-31)

Codex confirmed the LUT conversion exact (all 3,000 rows / 384,000 bytes against `classic-1.0`, every consumer traced) and raised three findings. All three are fixed on this branch.

1. **P2, the converter could modify published packs.** Fixed, and wider than hues:
   - **Published roots are refused.** `Uo.Pack.PublishedPacks.EnsureWritable` runs before any write. `--out` (when converting) and the `--debug` folder may not be, or resolve to (junctions and symlinks followed component by component, `FileSystemInfo.ResolveLinkTarget`), a folder under a published packs root. Roots: `C:\Repositories\uo-packs`, `UO_PACKS_ROOTS` (`;`-separated), `--packs-root <dir>`, and any ancestor folder holding a `CURRENT` file that names one of its subfolders (detection; it also catches 8.3 or UNC spellings of the real root). `--out` no longer has a default (it was `uo-packs\classic`); the default `--debug` folder moved from `uo-packs\debug` to `%TEMP%\uo-converter-debug\<pack folder name>`. `--verify-only` only reads, so it may still verify a published pack.
   - **The pre-existing hard-link hazard.** Every converter writer opened its path with `File.Create`, which truncates and rewrites the file a `cp -al` test pack shares with the published pack. All pack writers now go through `Uo.Pack.ReplacingFile`: write a temp file in the same folder, then `File.Move(tmp, path, overwrite: true)` on `Commit()`, which replaces the directory entry and breaks the link. Disposing without `Commit` (an exception) deletes the temp file and leaves the target as it was. Covered: sprite/texmap tables, atlas pages (Kind 0/1/2; the Kind 1 Brotli stream now leaves the file open), regions, tiledata, tiledata_ext, every `TableFile` table (hues_raw, radarcol, tileart, equipconv), multis, lights, anim/animdata/palettes, record stores (gumps, fonts, cliloc), speech, `facet.json` and `manifest.json`; also `AnimExperiments --bench-chunked` (copy and write) and `Uo.Render.App`'s debug page compressor. The manifest skips leftover `.*.replacing.tmp` files. Not changed: debug PNG writers (not pack files; the debug folder is guarded instead).
   - **Tests** (`PackOutputTests`, 6): a hard-linked `hues_raw.bin` is replaced, the published link keeps its bytes and its link count drops from 2 to 1; one writer of each shape (table, Kind 1 and Kind 2 page, manifest, copy) breaks the link; a failed write leaves the target and no temp file; a configured root and everything under it is refused, siblings and `..` escapes are not, and a `CURRENT`-detected root is refused; a junction into a root is refused (created with `FSCTL_SET_REPARSE_POINT`, runs here); a symlink into a root is refused (skipped here: no symlink privilege on this machine).
   - **End-to-end:** a scratch copy of `classic-1.0` made with `cp -al`, then `Uo.Converter --out <copy> --only hues`: verify OK (hues EXACT), the copy's `hues_raw.bin` and `manifest.json` are new files (link count 1), the published `hues_raw.bin`, `hues.bin` and `manifest.json` sha256 unchanged. `--out` under a `--packs-root` folder is refused with exit 1 before anything loads; no `--out` is a usage error. The scratch copy was deleted.
   - **Had it already happened?** Every file listed in `classic-1.0/manifest.json` (3,010) was hashed read-only and compared: no size or sha256 mismatch, no missing file, no unlisted file. So no earlier `--only` run wrote through a link into `classic-1.0`. Side note for the coordinator: the published manifest lists `manifest.json.2026-10-31.bak` (the backup was in the folder when the manifest was regenerated); harmless, but it ships a stale manifest copy as pack content.
2. **P2, verify approved a pack without `hues_raw.bin`.** Fixed: when hues are selected (`--only hues` or a full verify), a missing `hues_raw.bin` is a failure ("missing hues_raw.bin (the pack's only hue source)"), checked before the early return for a pack without `tiledata.bin`. Checked by hand: a pack holding only the root tables minus `hues_raw.bin` and `tiledata.bin` now ends `VERIFY FAILED` under `--verify-only --only hues`.
3. **P3, the byte-equality test passed silently without the pack.** Fixed: it is a `[FilesFact(dir, files...)]` now, a `FactAttribute` that sets `Skip` when a file is missing, so xUnit reports it as skipped. New portable fixture `Synthetic_Raw_Entries_Expand_To_The_Expected_Lut_Bytes`: three synthetic entries (32 shades each, bit 15 set on every fifth shade) go through `HueRawFile.Write`/`Read` and `HueLut.Build`, and the result is compared with 384 bytes written out in the test, computed independently (a Python expansion), so CI proves the expansion without the pack.

**Verification.** Client builds Release and `-p:CuoDevTools=false`: 0 errors. `dotnet test tests/ClassicUO.UnitTests -c Release`: 799 passed, 1 skipped (the symlink test), 0 failed, 800 total (7 new). Uo.Converter and Uo.Render.App build with 0 errors. Memory: none (the temp file replaces the target; no buffers added).

### Codex audit round 2 (coordinator scratchpad `astra-hues/out2.md`) and fixes (2026-10-31)

Codex reviewed the converter safety work (`PublishedPacks`, `ReplacingFile`) and raised seven findings, plus a note that link-loop resolution was not fail-closed. All are fixed on this branch, each with a test in `PackOutputTests` (tests named `R2_*`).

1. **P1, recursive cleanup could delete a protected root through its parent** (`--packs-root D:\assets\published --debug D:\assets`). Fixed two ways:
   - **Design: no recursive delete anywhere.** I chose "delete only what the converter wrote" over "refuse folders above a root", because it limits the damage of any future guard mistake to files the converter itself produced. A full conversion now deletes only the files the previous output's `manifest.json` lists, any crashed-writer temp files beside them, and the manifest (`PackOutputFiles.ClearPreviousOutput`). A non-empty `--out` without a manifest is refused ("not a converter output"; choose a new or empty folder or delete it yourself). A manifest entry that leaves the folder is refused before anything is deleted. `--only anims` deletes the `*.bin` files directly in `anim/` (it used to delete the folder recursively; in a `cp -al` test pack that folder holds hard links). The debug folders lose only their `*.png` files. The stale `hues.bin` delete goes through the same guarded `PackOutputFiles.Delete`. A full conversion no longer deletes the whole `--out` folder (and its leftover empty subfolders); that is the intended trade-off.
   - **Also refused:** an output folder that *contains* a configured root (`PublishedPacks.EnsureOutputDir`; `EnsureWritable`, used for each file, still allows writing a file beside a root).
   - Tests: `R2_1_An_Output_Folder_Above_A_Published_Root_Is_Refused`, `R2_1_A_Full_Conversion_Deletes_Only_The_Files_Its_Previous_Manifest_Lists` (keeps an unlisted file, refuses a folder without a manifest, refuses `../outside.bin`).
2. **P2, junctions inside an accepted output.** `ReplacingFile.Create` checks the canonical target folder before creating the temp file, and `Dispose` checks it again just before the move. Every delete in `PackOutputFiles` checks its folder too, so no writer or delete can bypass it. Test: `scratch/art` is a junction to `uo-packs/classic-1.0/art`; the write, the single delete and the pattern delete through it are all refused, the published file keeps its bytes and no temp file appears there.
3. **P2, `Synthetic.cs` wrote `facet.json` with `File.WriteAllText`.** Fixed: it uses `ReplacingFile.WriteAllText`. The converter's debug PNG writer (`Png.Write`) also uses `ReplacingFile` now, so the debug folder gets the same check. A source scan (`R2_3_4_...`) fails if `File.Create/WriteAll*/Copy/Move/Delete`, `Directory.Delete` or a creating `FileMode` appears in `Uo.Pack`, `Uo.Converter` or `Synthetic.cs` outside `PackOutput.cs`.
4. **P2, unguarded commands and ignored `--packs-root`.** `PublishedPacks.ConfigureFromArgs` reads every `--packs-root` first, wherever it appears, configures them process-wide and strips them. Both `Uo.Converter` and `Uo.Render.App` call it before anything else, so `--bench-chunked` (which returned before later arguments were parsed) sees the same roots as conversion. `--bench-chunked`, `--make-synthetic` and `--debug-compress-pages` call `EnsureOutputDir`, and a refusal is printed with exit code 1. `--make-synthetic` now defaults to `%TEMP%/uo-synthetic-pack` (it was `uo-packs\synthetic`), and `PackSet.FindDefault`'s fallback moved with it. Tests: `R2_4_Packs_Root_Arguments_Apply_Process_Wide_Wherever_They_Appear` (a root without `CURRENT` given after the command protects writes) and the source scan above. By hand in scratch: `--bench-chunked <dir> <root>/v --packs-root <root>`, `--make-synthetic <root>/v1 --packs-root <root>` and `--debug-compress-pages <src> <root>/v2` are refused with nothing written; `--make-synthetic` and `--debug-compress-pages` into scratch still work.
5. **P2, path aliases.** `PublishedPacks.Canonical` (Windows) opens the nearest existing folder (`CreateFileW`, backup semantics) and takes its final path from the file system (`GetFinalPathNameByHandleW`), so junctions, symlinks, subst drives, mount points, 8.3 names, `\\?\` and `\\.\` prefixes and volume GUID paths all become one drive path; the not-yet-existing rest is appended. Roots are canonicalised the same way. When the target or a root is a network path, the target's existing ancestors are also compared by file identity (volume serial + file index) with the identity of every folder of each existing root. That catches a share of a published version folder, and a root configured by its UNC spelling. Fail closed: an existing component that cannot be opened (link loop, access denied, unreachable share), a device path without a drive letter, a missing file id, or `.`/`..` after a missing folder makes the check refuse ("cannot establish"). Elsewhere `Resolve` (link walk) remains the canonical form. Test: `R2_5_Path_Aliases_Of_A_Protected_Root_Are_Refused` (`\\?\`, `\\.\`, a root given with `\\?\`, the volume GUID path, `\\localhost\C$\...` for the target and for the root, and an unreachable share refused). By hand: `Uo.Converter --only hues --out //localhost/C$/<scratch>/custom2/v1/x --packs-root <scratch>/custom2` (no `CURRENT`, so only the identity check can catch it) is refused.
6. **P2, a volume root as a protected root.** `IsSameOrUnder` appends a separator only when the root lacks one (`C:\`, `/`). Test: `R2_6_A_Volume_Root_Protects_Its_Descendants`.
7. **P2, a failed commit leaked its temp file.** `Dispose` now closes, re-checks and moves inside `try`, and deletes the temp file in a `finally` whenever the move did not happen (including a failed flush or close). Cleanup errors are swallowed, so the original exception propagates. There is no fallback to writing in place. Test: `R2_7_...`: the target is held open with `FileShare.Read`, as `RecordStore` and a running client do. The write throws, the target keeps its bytes and the folder holds no temp file.
- **Link loops fail closed.** `Resolve` no longer swallows `IOException` and throws when it runs out of hops; on Windows the loop already fails in `CreateFileW` (`ERROR_CANT_RESOLVE_FILENAME`), which refuses. Test: `R2_A_Junction_Loop_Fails_Closed` (two junctions pointing at each other).

**Cost.** Each file write now opens two or three handles and checks for `CURRENT` in each ancestor folder, at create and again at commit. Converting `--only hues` still takes 0.27 s in total. Not measured on a full conversion, which is dominated by compression. Memory: none.

**Left on disk (for the owner).** While testing the UNC case from Git Bash, a mangled argument (`\localhost\C$\...`, one leading backslash) was a rooted path on the current drive. The converter wrote a 3-file `--only hues` pack under `C:\localhost\C$\Users\kamron\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\...\scratchpad\hues-r2\fake-packs\v1\x`. The guard was right to allow it, because that is an ordinary folder. A safety check blocked my `rm -rf` of `C:\localhost`, so the owner should delete that folder. The forward-slash form `//localhost/C$/...` was then used and refused as expected.

**Verification.** Client builds Release and `-p:CuoDevTools=false`: 0 errors. Uo.Converter and Uo.Render.App: 0 errors. `dotnet test tests/ClassicUO.UnitTests -c Release`: 808 passed, 1 skipped (the symlink test), 0 failed, 809 total (9 new).

## Memory footprint per client: first pass (2026-10-31)

Branch `poc/mem-footprint`, base poc/modern-client 88da64e3e. Measurement only, no defaults changed. Full write-up: `memory-footprint.md`.

- **Tooling** (fd5450021): `CUO_MEM_LOG=<sec>` (dev builds only; logs the GC heap, committed bytes and per-generation sizes from a background thread). Plus a scratch external sampler: private working set and commit at 1 Hz, and an address-space walk by protection and reservation.
- **Matrix** (bench-000014/15/17): AOT and JIT, Gpu and Legacy, hard limit on and off, with and without the warm-up. Britain, a walk, then the ocean, at 1920×1080. The "MUL" arm is invalid: the client needs a pack. Its replacement is upstream itself, in bench-000031.
- **Per client, Task Manager "Memory":** Gpu 800–855 MB, Legacy 650–720 MB. Commit is 1.25–2.0 GB. AOT and JIT are within about 20 MB. The hard limit has no effect. `CUO_WARMUP=0` saves nothing in pws.
- **Where the pws goes (AOT Gpu):**
  - GC heap 351 MB (about 45%);
  - write-combine GPU-mapped memory 153 MB, the same in both renderers;
  - native heaps 229 MB;
  - image 8 MB;
  - mapped files 0 MB (shared).
- **The ~1.1 GB of commit that isn't resident is GPU-mapped** (write-combine regions). The Gpu world's 516 MB of it is untouched: art pages 256, anim 128, instances 64, palettes, staging. It counts against commit and VRAM, not in Task Manager.
- **Occupancy in a normal session:** art pages 10/24, anim pages 10/128, about 4.3k instances of 2M. Grow-on-demand recommendation: start 12 art layers, 32 anim layers and 256k instances, grow at 75% and during holds, ceilings at today's sizes. Saves about 320 MiB of commit and VRAM per client. The large scene still reaches 82 anim pages.
- **LOH lead:** gen3 is 303–425 MB right after login. Only 3–4 gen2s run per session, all at login, so later LOH garbage is never collected. Working hypothesis: much of it is dead buffers (region decompression, pack pages).
  - Waste found: the 18.5 MiB anim palette CPU copy, kept after the GPU upload.
  - Waste found: the Gpu world is built twice at login (facet 0, then facet 1), leaving about 34 MiB of dead LOH.
  - The unicode font table is 20 MiB up front.
  - Pending: heap dumps (bench-000030), `CUO_WARMUP_GC=2` / `GCConserveMemory` (bench-000032), and the upstream baseline (bench-000031, net10 retarget in scratch only).
- **Memory trade-offs logged:** none added on this branch. The `MemLog` thread is dev-only and starts only with `CUO_MEM_LOG` set.

**Follow-up: dumps, upstream, GC arms (2026-10-31, bench-000030/31/32).** `memory-footprint.md` has no pending sections left.
- **Upstream 9a23aa253** (net10 retarget, scratch only, worktree removed): 572–576 MB pws at Britain, the land spot and the ocean, 1060 MB commit. Ours: JIT Legacy +76–94, AOT Legacy +139–148, AOT Gpu +224–243, JIT Gpu +244–267 MB pws. The difference is the managed heap (+116–126), plus 90 MB of native memory in the Gpu world only. GPU-mapped resident memory (153 MB) and Legacy's native heaps match upstream's.
- **The LOH is mostly live; the dead-LOH hypothesis is wrong.** A full compacting gen2 at login keeps 309 MB of it. Dead LOH builds up after login: the JIT Gpu dump at 50 s has 478 MB of large objects, 311 live and 167 dead (35%); Legacy has 117 of 313 dead (37%); upstream 19 of 189. Dead: 85 MB of 1 MiB decode buffers, 34 MB of smaller transient buffers, 21 MB of the first Gpu world's instance arrays (confirms the double build), and 17 MB of bench screenshot buffers.
- **Live LOH measured:** PackPages 59 MiB (Gpu) and 55 MiB (Legacy) of the 88 MiB cap; page-job and Brotli decoder working buffers ~61 MB (a pool; the estimate was 12). Upstream's 170 MB of live LOH is mostly MUL/UOP and map indexes (114 MB).
- **GC arms (AOT Gpu):** `CUO_WARMUP_GC=2` gives pws 787/803/816 vs the default's 800/808/815, with a 32.6 ms pause in the login hold (default 10.8 ms). `GCConserveMemory=5` gives 794/801/803, with 7 collections in play vs 2 (max pause 4 ms, no hitch). Both are within noise. A background gen2 left 64 MB free, and pws didn't drop: the GC keeps the freed LOH resident. No GC setting is recommended.
- **The land spot is confirmed** by the screenshots: the Britain moongate in forest, the same in both renderers. Our AOT client: 882 MB pws there in a 90 s run.
- **New recommendation (measurement first):** an allocation trace of the LOH in the first 60 s after login, on the `poc/mem-reduce` build, to find the ~35–60 MB of transient decode buffers still unattributed. Pool them where they recur, and log the pool's size.
- **Memory trade-offs logged:** none added; the decode pools (~61 MB per client) are recorded as an existing trade-off.

## Memory per client: palettes, facet switch, grow on demand (2026-10-31)

Branch `poc/mem-reduce` from poc/modern-client 2ced75119. Follows "Memory footprint per client: first pass" (branch `poc/mem-footprint`, `docs/modern-client/memory-footprint.md` there) and the owner's decisions of 2026-10-31: players run several clients at once, so per-client memory matters. Three commits, one per change. Rendering is unchanged: no shader, bake or sampling change; layer indices and instance offsets survive every growth step.

**1. Anim palettes: no CPU copy (71b1a6f46).**
- Readers of `PackSet.Palettes` (18.5 MiB `ushort[]`, kept for the pack's lifetime): only `Renderer.CreatePaletteBuffer` (the GPU upload) and a log line in the standalone `Uo.Client` (palette count). Re-upload paths: every renderer re-creation (facet change before change 2, DevBench `reinit`, startup) goes through a new `Renderer`, so the upload must be repeatable, but it needs no long-lived copy.
- Now `PackSet` keeps only `PalettePath`, `PaletteCount` and `PaletteOffset`; the renderer reads palettes.bin straight into the mapped transfer buffer (no managed array at all, not even a transient one). `PackSet.ReadPalettes()` reads a CPU copy for a future reader that wants one.
- The frame → palette table (`uint[]`, 4.8 MiB) was read twice: by `AnimationsLoader` and by `PackSet`. The client now passes the loader's table through `PackTables.FramePalette`.

**2. Gpu world: facet switch in place (5e0948ad4).**
- Before: the startup probe built the world pass for map 0; the login on Trammel disposed it and built map 1 (renderer, page arrays, instance buffer, chunk store, page-job buffers, dynamic array), leaving about 34 MiB of dead LOH and re-allocating every GPU array. Every in-game facet change did the same.
- Now `WorldRenderer.ChangeFacet(pack)` swaps the `PackSet` (same pack, `WithFacet`), drops the chunks and regions (`ChunkStore.ChangeFacet`), and keeps the device resources, the resident pages, the workers and every CPU array. Bakes and region loads in flight are discarded when they finish; their regions are orphaned, not pooled, so no worker writes into a region the new facet reuses. A failed switch falls back to the old rebuild.
- The world object now survives a facet change, so the client's two caches keyed on it (GPU item cache, static season remap) also key on `world.Pack`. `WorldSettleGate` already treats a facet change as a discontinuity (hold). The new pack's bake switches (water wobble, remaps) start fresh, exactly as with a rebuilt world.

**3. Grow on demand (3615c22ca).**
- Art page array 12 → 24 layers, anim layers 32 → 64 → 128, instance buffer 256k → 512k → 1M → 2M instances. The ceilings are the old fixed sizes. `CUO_GPU_GROW=0` starts at the ceilings (A/B).
- Policy (`Uo.Render/GrowthPolicy.cs`, unit-tested): never at the ceiling; at once when starved (a loaded page with no free layer, or an instance allocation that failed last frame), so growth always beats eviction below the ceiling; at 75% occupancy during a hold (the settle gate's stream-only frames) or a camera jump; otherwise after 120 frames at 75%.
- A step creates the larger texture or buffer and copies the old contents GPU-side at the start of the frame's copy pass, before that frame's uploads (`SDL_CopyGPUTextureToTexture` per resident layer and mip; `SDL_CopyGPUBufferToBuffer`), then releases the old one (SDL frees it after the frames in flight). Same command buffer, same layer indices and offsets: nothing is dropped or flickers.
- Each step logs `GPU world: grown at frame N: art layers a/24 (k steps, last x->y t ms, max, total); anim layers ...; instances ...` (main-thread time: create + record; the GPU copy runs inside that frame). The `GPU world:` trace line now ends with `instances used u/c`.

**Memory trade-off log (per client).** "Computed" is from the sizes; "measured" is job bench-000035 (base 2ced75119, new 3615c22ca, and new with `CUO_GPU_GROW=0`; one run per arm, JIT Release, unpinned; see "Measured" below for the method and the noise).

| item | before | after | computed saving | measured (bench-000035) | what it costs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| anim palettes CPU copy (managed LOH, resident) | 18.5 MiB | 0 | 18.5 MiB | with the next two rows: GC heap at the last GC before Britain 450 → 400 MB (-50); GC heap commit at 120 s 458 → 401 MiB (-57); its resident part 351 → 319 MiB (-32). Task Manager private WS: -6 to -9 MiB, inside the ±20 MiB run-to-run noise | each new renderer reads 18.5 MiB from palettes.bin (once per session now, see 2) |
| frame → palette table, second copy (managed LOH, resident) | 4.8 MiB | 0 | 4.8 MiB | (above) | none (shared with AnimationsLoader) |
| second world pass at login (dead managed LOH until a gen2; nothing collects the LOH after login) | ~34 MiB | 0 | ~34 MiB | (above). After the Trammel → Felucca → Trammel round trip: GC heap 709 → 618 MB (-91), private commit 2480 → 2182 MiB (-298), private WS 1100 → 1066 MiB (-34) | none; facet changes also keep their resident pages (no re-upload) |
| GPU re-allocation at login and facet change (commit churn) | ~525 MiB freed and re-allocated | 0 | churn only | peak commit 2741 → 2242 MiB (-499: base's rebuild on the facet return, +499 MiB for a moment); commit spike on the return +499 → +37 MiB | none |
| art page array (GPU commit / VRAM, never resident) | 256 MiB | 128 MiB | 128 MiB | **0**: it grew 12 → 24 at frame 15 of every session (13 pages resident after login), 1.19 ms | one growth step at login; both arrays exist for that frame (384 MiB) |
| anim page array (GPU) | 128 MiB | 32 MiB | 96 MiB | with the instance buffer, in Britain: private commit -145 MiB (1947 → 1802 at 120 s), of which write-combined (GPU-mapped) -111 MiB. Back to 128 in the large scene (two steps), so 0 after a crowd | two steps in the large scene (0.71 and 0.98 ms) |
| instance buffer (GPU) | 64 MiB | 8 MiB | 56 MiB | (above). Never grew (peak 40,097 of 262,144); after the large scene new is still 54–66 MiB of commit below new-nogrow | steps only past 192k used instances |
| CPU instance mirror (managed, partly resident) | 18 MiB | 9 MiB | 9 MiB commit | not separable from the GC noise | resized (existing doubling) past 256k |

- **Totals, measured:** in Britain at 120 s, private commit 2010 → 1802 MiB (-208 per client: -63 from changes 1 and 2, -145 from 3); after a facet round trip -298 MiB; peak -499 MiB. Task Manager "Memory" (private WS) moves by -6 to -34 MiB: the GC heap really shrinks (-50 MB at login, -91 MB after the round trip), but at login the saving is inside the run-to-run noise, and other native read-write memory is 25 MiB higher in both new arms (open question below). Across four clients: about 0.8 GB of commit in Britain, 1.2 GB after a facet change. The computed 280 MiB of GPU commit is 145 MiB in practice, because the art array grows to its old size at login; and 54–66 MiB after a crowded scene (only the instance buffer stays small).
- **Growth stalls:** none visible. Three steps in the whole run (below), 0.71–1.19 ms of main-thread time each, none of them in a frame over 8 ms.

### Codex audit (coordinator scratchpad `astra-memreduce/out.md`) (2026-10-31)

Three P2s, all fixed (one commit after 5c6d516b4). The rest of the audit was clean: facet isolation (late bakes and region loads can't populate the new facet), picking/selection/caches keyed on `world.Pack`, facet-switch failure handling, GPU copies and handle refresh, allocator growth and the CPU mirror, and the CPU palette paths.

| # | finding | disposition | test |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Unchecked palette counts: `paletteCount = 8,388,609` is 4,294,967,808 bytes, which narrowed to `uint`/`int` allocates and reads 512; negative counts got through | Fixed. `AnimPaletteFile.ReadLayout(Stream)` validates before anything is sized: counts non-negative and within `MaxPalettes` (65,536 = `MaxPaletteBytes`, 32 MiB; the shipped pack has 37.9k / 18.5 MiB) and `MaxFrames` (2^24), and the frame table plus the whole payload inside the file (checked arithmetic). `ValidateFramePalette` checks every id is below the count or `uint.MaxValue`; `PackSet` validates a shared (AnimationsLoader) table too and checks it matches `AnimFrames.Length`. `Read`, `ReadFramePalette` and `AnimationsLoader.Load` all go through it. The renderer re-checks with `Renderer.PaletteUploadSize` (checked, explicit byte limit, extent against the open file's length) | `Renderer/PaletteFileTests.cs` (6): the audit's wrapping count, negative counts, an overlong frame table, a truncated payload, out-of-range ids, a valid file |
| 2 | An upload batch could evict before growing: growth was checked once, starved only when already full, so with 11/12 layers and two loaded pages the second upload evicted a resident page (or waited, if all were visible) | Fixed. `PageResidency.Upload` counts the batch's eligible uploads (loaded, successful, within the remaining budget) and asks `GrowthPolicy.CheckBatch`: starved when they don't all fit in the free layers. It grows once to `GrowthPolicy.NextFor` (doubled until the batch fits, at most the ceiling), so one copy covers a batch larger than one doubling. Growing inside the loop was not chosen: it would copy layers uploaded earlier in the same copy pass | `GrowthPolicyTests`: `A_batch_that_crosses_capacity_grows_before_uploading` (the audit's 11/12 + 2 case), `A_batch_that_fits_keeps_the_deferral`, `A_batch_never_grows_past_the_ceiling`, `NextFor_doubles_until_the_batch_fits_in_one_step` |
| 3 | A palette read failure leaked the palette buffer and the mapped transfer buffer, and the exception escaped the renderer constructor, leaking everything it had created (`CreateExternal`'s cleanup starts after construction) | Fixed. `CreatePaletteBuffer` validates (`PaletteUploadSize` against the open file) before allocating, and a `finally` unmaps and releases the transfer buffer and releases the palette buffer on every failure path (also a failed map or command-buffer acquire). The private constructor's body is wrapped: on any exception it calls `Dispose`, which now skips null handles and releases the window only if it was claimed; the window constructor disposes (and destroys its own device) when claiming the window fails | The validation half is covered by `PaletteFileTests.A_truncated_payload_is_rejected_before_any_upload` (including a file that shrank after the pack loaded). The release paths need a GPU device and are not unit-tested; both client builds compile them |

- **Cost:** none on the normal path. The checks run once at load (one pass over the 1.2M-entry frame table, sub-millisecond), and the batch count is one loop over the staging slots per frame. Job bench-000035 (measuring 3615c22ca) still stands for the memory numbers; it was not resubmitted.
- Unit tests 813 pass (803 + 10 new).
