## Music decoded by dr_mp3 (dr-mp3, branch poc/dr-mp3, 2026-10-31)

Base `f0d09f8ed` (poc/modern-client). Owner decision Q10 ([data-formats.md](data-formats.md) §10): music stays MP3 and is decoded by dr_mp3 instead of MP3Sharp. Phase 1 only covers the loose `Music/Digital/*.mp3` files. The music record store in the pack waits for the converter work on another branch.

**dr_mp3.** `external/dr_libs/dr_mp3.h` is v0.7.4 from mackron/dr_libs, tag `mp3-0.7.4`, commit `aec2dd20667f54acfdb66031217df6d240f56c52`, sha256 `f5c8020eeebb79877184432efdd2651f24869f5bb8f379d45450fd0aed1ee915` (public domain / MIT-0). The coordinator fetched and reviewed it; it is copied unchanged, with `SOURCE.txt` beside it. `.gitattributes` marks `external/dr_libs/**` `-text`, so the hash holds on Windows checkouts, and `*.sh` `eol=lf`. It is pinned for 0.7.4's bounds checks in the Xing/Info/LAME parser. 0.7.4 parses the LAME tag and **trims by itself**: reads skip the Info frame and the delay (`encoder delay + 529`) and stop before the padding (`padding - 529`), and `seek(0)` skips the delay again. So nothing trims twice; the C# side only reports the values.

**Native build** (`src/native/cuo_mp3`). `cuo_mp3.c` includes dr_mp3 with `DR_MP3_NO_STDIO` (no fopen paths) and SIMD on. It exposes a flat C API with an opaque handle: `open_memory`, `get_info`, `read_s16`, `seek`, `get_frame_count` and `version`. It also refuses streams outside 1-2 channels and 8-48 kHz.
- **win-x64, built here.** `build-win-x64.sh` runs MSVC 14.51 / SDK 10.0.26100 straight from Git Bash, with paths from vswhere and no vcvars. Its outputs are committed, like SDL3.dll:
  - `external/x64/cuo_mp3.dll` (141 KB, static CRT, so no VC++ redistributable is needed);
  - `external/x64-static/cuo_mp3.lib` (115 KB, built with `/Zl` so ILC's link picks the CRT).
- **linux-x64 and macOS** (arm64, x86_64 or universal): `CMakeLists.txt` and `build-unix.sh` write `external/lib64[-static]` and `external/osx[-static]`. **Not run:** there is no Linux or Mac here.
- **NativeAOT.** When the static archive exists for the RID, `ClassicUO.Client.csproj` adds `DirectPInvoke cuo_mp3` and the archive as `NativeLibrary`, and drops the shared library from the publish. The win-x64 publish shows all four signs: `--directpinvoke:cuo_mp3` in `cuo.ilc.rsp`, the `.lib` in `link.rsp`, no `cuo_mp3.dll` in the output and no `cuo_mp3.dll` string in `cuo.exe`. JIT builds and the tests load the DLL, which `ClassicUO.IO.csproj` copies to every output (`CopyToPublishDirectory=Never`).

**Client** (`ClassicUO.IO/Audio`):
- **`Mp3Validator`** runs before any native call. It requires:
  - at most 32 MB (the largest stock track is 12.9 MB);
  - an ID3v2 size that fits the data;
  - within 64 KB, a Layer III header (no reserved version or rate, no free-format or bad bitrate) whose next header is valid and consistent, or which ends the data.
- **`Mp3Decoder`** (LibraryImport) opens from a span, a stream or a file into native memory with one copy. It reads s16 frames, seeks, and reports the rate, channels, delay, padding and total frames (the Xing count minus delay and padding, else a header scan). Bad data returns `false` and a reason, never an exception.
- **`MusicStream` + `MusicDecodeWorker`.** One background thread ("Music decode") opens the file and decodes 8192-frame buffers (32 KB stereo, the old chunk size), keeping 4 ready ahead.
  - `UOMusic.Update` (game thread, every frame) only submits ready buffers, keeps 3 queued in FAudio and returns each buffer to the pool (FNA copies on submit). No MP3 work runs on the game thread now.
  - `Play` returns at once, and the sound starts when the first buffer is ready (`Trace`: `music <name>: first buffer after N ms`; loop wraps log `music <name>: looped (n)`).
  - A failure logs `music <name>: skipped (<reason>)` once, and the track is skipped.
- **The loop-remainder bug is fixed.** The old `GetBuffer` rewound and read the rest into the same buffer, but returned the pre-rewind byte count, so the wrapped samples were dropped: a short buffer at every loop. The fill now seeks to 0 and keeps filling. An empty read right after a seek ends the track instead of spinning.
- **Gapless loops.** For the 55 LAME-tagged tracks the seam is sample-exact: a unit test on Boattravel.mp3 checks that the PCM after the wrap equals the first 40,000 samples. The 36 tracks without a LAME tag keep the decoder's 529-sample start and the encoder padding, as every decoder does without the tag.
- `Sound.Play` is now virtual and `DurationTime` settable, so music can start asynchronously. `IsPlaying` keeps its old meaning: the first buffer's duration.
- **Memory (a deliberate trade-off).** Per playing track:
  - the MP3 bytes in native memory: 1.2 MB on average, 12.9 MB at most;
  - up to 6 × 32 KB PCM buffers (192 KB).

  There are at most two music slots (normal and war). The decoder and its file copy are freed on stop and at the end of a non-looping track. MP3Sharp streamed from the file through a 32 KB buffer, so this costs about 1-13 MB per playing track. In return there is no file I/O after open and no decode on the game thread.

**Parity, all 91 tracks.** Three decoders: MP3Sharp (before removal), dr_mp3, and mpg123 inside libsndfile 1.2.2 (the survey's venv) as a third reference. Each pair was aligned by searching ±6000 frames, then compared over the whole overlap.

| | max abs diff (LSB) | mean abs diff | SNR vs mpg123 | length vs mpg123 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| dr_mp3 | 2 (3 tracks), else 1 | 0.001 | 80.8 dB min, 102.6 dB median | identical for all 91, offset 0 |
| MP3Sharp | 69 | 6.6 | 45.5 dB min, 53.3 dB median | 64 tracks differ (below) |

Where MP3Sharp is wrong:
- **Precision.** It differs from both other decoders by 6.6 LSB on average (about -53 dB). That is inaudible, but the error is MP3Sharp's, since dr_mp3 and mpg123 agree to 1-2 LSB.
- **No gapless handling** on the 55 LAME tracks. It plays the Info frame as silence plus the encoder and decoder delay at the start (1,681 frames at 22.05 kHz, 2,257 at 44.1 kHz), and the padding at the end (352-1,125 frames). That is the 0.1 s gap at each loop that the survey saw.
- **It drops the last MP3 frame** of 9 of the 36 untagged tracks (1,152 frames; 576 for TheWanderer.mp3): BattleOnStones, Castle, dread_horn_area, elf_city_1, Festival, grizzle_dungeon, melisandes_lair, paroxysmus_lair and TheWanderer.

**Fuzzing** (`src/native/cuo_mp3/fuzz`). This box has no clang, so the build uses MSVC's libFuzzer and ASan (`-fsanitize=fuzzer -fsanitize=address`). For each input the target:
- copies it to an exact-size heap block;
- opens it and reads up to 2^20 frames;
- seeks to 0, to the middle and past the end, and reads again;
- counts the frames.

The 273 seeds are the first 16 KB, a middle 16 KB and the last 8 KB of each of the 91 tracks (`make-seeds.sh`; kept out of the repo because they are UO data).

Two runs of 15 minutes each (`-max_len=65536 -timeout=20 -rss_limit_mb=2048`, at BelowNormal priority through agentnice, side by side):

| Build | Executions | Average exec/s | New units | Final corpus | Coverage features | Crashes, leaks, timeouts, OOMs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SIMD (SSE2) | 105,365 | 116 | 1,313 | 499 | 2,836 | **none** |
| `DR_MP3_NO_SIMD` | 70,891 | 78 | 1,006 | 439 | 2,516 | **none** |

The slowest unit took under 1 s, and peak RSS was 487 MB. The exec rate is low because each input decodes up to 16-64 KB of real audio under ASan, and the runs had a low priority. So this is a smoke-level campaign (176k executions), not an exhaustive one. A longer run is worth doing on an idle machine: `fuzz_cuo_mp3.exe -max_total_time=3600 <corpus> <seeds>`.

**Regression corpus as a unit test** (`Mp3DecoderTests`, 18 tests). The test builds its own synthetic MP3s (silent Layer III frames, optionally led by an Info + LAME frame), so no UO data is committed. It covers:
- validator rejections;
- the LAME trim (delay 576 + 529, padding 1000 - 529, also after `Seek(0)`) and mono;
- 360 deterministic mutations of 6 synthetic seeds, plus the first 48 KB of 12 real tracks when the UO folder exists. The mutations are bit flips, truncation, 0xFF and zero runs, chunk copies, corrupt Xing/LAME fields, random header fields and spliced junk;
- `MusicStream`: loop fills (every buffer full across the seam), a non-looping end, a bad or missing file, and the sample-exact seam on a real track.

**MP3Sharp removed:** the `external/MP3Sharp` submodule, its solution entry, the project reference and the commented-out duplicate `MP3Sharp 1.0.5` NuGet reference.

**CPU per audio-second and first-play latency (bench-000042, ok, 121.6 s).** An offline decode of all 91 tracks (7439 s of audio), MP3Sharp vs dr_mp3, 6 interleaved rounds, then open + first 32 KB buffer × 3 rounds per track (n = 273 each), JIT with `TieredCompilation=0`, pinned to the P-cores. CPU per audio-second, min/median/max over the 6 rounds: **MP3Sharp 2.277 / 2.290 / 2.311 ms, dr_mp3 0.374 / 0.376 / 0.378 ms**. The spread is 1.5 % for MP3Sharp and 1.1 % for dr_mp3, so dr_mp3 uses about 6.1× less CPU (median ratio), far outside the noise. MP3Sharp's figure is higher than the survey's earlier 1.6-1.9 ms; that number came from a different method. MP3Sharp decodes 7444 s of audio and dr_mp3 7439 s; the 5 s gap is the decoders' different handling of frame padding (see the parity section). Open + first 32 KB buffer, ms: **MP3Sharp p50 0.68, p95 1.09, max 80.17; dr_mp3 p50 0.25, p95 1.41, max 6.12**. dr_mp3's open reads the whole file into memory (MP3Sharp streams), so its latency grows with file size. That is why its p95 is above MP3Sharp's; the largest file is elf_city_1.mp3 at 12.9 MB. The client pays this on the music worker thread, not the game thread. MP3Sharp's 80 ms max is a single outlier.

**Listening check (bench-000043, ok, 245.8 s): pass.** The AOT build logs in as kbatman4 and walks a plan that dwells about 50 s per stop: Britain, Minoc, Cove, then Britain again. The check reads the `music … first buffer` / `looped` / `skipped` Trace lines in the client log. The server played Britainpos and Minocpos for those regions, not Britain1 as planned; Britainpos still looped within the dwell. (1) No native DLL beside the AOT exe: pass, `OK: no cuo_mp3.dll next to the AOT cuo.exe`, and the folder listing has no cuo_mp3 file. (2) Plan teleports: pass, all four `[bench] … done` lines (brit, minoc, cove, brit2) and `[bench] plan done`. (3) First track: pass, `music LoginLoop: first buffer after 34.5 ms (open 0.5 ms)` and `music Britainpos: first buffer after 3.3 ms (open 0.3 ms)`. (4) Loop: pass, `music Britainpos: looped (1)` at 07:16:01, 51 s after it started; also `music Cove: looped (1)` and a second `music Britainpos: looped (1)` on the return. (5) Area changes: pass, `music Minocpos: first buffer after 1.0 ms (open 0.3 ms)`, `music Cove: first buffer after 0.7 ms (open 0.2 ms)` and `music Britainpos: first buffer after 1.3 ms (open 0.3 ms)` on the return to Britain. Minocpos did not loop within its dwell; the log has no failure line for it. (6) No failures: pass, there are 0 matches for `skipped`, `DllNotFound`, `EntryPointNotFound` or `exception` (case-insensitive) in the 5737-line client log, and the client exited 0 after 244 s.

**Verification.**
- Client builds, Release and `-p:CuoDevTools=false`: 0 errors.
- NativeAOT publish win-x64: 0 errors, no new trim/AOT warnings.
- `dotnet test tests/ClassicUO.UnitTests -c Release`: 996 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed, 997 total (18 new).
- The write-site budget is unchanged (no ECS writes).

### Codex audit (gpt-6-astra, 2026-10-31) and dispositions

Codex audited `f0d09f8ed..e5421ab27` (the vendored dr_mp3 excluded). It found one P1 and three P2 issues, plus test gaps. All are fixed on poc/dr-mp3; each fix has a unit test except the CI part, which the owner moved to separate work.

- **P1, Linux/macOS builds had no decoder library: fixed (build guard, scripts, runtime).** CI wiring is deferred by the owner to the queued CI work (`cuo-poc-state/handoffs/ci-release-artifacts.md`, section "dr_mp3 native build"); no workflow files were changed.
  - **Build-time error `CUOMP3`.** `ClassicUO.IO.csproj` resolves the platform from the RuntimeIdentifier, or else from the build machine. A build fails when that platform's shared library is missing or not defined (only win-x64, linux-x64 and osx-* are). `ClassicUO.Client.csproj` fails a NativeAOT publish (`PublishAot` with a RID) when the static archive is missing. The message names the file and the script to run. `-p:CuoMp3Optional=true` turns either error into a warning. Checked here: `dotnet build ClassicUO.IO -r linux-x64` fails with CUOMP3, and passes with a warning under `CuoMp3Optional`. The publish guard (`-t:CuoMp3CheckStaticLibrary`) errors for linux-x64, osx-arm64 and linux-arm64, and passes for win-x64. win-x64 builds as before.
  - **One build script per OS** in `src/native/cuo_mp3`, each one command with its prerequisites documented. Each checks its toolchain and names what's missing, writes exactly the files the csproj files look for, and checks the seven exports.
    - `build-linux.sh`: cmake and cc/gcc/clang, writes `external/lib64/libcuo_mp3.so` and `external/lib64-static/libcuo_mp3.a`.
    - `build-macos.sh [universal|arm64|x86_64]`: Apple clang and cmake, universal by default, macOS 11.0 minimum. Writes `external/osx/libcuo_mp3.dylib` and `external/osx-static/libcuo_mp3.a`, and checks each architecture with `lipo -verify_arch`.
    - `build-windows.sh`: the former `build-win-x64.sh`, MSVC from Git Bash through vswhere, plus toolchain checks and a `dumpbin -exports` check.

    `build-unix.sh` is gone. The Windows script ran end to end here. Its outputs differ from the committed binaries only in timestamps and temp object paths, so the committed DLL and lib were kept, and jobs 42 and 43 use identical binaries. **Unverified until CI:** the Linux and macOS scripts passed only `bash -n`. This box has no cmake, gcc or clang, so no CMake configure was possible.
  - **Runtime.** `Mp3Decoder.IsAvailable` probes `cuo_mp3_version` once. On `DllNotFoundException`, `EntryPointNotFoundException` or `BadImageFormatException` it logs one error (`music disabled: the native MP3 decoder (cuo_mp3) could not be loaded: …`). After that, `UOMusic.Play` returns false without starting a stream, and `MusicStream.Pump` fails cleanly. No exception reaches the game loop, and nothing is allocated, so nothing leaks.
- **P2, raw-handle ownership: fixed.** A private `Mp3Handle : SafeHandle` now owns both the dr_mp3 decoder and the input copy, and releases both exactly once, on Dispose or in its critical finaliser. `Read`, `Seek`, `TotalFrames` and `Dispose` take one lock. Each native call holds `DangerousAddRef`/`DangerousRelease` around it, so neither a Dispose from another thread nor finalisation can free memory under dr_mp3. `Dispose` is idempotent and thread-safe, and later calls throw `ObjectDisposedException`. The decoder class has no finaliser any more.
  - Tests: `Dispose_IsIdempotentAndFreesOnce`, and `Dispose_RacingRead_IsSafe`. The race test runs 200 rounds: a reader loops Read/Seek while two threads call Dispose at staggered spin delays. The reader only ever sees frames or `ObjectDisposedException`, and the live input count returns to its baseline.
- **P2, input leak when the native open throws: fixed.** `TryOpenOwned` keeps the native handle and the input copy in a `finally` until the `Mp3Handle` owns them. Every exit before that point (a validator rejection, a null handle, a `GetInfo` failure, any exception) closes the handle and frees the input.
  - A test hook, `Mp3Decoder.OpenMemoryOverride`, can replace `cuo_mp3_open_memory`. A global count, `LiveInputAllocations`, tracks every input copy.
  - Tests: `FailedNativeOpen_FreesTheInputCopy` (forced `DllNotFoundException`, `EntryPointNotFoundException` and a 0 handle, 50 opens each, count back to baseline) and `FailedNativeOpen_FailsTheMusicStreamCleanly`.
- **P2, EOF published before the final buffer: fixed.** `Fill` now returns the end through an out parameter. `Pump` sets the volatile `_ended` only after the last buffer is in the ready queue, so the game thread's stop condition (`IsEnded`, nothing ready, nothing pending in FAudio) can't be true while the tail is still unqueued.
  - Test: `MusicStream_EndIsPublishedAfterTheLastBuffer`, with 10 frames and 3 frames (the whole track in one buffer). A worker hook, `TestAfterFill`, runs between the fill and the enqueue. In it, the "game thread" drains every ready buffer and evaluates the stop condition; it must never hold. All PCM bytes must arrive.
  - Playback effect: none in the normal path. The flag only becomes visible later within the same `Pump` call, and looping tracks never set it. So **bench-000042 and bench-000043 (queued on e5421ab27) were kept**.
- **Tests (audit's test notes): done.**
  - `RealTrack_LoopSeamIsSampleExact` now uses `[FilesFact]`, so without UO data it is reported as skipped instead of passing with no assertions.
  - New committed fixture `tests/ClassicUO.UnitTests/IO/Fixtures/seam-noise.mp3`: 10 KB, our own and redistributable. It is generated by `make_mp3_fixture.py` there, without an encoder or recorded audio: an Info + LAME frame (delay 576, padding 700) and 24 self-contained Layer III frames with fixed-seed noise main data. It is non-silent (peak above 1000) and differs from frame to frame. Its loop seam falls inside a buffer. `Fixture_LoopSeamIsSampleExact` runs the same sample-exact seam check as the real-track test, on every machine.
  - **Synthetic fuzz regressions.** The earlier campaign found no crashes, and its corpus is UO-derived, so none of it is committed. A new 5-minute run used only synthetic seeds: the fixture, the fixture without its Info frame, its first 6 frames and the Info frame alone. It ran on the MSVC ASan + libFuzzer build at 178,447 executions (592/s), added 2,149 new units, and found no crashes, leaks, timeouts or OOMs. `-merge=1` reduced the corpus to 311 files. The smallest 167 of them (at least 64 bytes each, 163 KB in total) are committed in `IO/Fixtures/mp3-regressions`. `FuzzRegressions_DecodeOrRejectCleanly` opens each one and runs read, seek to 0, seek to the middle, seek past the end, and the frame count.
- **Prefilter (optional): tightened.** `Mp3Validator` now needs 3 back-to-back frame headers (`ChainLength`) with the same MPEG version and sample rate, all Layer III. A chain that ends exactly at the end of the data is still accepted, so complete 1-2 frame streams pass. With 3 headers, the second frame must be complete.
  - Replay: `Validator_AcceptsEveryStockTrack` (FilesFact) accepts **all 91** stock tracks.
  - `Validator_NeedsThreeConsistentHeaders` covers: 2 frames then junk (accepted before, rejected now), a third header at 48 kHz, and a third header of MPEG-2.
  - It remains a plausibility check, not a validation of the whole file.
- **Not changed (audit notes, by design):** short reads still conflate EOF and undecodable data, as before. Memory per track is the whole compressed file (at most 32 MiB; stock average 1.21 MB, maximum 12.86 MB) plus at most 192 KiB of PCM buffers. There is still no worker shutdown/join, because it is a background thread.

**Verification (audit fixes).**
- Client builds, Release and `-p:CuoDevTools=false`: 0 errors.
- NativeAOT publish win-x64: 0 errors, no IL or CUOMP3 warnings. `cuo_mp3` appears in `cuo.ilc.rsp` and `link.rsp`, and there is no `cuo_mp3.dll` in the output. (The ILC link step needs vswhere on PATH: `C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Visual Studio\Installer`.)
- `dotnet test tests/ClassicUO.UnitTests -c Release`: 1,008 passed, 1 skipped (as before), 0 failed, 1,009 total, of which 12 are new. The 30 Mp3DecoderTests ran with UO data present.

### Codex round 2 (gpt-6-astra, audit of 591b27218) and dispositions

Codex found no new playback, deadlock or EOF-race issue, and three smaller ones. All three are fixed; the two in managed code have tests. Playback paths are unchanged, so no client run was needed.
- **P2, a library without `cuo_mp3_close` could leak, or throw from the finaliser: fixed.** Every `TryOpen` path (span, seekable stream, non-seekable stream) now resolves the release entry point before it allocates anything, by calling `cuo_mp3_close(NULL)` (a no-op in `cuo_mp3.c`). On `DllNotFoundException`, `EntryPointNotFoundException` or `BadImageFormatException` the open returns false with "no usable release entry point", logged once. `IsAvailable` binds close as well as version. `ReleaseHandle` never throws now: a failing close is counted in `CloseFailures`, and the input is freed in its own `finally`. The pre-ownership cleanup in `TryOpenOwned` also frees the input in its own `finally`. New test hook: `CloseOverride`. Tests:
  - `MissingCloseExport_FailsTheOpenBeforeAllocating`: three exception kinds, all three open paths, no input allocated, the native open never reached.
  - `FailingCloseAtRelease_NeverThrowsAndFreesTheInput`: covers both Dispose and the finaliser. The finaliser half passes only if no exception escapes, because one that did would end the test host.
- **P3, a cached `TotalFrames` was readable after Dispose: fixed.** Disposal is now checked before the cache. Test: `TotalFrames_Cached_ThrowsAfterDispose`.
- **P3, `build-linux.sh` could install a non-x86-64 build as linux-x64: fixed.** On a host other than x86_64 the script refuses to run unless `CUO_MP3_CROSS=1` is set together with `CC` or `CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE`. Before anything is installed, `readelf -h` must report ELF64 / X86-64 for the `.so` and for every member of the `.a`, and the export check now runs on the build output. The script also checks for readelf and nm. **Unverified:** it passed `bash -n` only, plus a check of the header parsing against sample `readelf` text, because this box has no Linux toolchain. Its first real run will be in CI.
- **Test note: done.** `FailedNativeOpen_FreesTheInputCopy` now also covers `BadImageFormatException`.

## Memory per client, round 2: art starts at 24, palette staging bounded (2026-10-31)

Branch `poc/mem-reduce-2` from poc/modern-client 5ed1619dd. Owner follow-ups to "Memory per client: palettes, facet switch, grow on demand" (bench-000035).

**1. The art page array starts at its ceiling, 24 layers (cfbd6e529).** bench-000035 showed every login growing art 12 → 24 at frame 15 (13 pages resident after login), so the smaller start saved nothing. The start sizes and ceilings are now `GrowthPolicy` constants (`ArtLayersStart = ArtLayersMax = 24`; anim 32 → 128 and instances 256k → 2M still grow on demand); `GrowthPolicyTests.Steps_from_the_start_sizes_to_the_ceilings` checks 0 / 2 / 3 steps and the ceilings.

**2. Palette upload staged through 4 MiB (3a084a68b).** What the SDL_GPU source says (external/SDL 27ac7d26b, `SDL_gpu_vulkan.c`; the client runs FNA3D's device on Vulkan):
- `VULKAN_CreateTransferBuffer` creates every transfer buffer as a **dedicated** allocation of exactly its size, in a host-visible, host-coherent type that prefers **HOST_CACHED**: on this machine that is ordinary private read-write (0x4) memory in our process, not the write-combined (0x404) upload heap. So the old one-shot upload made an 18.5 MiB read-write allocation: exactly the size of the region in bench-000035's walk (reserve 18.5 MiB).
- Release is deferred: `SDL_ReleaseGPUTransferBuffer` marks it; it is destroyed in the cleanup of a later swapchain-presenting submit once its command buffer's fence has signalled, and the emptied `VkDeviceMemory` is freed (`vkFreeMemory`) at the cleanup after that. In steady state that is two presented frames, so SDL does not keep it forever by design.
- But the walk only shows the 18.5 MiB region in `new` (16.7 MiB committed and resident at 120 s), not in `new_grow0`, which has the same +25 MiB. So it is not a deterministic leak; why it outlived the upload in one run is not settled offline (the job below walks it at 5–120 s).
- Change: `Renderer.CreatePaletteBuffer` uploads in `PaletteChunks` of at most `PaletteChunkBytes` (4 MiB) through one transfer buffer, waiting for each chunk's fence (5 chunks for the shipped 18.5 MiB), then releases the idle buffer. The staging allocation is 4 MiB instead of 18.5 whatever SDL's release timing. Validation and the failure paths are unchanged (the `finally` also waits for and releases a pending fence). `PaletteFileTests.Palette_upload_chunks_tile_the_payload_within_the_staging_size` (5 cases).
- **The rest of the 25 MiB is not attributed yet.** By reservation size, the extra resident memory in both new arms of bench-000035 is in 4–64 MiB reservations (ws 397 → 421 MiB), not the GC heap. Other host-cached transfer buffers are candidates: the page staging slots (`PageResidency._staging`, mapped with cycle=true, so SDL adds an internal buffer to the container whenever the active one is still in flight, and containers never shrink) and the frame transfer buffer (8 MiB, cycled each frame). With the world kept across the facet switch (change 2 of mem-reduce), those containers live for the session instead of being rebuilt at login. The walk's 16.0 MiB fully committed read-write allocations (3 in new, 1 in new_grow0; base's list was cut off) fit that.
- **Diagnostics:** `CUO_MEM_REGIONS=<s>,<s>,...` (dev builds, `MemLog.cs`) logs every private allocation with 1 MiB or more committed, with its protections, at those times. The job's run.py copy lists every such allocation too (not the top 40).

**Memory trade-off log (per client), computed before bench-000044 (measured results below):**

| item | before | after | saving | what it costs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| art page array (GPU commit, never resident) | 128 MiB, grown to 256 MiB at frame 15 | 256 MiB from the start | 0 steady (it always grew); the 384 MiB login transient (both arrays for one frame) becomes 256 MiB, and one 1.19 ms growth step goes | none: the same 256 MiB the session always reached |
| palette upload staging (private read-write, host-cached) | 18.5 MiB, freed after SDL's deferred release (seen still resident at 120 s in one run) | 4 MiB, released idle after the last chunk | 14.5 MiB transient; 16.7 MiB resident where it lingered | 5 fence waits at renderer creation (startup, once per session) instead of none; the upload's GPU time is unchanged |

**Measurement:** job bench-000044 (`mem-reduce-2-ab`, queued): base 5ed1619dd vs new 3a084a68b, interleaved base/new/base/new, JIT Release dev builds, through benchpin; plan login, Britain b1–b3, `[TestScene go` (large scene, zoom 1 and 2.5), `[TestScene return`, Britain (`q`); 3 windows of 5 s per spot; private WS and commit at 1 Hz, GC heap from `[mem]`, external walks at 60 and 120 s listing every private allocation of 1 MiB+, in-process walks at 5/15/30/60/120 s in new. Results below.

- Unit tests 1028 pass (1 skipped); both client builds (dev and `-p:CuoDevTools=false`) 0 errors.

### Measured: bench-000044

Status ok (1684.6 s). All four runs (base1 new1 base2 new2) completed the plan; every large-scene window had 1,985 mobiles and 25,161 items. Each run stood 420 s; the plan ended at about 160 s. Windows use the 1 Hz samples and the `[mem]` lines: login = the 3 s before b1 starts (12–15 s), Britain = the b3 window (63–78 s), large scene = ls_z1 (91–106 s) and ls_zo (115–130 s), after the round trip = q (143–158 s), idle = the last 60 s, login transient = the maximum over 2–10 s. Values are medians in MiB, each arm as run 1 / run 2. Spread = (max-min)/min within an arm; a difference counts only if it is more than twice the larger within-arm spread.

- **Art at 24 layers:** the login growth step is gone (base grew 12 → 24 at frames 14 and 17, 1.06 and 0.97 ms; new 0 art steps). The login commit transient drops by 128 MiB, the computed 384 → 256 MiB. It lasted about 3 s in base (samples at 3–5 s), not one frame: the old 128 MiB array's release is deferred. Steady windows are unchanged, as computed. The facet-switch peak (82 s in every run) is unchanged.
- **Palette staging: the 18.5 MiB region is gone.** The external walks list an 18.5 MiB read-write allocation in both base runs at 60 s (15.7 MiB resident in each) and at 120 s (17.7 and 15.7 MiB): this time it lingered in every base run. Neither new run has it, at any of the in-process walks (5/15/30/60/120 s) or the external ones, and no 4 MiB palette buffer remains either (the only 4 MiB read-write allocation is in all four runs and has 0 resident).
- **Why the resident total didn't drop by those 17 MiB:** the art page staging containers. Their buffers are 10.67 MiB each (2048², B5G5R5A1, 6 mips: the art chain), private read-write and fully resident. Base held 7 and 6 of them, new 8 and 8, so new carried 1.5 more on average (+16 MiB), cancelling the palette saving. All read-write-only allocations with 4–64 MiB reservations at 120 s sum to 267.5 / 252.8 MiB committed (base) vs 276.1 / 275.1 MiB (new).

**What the walk says about the 25 MiB from bench-000035 (diagnosis only; nothing changed):**
- The art residency has 4 staging slots (`Math.Max(2, PageBudget * 2)`, PageBudget 2), but every run holds 6–8 art staging buffers: 64–85 MiB resident, where 4 slots need 42.7. `StartLoads` maps a slot with `cycle=true` as soon as its upload is recorded. If the copy is still in flight, SDL adds a new buffer to that slot's container, and a container never shrinks.
- Timing: in both new runs all 8 buffers exist at the first in-process walk (5 s; 9 art pages had been uploaded by about 6 s), and the set of 4–64 MiB read-write allocations is identical at 5, 15, 30, 60 and 120 s, apart from heap-like 32 MiB regions whose commit moves. Base has the same counts at 60 and 120 s. So the extra buffers come from the login page burst. Nothing is added at the facet switch (about 80 s) or in the large scene.
- So the walk supports the cycled staging containers as the mechanism. It does not support the facet-switch part of the earlier explanation: keeping the world across the switch does not grow them. The count varies by run within the same binary (6, 7, 8, 8 here), in steps of 10.7 MiB. Two extra buffers (21.3 MiB) fit most of bench-000035's +25 MiB. That job had one run per arm, so the 25 MiB is probably this variation, not a cost of mem-reduce. This job has no pre-mem-reduce arm to confirm it.
- Other read-write regions, for reference: 2–3 fully resident 8 MiB regions in every run (the frame transfer buffer, cycled across frames in flight); three 16.0 MiB fully resident ones in every run (the size of SDL's `SMALL_ALLOCATION_SIZE` blocks for host-visible non-dedicated buffers, not staging); the anim staging buffers (1 MiB chain, 8 slots) are below the walk's size floor.
- **Proposed fix (needs owner approval before it is built or measured):** keep a slot's staging buffer and never cycle it. Record the frame of each slot's last copy. `StartLoads` reuses a slot only once that frame has retired (SDL keeps at most 3 frames in flight; or keep the copy's fence), then maps it with `cycle=false`. Art then holds exactly 4 × 10.67 = 42.7 MiB. Expected saving: 2–4 buffers, 21–43 MiB resident per client (43 MiB in both new runs here), and the run-to-run 10.7 MiB steps go away, which also makes A/B memory jobs less noisy. Cost: during the login burst a slot may wait up to 3 frames before its next page load starts (a few ms at login); no change once the 9–10 pages are resident. An alternative is to drop to fewer art slots after the login burst, but that keeps the cycling. Anim staging would get the same change for consistency, at 1 MiB per buffer.

| item | before | after (measured) | saving | what it costs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| art page array starts at 24 | 384 MiB commit for ~3 s at login, then 256 | 256 MiB from the start | **128 MiB** of login commit transient (bench-000044); 0 steady, as computed; one ~1 ms growth step gone | none |
| palette upload staging 4 MiB | 18.5 MiB RW, still resident at 120 s in both base runs (15.7–17.7 MiB) | gone by 5 s | 15.7–17.7 MiB resident where it lingers. Not visible in the window medians here, because the art staging count varied by +1.5 buffers (+16 MiB) the other way | 5 fence waits at renderer creation |

### Codex audit (coordinator scratchpad `astra-memreduce2/out.md`) and dispositions (2026-10-31)

Codex found one P2 and two P3s; all three are fixed. Chunk boundaries, empty input, upload ordering, the untrusted-palette checks, the 24 art layers, the enabled diagnostics and multi-instance safety were checked and found fine.
- **P2, fence wait result ignored (fixed).** `SDL_WaitForGPUFences`' result was discarded, so a failed wait (e.g. device lost) let the palette upload remap and overwrite its transfer buffer while a copy might still read it, and return a partially filled buffer. Now `TryWaitFence` returns the result, and `WaitAndReleaseFence` releases the fence either way and throws `GpuFenceException` on failure. The palette chunk loop moved into `Renderer.UploadChunked` (stage, submit, wait, release per chunk), which throws before staging the next chunk; the `finally` no longer waits (no fence is outstanding there) and only releases, which cannot throw. Every other wait was fixed the same way: the throttled offscreen path (a zero fence from submit now counts as a submit failure; the new fence takes its slot before the old one is waited on), `MeasureSubmitOverheadMs`, `DrainInFlight` (releases every fence, checks `SDL_WaitForGPUIdle`, then throws), and `SubmitAndSave` (throws before mapping the download, so never a half-written screenshot; the transfer buffer is released in `finally`). `Dispose` catches a failed drain, logs it and still releases everything. Tests: `PaletteFileTests` drives `UploadChunked` with fakes (no GPU): a failed wait at chunk 0, 2 or 4 throws, releases that fence, and stages nothing more; a successful upload is stage, submit, wait, release five times.
- **P3, protections deduplicated by substring (fixed).** `[memregions]` collected protections with `string.Contains`, so `0x404` hid a later `0x4`. They are now a `HashSet<uint>` per allocation, formatted ascending (`0x4|0x404`).
- **P3, unset diagnostics allocated a closure (fixed).** `MemLog.Start` and `StartRegions` captured locals in lambdas, so their display classes were allocated on entry, before the environment checks. The threads now start in `StartLog(seconds)` and `StartRegions(value)`, called only after the checks; unset, `Start` allocates nothing.
- Not part of this round: the art staging slot fix (cycle=false after the slot's fence), which waits for owner approval.
- Verified: client Release build and `-p:CuoDevTools=false` build, 0 errors; unit tests 1032 pass, 1 skipped (was 1028: +4 `UploadChunked` cases). No client runs.

## Tile data single source: one tiledata.bin, draw rules as data (2026-10-31)

Branch `poc/tiledata-single`, from poc/modern-client f27759989. Owner decisions: one source of truth per pack file, and ClassicUO's hard-coded per-tile rules become data. The coordinator publishes classic-1.1 when it merges.

**Format.** `tiledata.bin` (new magic `TILE`) is the pack's only tile data file: the full entries of the old `tiledata_ext.bin` (flags, names, texId, count, animId, hue, light, weight, layer, height) plus `packFlags` (land entry 16 → 20 B, static 28 → 32 B). The compact renderer copy (`TLTD`, 12 B per entry) and `tiledata_ext.bin` (`TLDX`) are retired: 2.50 MB instead of 0.98 + 2.18 MB.
- I kept the name `tiledata.bin`: it is the natural name, and an old client fails loudly on a new pack (`tiledata_ext.bin` is missing, and its `tiledata.bin` reader meets the wrong magic).
- `TileDataFile.Read` validates the magic, version, Kind 0, land count = 0x4000, static count 1..0x10000, the exact file size (before allocating) and every name reference. A 1.0 layout gets a "convert again (--only tiledata)" message.
- The renderer's 12-byte `LandTileData`/`StaticTileData` arrays are built at load (`TileDataFile.Compact`, in `PackSet`, which the client's `GpuWorldRenderer` uses). **Read and validate: 0.93 ms median. Building the compact arrays: 0.25 ms median** (2.50 MB file, 100 runs in `TileDrawOracleTests.Compact_Arrays_Load_Time`, JIT, noisy machine; minimums 0.54 and 0.13 ms).
- Memory: unchanged. The compact arrays are the same 0.98 MB as before, and the full arrays are transient.

**Rules moved into data.** The converter's `Uo.Converter/TileRules.cs` is the only code that knows them; readers use `Uo.Pack.TileDraw`.

| Rule | Lived in | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Land 0, 1, 2 not drawn | `Land.Create` and `Land.UpdateGraphicBySeason` (`graphic > 2`), `Map.RequestBlockArt` (`graphic <= 2`), poc `ChunkBaker` (`tile <= 2`) | land `NoDraw`; `Land.IsDrawn` |
| Statics 0x1, 0x21BC, 0xA1FE–0xA201; 0x9E4C/64/65/7D with Background or Surface; 0x63D3; 0x2198–0x21A4 | `GameObject.CanBeDrawn`, poc `ChunkBaker.CanBeDrawn` | static `NoDraw` |
| Easel 0x0F65 drawn before 6.0.14.4 | `GameObject.CanBeDrawn` (client version) | evaluated with the source client's version |
| Name starts with `nodraw` | `GameObject.CanBeDrawn`, `ChunkBaker` (via `NameNoDraw`) | static `NoDraw` (`NameNoDraw` stays, informational only) |
| `NoDiagonal` hides; animated ones are shown to gargoyles | `GameObject.CanBeDrawn`, `ChunkBaker` | `NoDraw` / `NoDrawUnlessGargoyle`; the race check stays runtime |
| A multi item is drawn only when its display graphic > 2 | `Item.RefreshGraphicState` (`MultiGraphic > 2`) | new bit 3 `NoDrawAsMulti`; `Item.IsMultiItemDrawn` |

- `GameObject.CanBeDrawn(world, g)` covers statics, items, multi components, effects, the minimap, the world map and overhead names. It is now `TileDraw.Static(StaticData[g].PackFlags, player is gargoyle)`.
- The season swap stays runtime, and the flag is read on the swapped graphic.
- The poc renderer bakes as for a non-gargoyle player, as before.
- One change in the standalone poc renderer only: it used to bake 0x63D3 when the tile lacked `NoDiagonal` (its copy of the rules skipped the id rules for 0x63D3, unlike the client). It now hides 0x63D3 as the client did. The client already hid it with an override, so the client's picture does not change.

**Pixel-neutral oracle.** The old client code is kept verbatim, only as an oracle, in two places:
- the client test `TileDrawOracleTests`, through the client's own loader (`TileDataLoader.Read`) and draw functions, on the pack alone;
- the converter's `Verify.CheckNoDraw`, on the source client's tiledata.

On the 7.0.103 test pack, both report **212,992 decisions, 0 mismatches**: 16,384 land ids, 65,536 static ids × 2 player races, and 65,536 multi display graphics. Hidden: 3 land ids, 32 statics (31 for a gargoyle) and 3 multi items; 20 statics are named `nodraw`.

Two portable tests go with it. One edits flags to show that no rule is left in code (0x0001 is drawn without its flag and hidden with it). The other tests the reader's validation: bad counts, sizes and name references, and the two pack 1.0 magics.

**Version 0 / 1.0 packs.** There is no fallback. `ChunkBaker`'s own id rules (its version-0 fallback) are gone, and a pack without a `TILE` `tiledata.bin` fails at tiledata load with the "convert again" message. `PackAssets.Open` already required `tiledata_ext.bin`, so version-0 packs never loaded; it now requires `tiledata.bin`. Nothing still loads v0. `FileHeader.version` and the manifest version stay 1, because the magic identifies the layout.

**`art/sprites.bin` partial-hue bit.** Bit 2 copied tiledata's `PartialHue`.
- It is no longer written (`SpriteFlags.RetiredPartialHue`).
- Nothing at runtime read it. The converter's verify and debug PNGs did, and they now take the flag from tiledata.
- Packs before 1.1 still set it. Verify reports them (12,732 entries in the test pack, whose `sprites.bin` is hard-linked from classic-1.0) and fails on any other unknown bit.
- A full conversion drops it.

**Test pack.** A `cp -al` copy of classic-1.0, then `Uo.Converter --only tiledata --out <scratch>/tiledata-single/pack`. The converter deleted the stale `tiledata_ext.bin` from the copy, and the published files keep their bytes. `--verify-only` on everything: all checks passed.

**Client parity: pixel-neutral** (bench-000045 and bench-000046; bench-000041 was cancelled before it started). f27759989 runs on CURRENT (classic-1.0), 41b109e7f on the test pack. Binaries: NativeAOT, in the scratch folder with build-info.txt. Neither job logged an exception.

- **bench-000045** (one run per arm, Gpu and Legacy; Britain 1495 1629, house 1427 1691, then `[TestScene go` and the large scene at zoom 1 and 2.5). Each spot had the same position in both arms: Britain 1495,1629,Z 10 (2 mobiles, 70 items), house 1427,1691,Z 0 (4 mobiles, 59 items), large scene 5156,2150,Z 0 (1,985 mobiles, 25,161 items). Pixel diffs, new vs base, on the world layer:

  | Spot | Gpu | Legacy |
  |---|---|---|
  | Britain | 0.000 % | 0.002 % |
  | house | **30.180 %** | 0.331 % |
  | large scene, zoom 1 | 7.197 % | 5.893 % |
  | large scene, zoom 2.5 | 1.980 % | 1.719 % |

  The large-scene differences are its moving mobiles, and they are about the same size on both renderers. The `_lights` layer differed by 90–98 % at Britain and the house on both renderers, because the day/night light level changed between sessions. That layer is 0 % within bench-000046.

  The one real difference was the house on Gpu. Base drew the house roof, the chimneys of the bottom-left building and a tree; new hid them, as both Legacy runs did. The house-window counters were steady for the whole window: base had foliage 1, cap_statics 2, pick_tests 36 and override_calls 28; new had 0, 0, 24 and 14.
- **bench-000046** (coordinator re-run of the house only: Gpu, base, new, base, new, base, new; same binaries and packs; a `house` shot 8 s after arrival and a `house_late` shot about 6 s later). **All three base runs hide the roof, chimneys and tree in both shots, as all three new runs do.** All six runs stood at 1427,1691,Z 0 with 4 mobiles and 59 items. The house-window counters (mean) are the same in every run: foliage 0, cap_statics 0, pick_tests 24, hidden_tiles 80, objects 218, override_calls 14, gpu_overrides 21, gpu_instances 3,069–3,070. These are new's bench-000045 values. Pairwise diffs of the world layer (min–max over the pairs):

  | Pairs | house | house_late |
  |---|---|---|
  | base vs base (3) | 0.446–0.492 % | 0.467–0.517 % |
  | new vs new (3) | 0.335–0.520 % | 0.427–0.472 % |
  | new vs base (9) | 0.210–0.490 % | 0.240–0.507 % |

  New vs base is no larger than base vs base. What remains is moving NPCs inside the house; the roof alone was 30 %.
- **Verdict (A): a pre-existing race on the base side, not a branch change.** The same base binary on the same pack drew the roof once (bench-000045) and hid it in 6 of 6 later shots. Its counters moved with it (foliage 1 → 0, cap_statics 2 → 0). Gpu with the roof hidden matches Legacy. The race is probably in the roof-hiding decision for a player standing under a roof, made when the Gpu host arrives at a spot. It was not investigated; it can be reproduced with the same binary, and it does not involve this branch. Every other shot was pixel-neutral apart from motion and the light level.

**Load time of the compact arrays** (from the client log, `tiledata` in the `[load]` line, bench-000046): base 2.1–2.7 ms with 6,399 KB allocated; new 2.3–2.6 ms with 6,719 KB (+320 KB for the per-tile draw flags and the compact copies). The difference is within run-to-run noise.

**Open for the coordinator:** run.py printed "WARNING: password appears in the log" for every run of bench-000045 and bench-000046, on base and on new. The check is a plain substring test of `$CUO_TEST_PASSWORD` against the client log, and the client logs no password argument (`-autologin` and the encrypted settings.json only). It may be a false positive from a short password, but it was not confirmed. Please check the run logs in the two job folders.

- Client builds, Release and `-p:CuoDevTools=false`: 0 errors. Uo.Converter, Uo.Render.App and Uo.Client: 0 errors.
- `dotnet test tests/ClassicUO.UnitTests -c Release` with `CUO_TEST_PACK` set to the test pack: 982 passed, 1 skipped (the symlink test), 0 failed (4 new).

### Codex audit (coordinator scratchpad `astra-tiledata/out.md`) and fixes (2026-10-31)

Codex (gpt-6-astra) audited 41b109e7f: one introduced finding and five inherited ones (also in f27759989). All six are fixed or decided, each with a test in `TileDataAuditTests` unless noted.

1. **P1, untrusted names could exhaust memory.** A valid-sized 2,490,395-byte file could point all 81,920 entries at one 65,535-byte name, which decoded to about 10 GiB of strings. Fixed: a name reference may be at most 64 bytes (`TileDataFile.MaxNameBytes`; source names are 20 bytes) and the name table at most 5 MiB (`MaxNameTableBytes`). The references are checked before the name table is allocated. `TileDataFile.DecodeNames` decodes each distinct (offset, length) once, so shared references share the string. The converter refuses longer names. Test: the audit's file is rejected with under 4 MB allocated (the entry arrays), plus the 64/65-byte boundary, the table cap, and string sharing. No format change, so the test pack was not re-converted (its longest name is 20 bytes).
2. **P2, the easel's visibility follows the source version, not the runtime one (introduced).** Coordinator decision, under the owner's rule that the pack's data decides: this is intended, and no runtime version rule comes back. It is documented as a deliberate behaviour change in pack-format.md ("NoDraw flags", "The easel") and data-formats.md 5.6, with how an admin changes it (edit the 0x0F65 flag in the source tiledata and rebuild). Test: the easel follows only its flag, `CanBeDrawn` takes no version, and no client or renderer source mentions 0x0F65.
3. **P2, gargoyle-only animated statics lost their zero-offset frame on the Gpu path.** ChunkBaker leaves out statics hidden from a non-gargoyle player (e.g. 0x5683, offsets 0,1,2,3). The Gpu host replaced an animated static only when its `AnimOffset` was not 0, so a gargoyle saw nothing on the offset-0 frames. Legacy keeps animated statics out of its chunk mesh and draws them with `StaticView` on every frame. Fixed: a static the client draws but the bake omitted (`GameScene.BakeOmits`, the bake's own predicate) goes to `GpuReplaceStatic` in `CollectGpuStatic` and in the meshed branch, and counts as a walk reason (4, now "season or unbaked graphic"), so the skip mask never hides it. It is drawn through the same `StaticView` as Legacy, so its pixels are Legacy's. Only gargoyle players see a difference (for anyone else these statics are not `AllowedToDraw`). Tests: `BakeOmits` equals ChunkBaker's predicate for all 16 flag combinations, 0x5683 is omitted but drawn for a gargoyle, and on the pack 0x5683 is `NoDrawUnlessGargoyle`. Not checked in the client: the parity jobs' character is not a gargoyle, so this fix does not change their pictures (see "Client parity" above).
4. **P2, multi components kept stale visibility across season changes.** `Multi.UpdateGraphicBySeason` now recomputes `AllowedToDraw` for the swapped graphic, like `Static`'s. `Create` relies on it. Test: a component (0x0CA7, swapped in spring) whose spring graphic is `NoDraw` is hidden in spring and shown again in summer. To make that testable, `GameObject.CanBeDrawn(world, g)` reads a `[ThreadStatic]` `TestStaticData` when no client runs.
5. **P2, the poc client's ground items ignored draw flags.** `RenderExtract` now applies `Uo.Render.GroundItemDraw.Drawn`: `TileDraw.Static` with the player's race (gargoyle bodies 0x029A/0x029B and their ghosts 0x02B6/0x02B7) and the corpse exception (0x2006 is always drawn, as ClassicUO's `Item.AllowedToDraw = IsCorpse || CanBeDrawn`). The helper lives in Uo.Render so the unit tests can reach it. Test: flags, race, corpse, out of range, and that `RenderExtract` calls it.
6. **P2, verify approved a pack missing `tiledata.bin`.** Fixed: when tiledata is selected, a missing `tiledata.bin` fails ("missing tiledata.bin (the pack's only tile data)"), checked before the early return. Checked by hand, not a unit test (the unit tests do not reference the converter): a hard-linked copy of the test pack's root tables without `tiledata.bin` (manifest rewritten to list only those) ends `VERIFY FAILED` with exit 2 under `--verify-only --only tiledata`, and passes under `--only hues`.

**Verification.** Client builds (Release, and `-p:CuoDevTools=false`): 0 errors. Uo.Converter, Uo.Render.App, Uo.Client: 0 errors. `dotnet test tests/ClassicUO.UnitTests -c Release` with `CUO_TEST_PACK` = the test pack: 989 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed (7 new). `--verify-only` (everything) on the test pack: all checks passed, oracle 212,992 decisions, 0 mismatches.


## Legacy (pre-UOP) import: UOML 4.0.11c end to end (2026-10-31, `poc/legacy-import`)

Owner requirement: the converter imports pre-UOP installs with pre-7.0.9 data as well as UOP ones. Base `poc/tiledata-single` 1f7b49ae6. Test install `D:/Ultima Online Installations/UOML` (read-only): client.exe of July 2005, MUL only, no verdata.mul, no map1.mul.

**Client version.** The UOML exe has no VS_VERSION_INFO and no version text: it builds "4.0.11c" at run time with `sprintf("%d.%d.%d%s", 4, 0, 11, "c")` (format at file offset 0x1dfc88, code at 0x125979). The converter now resolves the version as ModernUO does: `--client-version`, else `--cuo-settings <settings.json>` (`clientversion`), else client.exe VS_VERSION_INFO, else the push sequence of that sprintf call (`LegacyClientVersion.cs`, a port of ModernUO PR #2735 at 61d0651af, kept identical). Nothing found: the error names both options. Below 4.0.11c: refused as unsupported (owner). Results: UOML 4.0.11c from the format call; `C:/Ultima Online Classic` 7.0.103.0 from VS_VERSION_INFO, as before. **ClassicUO's parser reads "4.0.11c" as 4.0.11.2** (0x04000B02: letters count from `a` = 0; ModernUO says .3), and its `CV_4011C`/`CV_4011D` enum values carry the letter's ASCII code, so no parsed 4.0.11x compares as the enum intends. The converter's thresholds (CV_6000, CV_7090) are unaffected. A tiledata.mul whose size does not fit the layout the version selects is refused (`ClientLoad.CheckTileDataLayout`), so a wrong version cannot silently misparse every record.

**UOML, stage by stage** (full conversion 28 s, then `--verify-only`: all checks passed):

| Stage | Result |
|---|---|
| art / tex | 15,319 art (10 pages), 1,870 tex; BIT-EXACT |
| anims | 2,048 bodies, 477 with frames, 0 UOP bodies, 374,998 frames, 691 pages; sample BIT-EXACT (absent/cross-page frames as usual) |
| tiledata | old layout: 16,384 land, 16,384 statics; every field and name EXACT |
| hues / radarcol | 3,000 hues EXACT |
| multis | multi.mul, 12-byte components: 233 multis, 49,380 components (flags only 0 and 1; 1,092 invisible) EXACT; independent check: every entry length is a multiple of 12, all offsets within ±64 |
| lights, equipconv | 55 lights, 198 rows EXACT; tileart: no tileart.uop, `tileart.bin` written empty |
| gumps, fonts | 2,630 gumps, 10 ASCII + 3 unicode fonts EXACT |
| cliloc, speech | 8 languages (377,912 strings), 5,548 speech entries EXACT |
| maps | **three fixes, below** |

**Map fixes.**
1. **Felucca was cut at 6144.** ClassicUO picks 6144 for any client below `CV_4011D`, which every parsed 4.0.11x is, but the UOML map0.mul holds 7168×4096 (the Mondain's Legacy columns), and ModernUO serves a 7168-wide Felucca. The width now comes from the map0 size (7168 or 6144).
2. **No Trammel, and no diffs.** Below 6.0 ModernUO reads Trammel from map0 (`maps.enablePre6000Trammel`), applies mapdif (below 6.0) and stadif (below 7.0.9) for every facet, and announces the counts in 0xBF/0x18. The converter now does the same through ClassicUO's own `ApplyPatches` (`ClientLoad.ApplyLegacyMapRules`), so the pack holds the world the server walks on; the client already ignores 0xBF/0x18. UOML: facet 0 1,405 land / 1,807 static diff blocks, facet 1 8,034 / 10,931, facet 2 268 / 268. This changes the data-formats rule "no patch formats" for map diffs of legacy clients only; verdata.mul is still not applied (ClassicUO opens it and applies nothing) and the converter warns when one is present.
3. **Statics stored at offset 0 were dropped** (`MapConvert`: `StaticAddress != 0`). Address 0 is the first block of every statics*.mul and stadif*.mul. Now `StaticCount > 0` decides. This also changes the classic pack: one region per facet (6 region files: 0/r_0_2, 1/r_0_2, 2/r_0_1, 3/r_0_0, 4/r_0_1, 5/r_0_0) gains the statics of that block (UOML: +2 statics each on facets 3 and 4).

Verify now compares every block of a MUL facet with an independent reader of the MUL files and diffs (`MulMapOracle`, no shared code with MapLoader): UOML 5 facets (0 and 1: 7168×4096, 2, 3, 4), 1,089,785 blocks, all EXACT.

**Pack format: unchanged.** Files a legacy install lacks: tileart (empty `tileart.bin`), UOP anims (none), map5 (facet absent; the client reports a missing map). The client copes with 0x4000 statics in `tiledata.bin` at load.

**Can the client load it?** Offline only: `LegacyPackLoadTests` (ClassicUO.UnitTests, gated on `CUO_LEGACY_PACK` and `CUO_LEGACY_UO`) loads the UOML pack through `UOFileManager.Load("ENU")` and checks 0x4000 land/statics, multis, facets 0-4 present (5 absent), 7168-wide facets 0/1, and Trammel's last mapdif1 block against mapdif1.mul. No client job was submitted: a ModernUO login would need a server configured with the UOML data and a 4.0.11c client version, which the bench server is not.

**Tests.** New project `tests/Uo.Converter.Tests` (11 tests; separate because the converter's frozen MUL loaders share namespaces with the client's pack loaders, and not in ClassicUO.sln, like Uo.Converter): synthetic PE for the version format call (UOML layout, no suffix, ambiguous/missing/two-letter/upper-case/imm32 refused), the resolution order, old and new tiledata layouts through `tiledata.bin`, layout mismatch refused, 12- and 16-byte multis with visibility, map diffs baked below 6.0 and not from 7.0.9, statics at address 0 (fails with the old test), Trammel from map0 below 6.0 only.

**Verification.** Client builds (Release, and `-p:CuoDevTools=false`): 0 errors. `dotnet test tests/ClassicUO.UnitTests -c Release` (with the UOML pack): 987 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed (1 new). `tests/Uo.Converter.Tests`: 11 passed. Classic spot check (`--only tiledata,data,maps` from `C:/Ultima Online Classic` into scratch): all checks passed; multis.bin identical to classic-1.0, tiledata.bin as on the base branch, regions differ only in the 6 files above.

**Open.** (a) ClassicUO's 4.0.11c → 4.0.11.2 parse versus ModernUO's .3: harmless for the converter, but the client would send/compare it; change the client's parser? (b) Felucca width by file size instead of ClassicUO's version rule. (c) **Owner decision needed:** baking map diffs contradicts README "No patch formats" (owner, 2026-10-24: mapdif/stadif never supported, shard owners merge first). It is on by default here because without it a 4.0.11c pack has no real Trammel (it would be Felucca) and differs from what ModernUO serves by default; `--no-map-diffs` restores the old rule. The README line is left unchanged until the owner decides.


### Codex audit and dispositions (2026-10-31, `poc/legacy-import`)

Codex (gpt-6-astra) audited e58afd14b: seven findings (six P2, one P3) plus a server-parity note. All fixed or resolved, each with a test on synthetic inputs (no UO data committed). The converter no longer uses ClassicUO's frozen `MapLoader` for maps at all (`fm.Maps.Load()` is not called; `tools/ClassicUO.Assets.Mul` is unchanged): `FacetSources` picks the files of a facet and `FacetTable` builds its block table (base map, base statics, then the diffs), both in `poc/Uo.Converter/FacetSource.cs`.

1. **P2, offset-0 statics with a negative length.** The loader's unsigned `StaidxBlock.Size` turned (0, 0xFFFFFFFF) into 1,024 records from the start of the file once the converter accepted offset 0. Fixed: staidx and stadifi entries are read signed, as ModernUO does (offset < 0 or length <= 0 is an empty block), and the range must lie inside the statics file before the count is computed and capped at 1,024 (`FacetTable.TryStaticRange`; the oracle has its own copy). Valid offset-0 records stay. Tests: `Static_Index_Entries_Are_Checked_Signed_And_In_Range_Before_The_Count` (9 cases), `Negative_Length_At_Offset_0_Is_An_Empty_Block_In_Staidx_And_Stadifi` (both versions; a 1,100-record statics file, so the old reading would have been in range).
2. **P2, patch families.** The frozen loader opened all five diff files only when mapdifl existed (land-only sets threw on the missing static files, static-only sets were never loaded) and skipped static diffs when stadif was empty. Fixed in converter code (`FacetTable.ApplyDiffs`): the land family (mapdifl + mapdif) and the statics family (stadifl + stadifi + stadif) are applied independently, each when its own files exist; a deletion-only set with an empty stadif is applied. Tests: `Land_Diffs_Alone_Are_Applied`, `Static_Diffs_Alone_Are_Applied`, `Static_Diffs_That_Only_Delete_Are_Applied_With_An_Empty_Stadif`, each also checked block by block against the oracle. The old `land-only` case reproduced the throw (`stadifl4.mul` not found) before `Maps.Load()` was dropped.
3. **P2, `--xfiles` discarded the patches.** Resolved by removal (owner, 2026-10-31): the x files (`map<N>x`, `staidx<N>x`, `statics<N>x`) are not supported at all. `--xfiles` is gone; the converter, the verifier and the oracle read only `map<N>.mul`/`map<N>LegacyMUL.uop`, `staidx<N>.mul` and `statics<N>.mul`, with no fallback. A shard that wants the x files renames them to the regular names before importing. (On OSI they were chosen per account by the character-list flag 0x8000, which ModernUO never sends; on the classic install they share the terrain and differ only in statics: Felucca 1,344 blocks, Trammel 439.) The client's dead `useXFiles` parameter of `MapLoader.LoadMap` is removed with its three callers (World.cs twice, WorldMapGump.cs); the `CLF_UNLOCK_FELUCCA_AREAS` enum value stays (protocol). Test: `X_Files_Are_Never_Read`.
4. **P2, oracle source selection.** Fixed: `MulMapOracle.TryOpen` restates the converter's precedence independently (UOP over MUL on a UOP installation, Trammel from map0 below 6.0) and returns "not applicable" (null) when the selected map is UOP, so a stale `mapN.mul` next to `mapNLegacyMUL.uop` is never compared. The X part is resolved by removing x files (3). Test: `Oracle_Is_Not_Applicable_When_The_Converter_Reads_The_Uop_Map`.
5. **P2, dimensions came from the pack.** Fixed: `SourceFacets.For` works out the expected facets and sizes from the source files alone (map size, or the UOP entries' total; ModernUO's facet heights; staidx size reported when it disagrees), `Verify.CheckMaps` compares them with the manifest and each facet.json (missing facet, extra facet, wrong size), and only then compares blocks with the oracle, sized from the source. `--facets` and `--no-maps` limit what is expected; `--regions` limits only the block comparison. A stock 7.0.103.0 LegacyMUL.uop holds one block more than its facet (458,753 for 7168x4096, staidx 458,752); that one trailing block is ignored for UOP maps. Tests: `Verify_Fails_A_Pack_Narrower_Than_Its_Source_Map` (synthetic 1456-wide facet 4 in a 1448 pack, and the right size passes), `Verify_Fails_A_Pack_Missing_A_Facet_The_Source_Has` (and `--facets` respected), and **`Verify_Fails_A_6144_Wide_Felucca_Built_From_The_7168_Wide_Uoml_Map0`** on the real UOML map0 (`LegacyUoFact`, gated on `CUO_LEGACY_UO`, skipped otherwise): "pack 6144x4096, the source map0.mul holds 7168x4096", then the fixed width passes.
6. **P2, `LegacyPackLoadTests` proved nothing about Trammel.** Missing fixtures returned as a pass, and the checked block (382,507, the last mapdif1 entry) is identical to map0 (checked: yes). Fixed: missing fixtures are reported as skipped (`LegacyPackFact` sets xunit's `Skip`); the test now checks blocks 20,090 (Codex's: differs from map0 in one cell's z only; ids equal, checked with an independent script) and 238,434 (all 64 ids and z differ) against their last mapdifl1 entry, ids and z, and asserts each differs from map0. **CI:** `tests/Uo.Converter.Tests` is not in ClassicUO.sln, so a root `dotnet test` skips it; added to the CI brief (`cuo-poc-state/handoffs/ci-release-artifacts.md`) as an explicit step.
7. **P3, tiledata size check.** Some sizes fit both layouts (1,383,184 B: 804 old or 676 new static groups), so the size cannot confirm the layout. Now such a size is refused with a message naming `--client-version`; with an explicit `--client-version` it is accepted and the converter warns that the layout is unconfirmed. The stock sizes (1,036,288 and 1,644,544 B old, 3,188,736 B new) fit exactly one layout and pass. Test: `Tiledata_Size_That_Fits_Both_Layouts_Needs_An_Explicit_Version`.

**Server parity: Trammel below 6.0 is map0 even when map1 exists.** ModernUO: `TileMatrix` uses `mapFileIndex = Pre6000ClientSupport && mapID == 1 ? 0 : fileIndex` (`maps.enablePre6000Trammel`, default `ServerClientVersion < 6.0.0.0`), so Trammel reads map0/staidx0/statics0, while `TileMatrixPatch` takes the map's fileIndex (1), so its diffs are mapdif1/stadif1. The converter and the oracle now do the same (`FacetSources.FileIndex`); from 6.0 Trammel needs its own map1. Tests: `Trammel_Comes_From_Map0_Below_6000_Even_When_There_Is_A_Map1`, `Trammel_Below_6000_Is_Map0_With_The_Facet_1_Diffs`. UOML has no map1, so its pack is unchanged.

**Owner additions in the same pass.**
- **Map patches merged at import, decided** (open question c above): kept as built and on by default; README "No patch formats" reworded (no patch formats in the source tree or the pack; legacy map patch files are merged into the maps at import), recorded in data-formats.md 4.9 and the 10 owner decisions with the version gates (land below 6.0, statics below 7.0.9, ModernUO's `maps.enableMapDiffPatches`/`maps.enableStaticsDiffPatches` defaults). pack-format.md's intro updated.
- **Felucca width from the map0 file size, decided** (open question b): recorded in data-formats.md.
- **ClassicUO's version parser fixed the ModernUO way** (open question a; ModernUO PR #2735 at 61d0651af): letter 'a' = 1, so "4.0.11c" is 4.0.11.3 = `CV_4011C` (UOML is now reported as 0x04000B03); a letter is read only before 5.0.7, decided by a version comparison (`ClientVersionHelper.IsLetterVersion`), and ignored after it as ModernUO does; the lettered constants are `(maj<<24)|(min<<16)|(rev<<8)|(letter-'a'+1)`; `ClientVersionHelper.ToVersionString` round-trips. Comparisons now select the clients their names say: `< CV_4011D` (character creation's race byte; the frozen loader's map width, which the converter no longer uses) is true for 4.0.11c and false for 4.0.11d (before, 4.0.11d also counted as older); `>= CV_500A` now includes 5.0.0a (before, it did not); `== CV_200X`/`CV_308D`/`CV_308J` can now match at all. One constant changed meaning: `CV_306E` was 3.0.0e and is now 3.0.6e, so clients 3.0.1 to 3.0.6d no longer count as at or after it (all below the supported 4.0.11c). A four-number letter-era text such as "4.0.11.3" still parses (ModernUO would read patch 0) and formats as "4.0.11c". Tests: `ClientVersionTests` (round trips of 4.0.11c, 4.0.11, 5.0.0a, 5.0.6e, 5.0.7.0, 7.0.103.0; every lettered constant equals its parsed text; comparisons; the 5.0.7 boundary).

**StaticData bounds (optional item: listed, not fixed).** The client indexes `TileData.StaticData` (0x4000 entries from a pre-7.0.9 pack) with server-supplied graphics without a bounds check at about 35 sites, so an out-of-era graphic throws. Guarded today: `FirstSightArt` (2) and the GPU path's own `_gpuStaticData`. Unguarded, reachable from server graphics: `Static.ItemData` (Static.cs:33), `Item.ItemData` (Item.cs:154), `Multi.ItemData` (Multi.cs:34), `ItemHold.ItemData` (ItemHold.cs:58), `DragEffect` (112), `GameEffectView` (102), `PlayerMobile` (299, 303: `Graphic ± 1`), `PacketHandlers` (3498), `TargetManager` (447), `Pathfinder` (211), `GameScene` (539), `GameSceneDrawingSorting` (126, 175, 529, 1275, 1366), `GameSceneGpuItemCache` (291), `GameSceneGpuWorld` (261), `GameSceneInputHandler` (504), `HouseCustomizationManager` (1102, 1420), `StaticFilters` (88, 140), `ButtonTileArt` (40), `ItemGump` (63), `StaticPic` (56), `CombatBookGump` (240), `CounterBarGump.CounterItem` (463), `MenuGump` (159), `ShopGump` (687, 808, 845), `Plugin` (425); `AnimatedStaticsManager` (28) loops within Length. Not a few-line fix site by site. Proposal: the loader pads `StaticData` to 0x10000 default entries for packs with fewer (about 0xC000 × the record size, ~2 MB per client, legacy packs only), which makes every site safe at once; it changes `StaticData.Length` (the legacy test asserts 0x4000, and loops over Length would grow), so it needs the owner's nod. **Decided 2026-10-31 (owner): pad, as a standardized pack format** (every `tiledata.bin` has 0x4000 land and 0x10000 statics; the converter pads); see "tiledata: standardized counts" below.

**Verification.** Client builds (Release, and `-p:CuoDevTools=false`): 0 errors. `dotnet test tests/ClassicUO.UnitTests -c Release` with `CUO_LEGACY_PACK` (the UOML pack below) and `CUO_LEGACY_UO`: 996 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed (`LegacyPackLoadTests` ran; 9 new `ClientVersionTests`). `dotnet test tests/Uo.Converter.Tests`: 32 passed with `CUO_LEGACY_UO` (without it: 31 passed, 1 skipped). UOML full conversion (23 s) and `--verify-only`: all checks passed; facets expected from the source: 0 and 1 7168x4096 (map0.mul), 2, 3, 4; every block of all five facets EXACT against the oracle; the five facets' region files are byte-identical to the pack of e58afd14b. Classic spot check (`--only tiledata,data,maps` from `C:/Ultima Online Classic` into a hard-linked copy of classic-1.0 in scratch): all checks passed; regions differ from classic-1.0 only in the six known files (0/r_0_2, 1/r_0_2, 2/r_0_1, 3/r_0_0, 4/r_0_1, 5/r_0_0), byte-identical to e58afd14b's spot pack; multis.bin identical.

**Codex round 2** (coordinator scratchpad `astra-legacy2/out.md`, on 235792ae3: four findings, three P2 and one P3; the stock UOP mapping, trailing blocks, offset-0 statics, signed indexes, patch semantics, source selection and the lettered-constant comparisons were checked and found fine). Dispositions:
1. **P2, maps-only verification skipped every map check.** `Verify.Run` returned before `CheckMaps` when the pack had no `tiledata.bin`, which `--only maps` permits, so a narrow or facet-missing pack passed on manifest hashes alone. Fixed: the tile data, tables and atlas checks move into `CheckTileDataAndAtlases`, run only when `tiledata.bin` exists; `CheckMaps` and the region timings run either way. Test: `Verify_Run_Checks_The_Maps_Of_A_Maps_Only_Pack_Without_Tiledata` goes through `Verify.Run` with `Only = {maps}` on packs without tiledata: too narrow (1448 pack, 1456 source) fails, missing facet 2 fails, the right pack passes. It fails on 235792ae3's Verify.cs ("expected false, found True").
2. **P2, a facet directory copied under another index was checked against the wrong source.** `CheckMaps` chose the expected size and the oracle by `facet.json`'s index. Fixed: the manifest's index (which also names the directory) is the facet; `facet.json` must agree (`facet 1: facet.json says facet 0, the manifest and directory say 1`, and the facet is not checked further), and the expected size, the oracle, the region header check and the messages all use the manifest index. Test: `Verify_Fails_A_Facet_Directory_Copied_Under_Another_Index` (synthetic 512x4096 map0 at 4.0.11c, where Trammel is map0, so the copied Felucca matches Trammel's source block for block; map/0 copied to map/1 with facet 0's facet.json and region headers fails; the real Trammel passes). It fails on 235792ae3's Verify.cs.
3. **P2, converter tests outside CI:** deferred to CI work (owner); the explicit `dotnet test tests/Uo.Converter.Tests/Uo.Converter.Tests.csproj` step is recorded in `cuo-poc-state/handoffs/ci-release-artifacts.md`.
4. **P3, a configured fixture that is missing was reported as skipped.** Fixed: `LegacyPackFact` skips only while `CUO_LEGACY_PACK` or `CUO_LEGACY_UO` is unset; once set, the test asserts `manifest.json` in the pack and `map0.mul`, `mapdifl1.mul`, `mapdif1.mul` in the install, so a conversion that did not produce its fixture fails (checked: an empty `CUO_LEGACY_PACK` folder fails with "is set, so it must hold a converted pack"; unset skips). The converter tests' `LegacyUoFact` follows the same rule (skips only when `CUO_LEGACY_UO` is unset; the test asserts `map0.mul`).

Verification: client builds (Release, and `-p:CuoDevTools=false`): 0 errors. `dotnet test tests/ClassicUO.UnitTests -c Release` with `CUO_LEGACY_PACK` and `CUO_LEGACY_UO`: 996 passed, 4 skipped (none of them the legacy test), 0 failed. `dotnet test tests/Uo.Converter.Tests`: 34 passed with `CUO_LEGACY_UO`; 33 passed, 1 skipped without it. `--verify-only` on the UOML pack: all checks passed, facets 0-4 expected from the source and every block EXACT against the oracle; on the classic spot pack (`--only tiledata,data,maps`): all checks passed, facets 0-5 expected from the LegacyMUL.uop maps.

## Memory per client, round 3: page staging slots stop cycling (2026-10-31)

Branch `poc/mem-reduce-3` from poc/modern-client 75747c25b. Owner-approved follow-up to round 2's diagnosis (bench-000044: the art staging containers hold 6–8 buffers of 10.67 MiB where 4 slots need 42.7 MiB).

**Change (cc3f904ee).** Before, `PageResidency.StartLoads` mapped a free staging slot with `cycle=true`. When the slot's previous copy was still in flight, SDL_GPU added a buffer to that slot's container, and containers never shrink. Now:
- `CopyRetirement` (owned by `Renderer`) numbers each frame command buffer. A frame that carries page staging copies is submitted with `SDL_SubmitGPUCommandBufferAndAcquireFence`, and the renderer polls that fence without blocking (`SDL_QueryGPUFence`, in submit order) at the start of `StartLoads` and before `Upload`. A signalled fence retires its serial and every earlier one, and the fence is released. Frames without staging copies take no fence. The offscreen throttle, GPU-sample, screenshot and drain paths wait for their own fences, so they mark the serial retired themselves. A failed submit counted as retired (wrong; replaced after the Codex audit, below).
- `StagingSlots` (one per `PageResidency`, so art and anim alike) records the serial of each slot's last copy. A slot is mapped only once that serial has retired, and with `cycle=false`. A queued page that finds only slots still being copied from stays queued for a later frame; the game loop never waits. Without a tracker (a host that does not render through `Renderer`), slots map with cycling as before.
- Slot waits are counted as episodes (runs of frames in which a queued page waited only for a copy to retire), frames, and ms (from an episode's first frame to the frame it ends, plus the longest episode). They are logged on the new `GPU world settled` line and on the DevBench 5 s stats line (`staging art ..., anim ...; copy fences N taken, M pending`).
- Instrumentation (756365911, also in the base arm): `[load] GPU world settled (<facet>) after X ms, N frames; last page upload at Y ms; art r/l resident, u uploads; anim ...`. It is logged once per world build or facet change (the login is one), timed from the first world frame until `WorldRenderer.Settled` (no chunk pending, no page queued, loading or missing).
- Tests: `StagingSlotsTests` (10 cases, fake fences, no GPU): a slot is reused only after its fence; retirement is in order (a later fence signalling first retires nothing); a frame without copies takes no fence; a failed submit or an outside wait retires the serial; without a tracker everything is reusable and cycles; dispose releases pending fences; wait statistics. A burst model (4 slots; 40, 13 and 4 pages; copies retiring 1–3 frames after submit) checks that no slot is rewritten while its copy is in flight, that every page loads, that each frame with copies takes one fence, and that only bursts larger than the slots wait.
- Verified: unit tests 1078 pass, 1 skipped; client Release build and the `-p:CuoDevTools=false` build have 0 errors; Uo.Render.App and Uo.Client build.
