### Codex audit (coordinator scratchpad `astra-memreduce3/out.md`) and dispositions (2026-10-31)

Codex found one P1 and one P2; both are fixed. Successful-submit coverage, the outside waits, fence ordering, normal fence lifetime, liveness, facet changes and reinit, idle-frame cost and multi-instance safety were checked and found fine.
- **P1, a failed submit retired copies the GPU might still run (fixed).** `CopyRetirement.Track` with a zero fence, and the throttle path's zero fence, called `MarkRetired(serial)`. That was wrong twice over: a null fence does not prove the buffer never ran (D3D12 executes the list before it acquires the fence; Vulkan can queue it and then fail at present), and since retirement is a watermark, a failed frame 2 also retired a still-running frame 1. Now a failed submit (zero fence from `SubmitFrame`, the throttle path or a frame screenshot) calls `CopyRetirement.Failed(serial)`, which retires nothing: the slots it copied from stay unavailable until a later fence signals (polled in submit order, so earlier unsignalled fences still come first) or a successful wait covers a later serial (throttle, GPU sample, screenshot) or the whole GPU (`DrainInFlight`). The queue runs in submit order, so that proof also covers the failed frame if it ran. For liveness, `NeedsFence` stays true while a failure is unresolved, so the next frame is submitted with a fence even without copies; once that fence signals, the slots free up without a blocking wait. The simpler choice over forcing an idle wait after a failure: nothing blocks in the frame loop, and on a lost device every later submit fails too, so the slots just stay blocked (safe) instead of a wait that also fails. State is one serial, so repeated failures use no memory. `Poll` now also releases, unqueried, the fences a successful wait elsewhere already covered (serial at or below the watermark). Callers that continue after `RenderFrame` returns false: the client reports `SubmitFailures` as device lost and exits; Uo.Render.App, Uo.Client and AnimSheet keep rendering, and with the fix they keep the failed frame's slots blocked until a later fence or drain proves completion.
- **P2, a failed world disposal skipped the fence cleanup (fixed).** `WorldRenderer.Dispose` called `DrainInFlight` first, so when it threw (device lost), the workers, page residencies and owned renderer were never disposed, and `_copies` never released its fences. Now the steps run through `Teardown.Run`: every step runs in order, the first exception is rethrown with its stack after they all ran, and later ones go to stderr. The owned renderer's `Dispose` catches its own failed drain and releases the tracker's fences.
- Tests: `StagingSlotsTests` now has 16 cases (was 10; the "failed submit retires" case is replaced): a failed submit retires nothing and a later fenced frame resolves it; a failed submit behind an unsignalled earlier fence keeps slot A unavailable (also when the later fence signals first); a failure after execution started keeps the slot through repeated failures until a fenced frame signals; a GPU-idle wait resolves a failure and releases the pending fences; throttle, screenshot, ordinary and drain retirement on one serial line, never going back; art and anim slot sets sharing the one tracker (modelled with their `StagingSlots`, since `PageResidency` needs a GPU device); a failed world disposal through `Teardown.Run` (drain and a pages step throw; every step runs, the drain's exception is reported, and the fences are released). The burst model now picks fences by `NeedsFence` and drains its final submissions: no fence pending, every fence released once, every slot reusable, and the watermark at the last serial.
- The normal path bench-000048 measures is unchanged: on success the same fences are taken, polled and released.
- Verified: client Release build and `-p:CuoDevTools=false` build, 0 errors; unit tests 1084 pass, 1 skipped (was 1078: +6). No client runs.
- **Codex round 2 (`astra-memreduce3r2/out.md`), P2, a retried world disposal released freed handles (fixed).** After the `Teardown.Run` change, a failed drain still released the pages and the owned renderer, and `GpuWorldRenderer`'s facet-rebuild catch then disposed the same world again (stale transfer buffers and fences; SDL's Vulkan backend frees transfer-buffer containers at once). Now `WorldRenderer.Dispose` is one-shot (`Teardown.Once` sets the disposed state before any step), `PageResidency.Dispose` and `Renderer.Dispose` are one-shot too, and `GpuWorldRenderer.DisposeWorld` clears `_world` before disposing it (all three call sites). Test `A_retried_world_disposal_after_a_failed_drain_releases_nothing_twice` runs a fake world through `Teardown.Once` (WorldRenderer needs a device): drain throws, cleanup completes, two retries are no-ops, every step and fence ran once. Unit tests 1085 pass, 1 skipped; both client builds 0 errors.

## Sounds and music in the pack (2026-10-31, `poc/audio-pack`)

Owner decision Q10 (data-formats.md): sound effects as raw PCM, music as the original MP3 bytes with the loop flag, decoded by dr_mp3 on the music worker. Base `poc/modern-client` f69641b97. Formats: pack-format.md, "Audio".

**What changed**
- **Pack:** two record stores. `audio/sounds.bin` (`SNDS`) has a record per distinct sound: raw 22,050 Hz mono 16-bit PCM, then the 40-byte entry name up to its NUL. `Sound.def` aliases share a record. `audio/music.bin` (`MUSC`) has a record per distinct MP3 file: the file's bytes, then the file name. The loop flag sits on each id's slot, since ids naming one file can differ in it. Both stores are codec 0 only. `Uo.Pack/AudioStores.cs` holds the format constants and the record checks. `RecordStore.OpenRawStream` gives a positional stream over a raw record.
- **Converter:** new stages `sounds` and `music` (`--only sounds,music`, `--no-sounds`, `--no-music`).
  - `AudioImport.cs` reads what the client read: `soundLegacyMUL.uop` on UOP installs, else `sound.mul` + `soundidx.mul`, with `Sound.def` and loose `Sounds/*.wav`; for music, `Music/Digital/Config.txt` (or `Music/Config.txt`, or the built-in table) and `GetTrueFileName`'s lookup. It depends only on ClassicUO.IO and Uo.Pack, so the unit tests compile it in.
  - Verification compares against a new frozen copy of the client's `SoundsLoader` (tools/ClassicUO.Assets.Mul): every id 0..0xFFFE, sound PCM and name byte-exact, and every music id's loop flag and MP3 bytes byte-exact against the file.
  - `--audio-report <pack>` gives the offline measurements below.
  - `--client-version x.y.z.w` is an interim flag for exes without version info. poc/legacy-import replaces it with its full resolution under the same name; expect a small conflict in Program.cs at merge, and keep legacy-import's version.
- **Client:** `SoundsLoader` reads only the pack. The client no longer opens sound.mul, soundLegacyMUL.uop, Sound.def, Config.txt or the MP3s; there is no MUL fallback.
  - **Loose `Sounds/<id>.wav` files still win at runtime.** The client already supported them, and the converter also folds them into the pack.
  - `UOSound` takes the PCM as its own array (it took an `ArraySegment` of the record array until the bench-000049 fix below).
  - `UOMusic` and `MusicStream` take an opener. The worker reads the record into native memory, and `Mp3Validator` checks it before dr_mp3, as it did for files.
  - Every record and music slot is checked at load. Overlapping payloads reject the whole store.
  - A first read per sound id is logged at Trace (`sound <id> (<name>): first read … ms`).
- **Fix, on purpose: 4.0.11c music.** ClassicUO parses "4.0.11c" as 0x04000B02, but `CV_4011C` is 0x04000B63 (the letter as ASCII). So no parsed 4.0.11x reached it, and UOML read the built-in table: 57 of its 67 ids had no file. The converter compares with the parsed value, and the frozen loader carries the same one-line change, marked. UOML now gets its own `Music/Digital/Config.txt`: 57 ids, all with a file.

**Conversions (into the session scratch, `--only sounds,music`, then `--verify-only --only sounds,music`):**

| install | sounds | music | verify |
|---|---|---|---|
| `C:/Ultima Online Classic` 7.0.103 (UOP) | 1,667 slots, 1,656 ids, 1,655 records (1 alias), 160.4 MiB PCM, file 160.5 MiB; 0.6 s | 103 slots, 102 ids (41 loop), 90 MP3 files, 103.5 MiB; 0.3 s | all EXACT (sounds 0.3 s, music 0.1 s) |
| `D:/…/UOML` 4.0.11c (MUL, interim `--client-version 4.0.11c`) | 1,488 slots, 1,488 ids, 1,487 records (1 alias), 107.8 MiB; 0.5 s | 57 ids (39 loop), 45 files, 53.2 MiB; 0.2 s | all EXACT |

The UOML exe has no version info, so it needed the interim flag. poc/legacy-import detects 4.0.11c by itself; with it merged, UOML converts without the flag.

**Measured offline** (`--audio-report`, classic, `DOTNET_TieredCompilation=0`, 2 runs, warm file cache; old = the frozen pre-pack loader on the same install):

| | old (UOP + Config.txt + loose MP3) | pack | notes |

| `SoundsLoader.Load` | 39.1 / 45.9 ms median (min 35.8–38.5), 15.0 MiB allocated | 0.25 / 0.28 ms (min 0.23–0.25), 62 KB allocated | the old load indexed the UOP and scanned `Music/` once per Config.txt line (102 scans) |
| held after load (GC heap) | 3,330 KB (65,535 `UOFileIndex` entries) plus a 160.6 MiB read-only mapping of soundLegacyMUL.uop | 56 KB (tables 54.7 KB), no mapping | |
| sound first read (all 1,656 sounds) | p50 0.036–0.040, p99 0.38–0.44, max 14–19 ms | p50 0.023–0.026, p99 0.22–0.24, max 7.5–13.7 ms | max = beatSlow (21 MB); one read either way |
| music: MP3 bytes into memory (102 ids) | p50 0.32–0.39 ms, max 5.5–11.8 | p50 0.26–0.31 ms, max 4.6–7.0 | the decode is unchanged (dr_mp3 on the worker) |

Noise: two runs, under other agents' build load; the old/new ratios hold in both runs. The read times are page-cache bound; a cold read is disk-bound either way.

**Memory and the trade-off** (the owner's rule: every held cost logged):

| item | cost per client | benefit |
|---|---|---|
| store tables (slots + records of both stores) | +0.05 MiB held | replaces ~3.3 MiB of UOP index entries and the 160.6 MiB file mapping; load 39 ms → 0.25 ms |
| sound cache (as first written: a sound's PCM kept from its first play for the session; **bounded to 64 MiB after the Codex audit**, see "Codex audit and dispositions" below) | 0 new; grew with the sounds played, as before | no read on replays; first plays are one positional read, p50 0.02 ms |
| music | 0 new: per play, the MP3 is read into native memory (as from the file before) | — |
| pack size | +264.0 MiB on disk (160.5 + 103.5) | the same bytes the install had (168.4 MB UOP + 103.5 MiB MP3s); no derived copies. FLAC would save ~52 MB (survey) and was declined (Q10) |

**Sounds load on demand**, not at startup: 160 MiB of PCM resident in every client (several run at once) would buy nothing, since a first read costs about 0.02 ms.

**Tests:** `AudioPackTests` (11, synthetic, no UO data):
- the importer on a synthetic sound.mul/soundidx.mul with Sound.def aliases, -1, a skipped line, a short entry and loose WAVs (wrong rate ignored, new id added), read back through the client's `SoundsLoader`;
- the loose-WAV runtime override;
- a music round trip (shared file, the loop flag per id, a missing file and a bad MP3 left out) and the built-in table;
- a looping track from a pack record through `MusicStream`, sample-exact across the seam (the seam-noise fixture);
- hostile stores:
  - truncated tables or payloads;
  - a slot count above 0xFFFF or 2²⁴, refused before allocation;
  - overlapping payloads, a payload inside the tables, an oversized record;
  - a 44.1 kHz record left out while the others play, plus every record and slot check;
  - junk MP3 bytes that fail the stream cleanly;
  - no audio in the pack (silence, no crash).

Unit tests: 1,079 passed, 1 skipped (pre-existing). Client Release and `-p:CuoDevTools=false` builds: 0 errors.

### Audio pack: the first sound effect crashed the client (bench-000049), fixed

**Failure.** In bench-000049, music played, but the first footstep (`sound 299 (feet12a.wav)`, 17,980 bytes of PCM) threw an unhandled `ArgumentException` in `DynamicSoundEffectInstance.SubmitBuffer` ("Buffer is invalid ... block alignment"), and the client exited after 11 s. Minoc, Cove and the walk never ran.

**Root cause.** `SoundsLoader.TryGetSound` read the whole record (PCM, then the name) into one array and handed `UOSound` an `ArraySegment` over the PCM part. `Sound.Play` passed `(segment.Array, offset 0, count = PCM)`. FNA's `SubmitBuffer` checks `buffer.Length % nBlockAlign` on the *whole array*, not on `count`. With mono 16-bit, `nBlockAlign` is 2, so any sound whose name has an odd byte count (`feet12a.wav` is 11) failed, although its PCM was even and correct. The stored format, the slicing and the converter's 40-byte header strip were all right. The old loader handed FNA an array of exactly the PCM (`new byte[entry.Length - 40]`), so it never hit this. The verify said EXACT because it compared the PCM slice with the frozen loader's bytes. It never looked at the array the client submits, and the unit tests compared `data.AsSpan()`, which hid the array length too.

**Fix.**
- `AudioConst.ReadSound` (Uo.Pack) is the client's decode. It makes two positional reads (`RecordStore.ReadRaw`, new): the PCM into an array of exactly its length, then the name. `TryGetSound` returns that `byte[]`, and `UOSound` takes a `byte[]` again, so a record can't share its array with anything.
- Bad records are refused before FNA sees them:
  - `CheckSoundRecord` now also rejects empty PCM and an odd PCM length (`CheckPcmLength`), at load, with one log line per record. The other records still play.
  - `TryGetSound` checks the result against FNA's argument rules (`AudioConst.SubmitError`, a mirror of `SubmitBuffer`'s checks) before it returns.
  - A loose `Sounds/<id>.wav` with an odd or empty data chunk is ignored with one warning, and the pack's sound plays.
  - As a backstop, `Sound.Play` skips any buffer that fails `Sound.CanSubmit` (the same rules) instead of letting FNA throw.
- Converter: the importer leaves out PCM the client would refuse (counted as "unplayable" and listed as a warning). Stock 7.0.103 has none, and the rebuilt `audio/sounds.bin` and `music.bin` are byte-identical to the previous ones (sha256).
- Verify: each sound is now decoded with the client's own `ReadSound`, the array is checked against `SubmitError`, and then it is compared byte for byte with the frozen loader's array. Result on 7.0.103: EXACT, 1,656 ids, 1,655 records. The limit: verify and client share `ReadSound`, so a client that bypassed it would not be caught. The unit test below covers `UOSound` itself.

**Tests** (`AudioPackTests`, +4):
- `A_Real_Shaped_Record_Reaches_FNA_As_Exactly_Its_Pcm`: a sound.mul entry shaped like bench-000049's (a 40-byte name field holding `feet12a.wav` + 17,980 bytes of PCM) goes through the converter, `SoundsLoader` and `UOSound.GetBuffer`. The submitted span is offset 0, count 17,980, an array of 17,980 bytes equal to the PCM, and it passes both FNA mirrors. The old shape (a 17,991-byte payload array) fails both.
- `The_Two_Mirrors_Of_FNAs_Submit_Rules_Agree`: `Sound.CanSubmit` against `AudioConst.SubmitError` on 9 cases (odd array, odd count, odd offset, empty, null, offset at the end, stereo).
- `Bad_Sound_Records_Are_Refused_Before_FNA_And_The_Rest_Play`: a patched record with odd PCM and one with no PCM. `TryGetSound` returns false without throwing, and the other record plays. The converter leaves out an odd entry with one warning.
- `An_Odd_Length_Loose_Wave_Is_Ignored_And_The_Pack_Sound_Plays`.
- The existing `Expect` helper now also checks that the array length equals the PCM length.
- A real `DynamicSoundEffectInstance` needs an audio device, so the tests stop at the exact `(array, offset, count)` that `Sound.Play` passes and at the mirror of FNA's checks.

**Verification.** Client builds Release and `-p:CuoDevTools=false`: 0 errors. Uo.Converter: 0 errors. `dotnet test tests/ClassicUO.UnitTests -c Release`: 1,083 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed. Converter `--verify-only --only sounds,music` on the test pack: all checks passed. Memory: a sound's cached array no longer holds its name (at most 40 bytes less per played sound). A first play makes two positional reads instead of one (the name read is at most 40 bytes).

**Client re-check: bench-000050** (the same listen job, a Release JIT build of ee1b24f60, the same 1.0-based scratch test pack; the branch predates the classic-1.1 tiledata merge). Status ok, 246 s, and the whole plan ran (Britain, Minoc, Cove, walk).
- Audio load: "Audio: pack, 1655 sound records, 90 music records in 8.35 ms", with no record refused.
- Music first buffer: LoginLoop 121.3 ms, Britainpos 79.7 ms (the first plays include JIT time), Minocpos 0.7 ms, Cove 0.7 ms, Britainpos again 1.2 ms. Britainpos and Cove each logged "looped (1)".
- Sounds: 7 ids played, first reads 0.028–0.070 ms, plus 3.0 ms for the very first (feet12a, the id that crashed bench-000049). The ids: feet12a/b, rat2, bird06, dog2, cat2, chicken2.
- No soundLegacyMUL.uop or MP3 file was opened, and there were no errors or exceptions.

### Audio pack: Codex audit and dispositions (2026-10-31)

Codex (gpt-6-astra) audited c1790edbe read-only and found six issues; all six are fixed in 1d7e8b897, each with a synthetic test (`AudioPackAuditTests`, 9 tests). Codex found no further playback regression: pack bounds, FNA submission shape, MP3 validation, names, import compatibility, threading and lifetime checked out.

| # | finding | disposition |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **P1, unbounded sound cache.** Every first-played id allocated and kept its own PCM, aliases included: one 64 MiB record with 128 aliases could hold 8 GiB (plus FNA's copies). | **Fixed.** `Renderer.Sounds.SoundCache` replaces the per-id array. Ids that share a record (`SoundsLoader.TryGetSoundSource` gives the record as key) share one immutable array. The distinct arrays stay within **64 MiB** and at most 1,024 ids are cached; the least recently played id that is not playing is evicted (its `UOSound` disposed, the array dropped when no other id uses it). A pack sound's size is known before the read, so a sound that cannot fit (everything else playing) is refused without reading it, and logged. Simultaneous submissions were unbounded in ClassicUO (one instance per id, but any number of ids at once): `AudioManager` now plays at most **32** sound effects and **64 MiB** of PCM at once; `Sound.LimitPlaying` stops the oldest, and a replay of a playing id is not counted twice. Tests: one 1 MiB record + 128 aliases holds 1 MiB in one shared array within a 1.5 MiB budget (Codex's case scaled 64x); 12 distinct 256 KiB sounds cycled twice through a 1 MiB budget (always within it, 20 LRU evictions, the most recent kept); the id cap; playing sounds pinned and a sound that cannot fit refused; the count and byte caps on playing sounds, aliases included. |
| 2 | **P2, loose WAV overflow** (client `SoundsLoader.ReadWave`, importer `AudioImport.ReadWave`): `at + 8 + size` overflowed for a data size of 0x7FFFFFF0 in a 44-byte file, skipped the clamp and tried a ~2 GiB allocation; `ReadAllBytes` had no size cap. | **Fixed.** One reader for both, `AudioConst.ParseWave` / `ReadWaveFile` (Uo.Pack): the file size is checked against `MaxWaveFileBytes` (64 MiB + 1 MiB) before the read, every chunk size is compared by subtraction (`size > length - at - 8`, then clamped to the end as ClassicUO did), and every failure is an error string, never an exception. Codex's file yields an empty data chunk, refused as "no PCM", and the pack's sound plays. Tests: Codex's 44-byte WAV, a huge LIST chunk, a file over the cap refused before reading, the client falling back to the pack sound. The frozen loader's ReadWave got the same one-line subtraction (marked), so verify cannot throw on such a file. |
| 3 | **P2, zero-length records bypass the overlap check** (`CheckNoOverlap` compared neighbours only and skipped pairs with an empty record). | **Fixed.** The sweep keeps the furthest end of all earlier non-empty payloads; empty records never reset it (this also catches a short record inside a long one, two records after the first). Tests: Codex's [128,228), [138,138), [148,168) in both table orders, two records inside a long one, adjacent and empty records accepted, and the same layout as real `sounds.bin` and `music.bin` files, which the client rejects. |
| 4 | **P2, an invalid loose override hid a valid archive sound** in the converter (`SoundSource.TryGet` picked the override, `WriteSounds` then dropped the id), and verify approved it (it expected the frozen loader's invalid override, i.e. "absent"). | **Fixed.** `SoundSource.TryGet` applies the client's eligibility (`ReadWaveFile`: size cap, format, non-empty even PCM) while resolving precedence, and falls back to the archive entry; refused files are counted (`LooseRefused`) and listed as warnings. Verify models the same resolution from the frozen loader's own answers: `AudioImport.ExpectedClientSound` takes the old `TryGetSound` and, past a loose file the client refuses, the old loader's archive read alone (`TryGetArchiveSound`, split out of the frozen `TryGetSound` unchanged, marked). Test: odd, empty, overflowing and wrong-rate overrides over valid archive entries, a valid override, and an odd override with no archive entry. The converter writes the archive sounds, the client reads them back from the pack alone and with the loose files present, and verify's model on the real frozen loader (now referenced by the tests under an extern alias) agrees, while the old loader alone still returns the 81-byte override. |
| 5 | **P3, the frozen loader leaked its archive**: `ClearResources` cleared only the static music table, so `--audio-report` mapped the archive again on every load. | **Fixed** (marked "Not verbatim" in tools/ClassicUO.Assets.Mul/SoundsLoader.cs): `ClearResources` disposes `_file`, the music table is per instance (a second loader's built-in-table `Add` threw on the static one), and `--audio-report` clears every temporary loader it opens. Also fixed: `--audio-report` with `--out` went through the full-conversion path and cleared the output folder's manifest files first. It now converts nothing and touches no output. That is how this session's scratch test pack lost its non-audio files; it was rebuilt from classic-1.0 (hard links) plus the two stores. Test: two frozen loaders load in turn, and after `ClearResources` the synthetic sound.mul can be deleted (the mapping is gone). |
| 6 | **P3, slot fields**: sound `arg` was ignored though the format says 0; `reserved` was unchecked for both. | **Fixed.** `CheckSoundSlot` (arg 0, reserved 0) and `CheckMusicSlot` (arg bit 0 only, reserved 0) run at load in the client and in verify. A failing slot is absent; its record still serves other ids. pack-format.md "Audio" now has a table of every field and whether readers reject or ignore it: header `flags` and `reserved` are ignored (informational), and everything that changes how a payload is read is checked. Test: Codex's sound slot with arg 0xFFFF, a sound slot and a music slot with reserved bits, the other ids still playing. |

**Memory and the trade-off** (the owner's rule):

| item | cost per client | benefit |
|---|---|---|
| sound cache, now bounded | at most **64 MiB** of PCM held (was unbounded: 160 MiB for stock data if every sound played, unbounded with aliases), plus at most 1,024 cached `UOSound`s | replays need no read. Why 64 MiB: stock 7.0.103 has 1,655 records, 160.4 MiB in total, median 55 KB, p95 220 KB, p99 447 KB; only three are over 1 MiB (8.2, 9.8 and 20.2 MiB, beatSlow the largest). bench-000050's whole plan (Britain, Minoc, Cove, a walk) played 7 ids, about 0.4 MB of PCM. A long session that plays 300 distinct typical sounds holds about 16 MiB. 64 MiB keeps that and all three large ones at once, and equals `MaxSoundBytes`, so the largest sound the format allows still fits on its own. A typical client holds well under 1 MiB, the same as before. |
| playing limit | at most 32 sounds and **64 MiB** of FNA native copies at once (was unbounded) | bounds what a shard can make the client submit; 32 simultaneous effects is far above what a scene plays |

**Pack bytes:** unchanged for stock data. `--only sounds,music` on 7.0.103 rewrote `audio/sounds.bin` (sha256 f41571ce...) and `audio/music.bin` (8085e9e0...) byte-identical to c1790edbe's. The install has no loose WAVs, so the precedence fix changes nothing there. `--verify-only --only sounds,music`: sounds 1,656 ids EXACT, music 102 ids EXACT, all checks passed. `--audio-report` ran clean on the rebuilt test pack. Its old load was 20.0 ms median this time, against 39-46 ms in the earlier report, when every repetition left one more 160 MiB mapping open. That is one run, not a series, so read it as a hint that the leak inflated the earlier "old" numbers, not as a measurement.

**Verification.** Client Release and `-p:CuoDevTools=false` builds: 0 errors; Uo.Converter: 0 errors. `dotnet test tests/ClassicUO.UnitTests -c Release`: 1,092 passed, 1 skipped (pre-existing), 0 failed (`AudioPackTests` 24 = 15 + 9). Client check of the cache and playing limit: **bench-000051** (`listen-audit`, the bench-000050 plan on a Release JIT build of 1d7e8b897 and the rebuilt 1.0-based test pack): status ok, 252 s, and the whole plan ran (Britain, Minoc, Cove, walk).
- Audio load: 1,655 sound records and 90 music records in 9.96 ms, with no record or slot refused.
- Sounds: 6 ids played (feet12a/b, rat2, dog2, bird06, cat2). Each was read once, 0.029-0.047 ms, plus 2.9 ms for the very first; the footsteps then replayed from the cache with no second read. No "do not fit" warning was logged.
- Music: Britainpos 73.1 ms, Minocpos 0.7 ms, Cove 1.3 ms and Britainpos again 0.9 ms to the first buffer, and Britainpos and Cove looped. LoginLoop took 391 ms against 121 ms in bench-000050. It is the first play of the session (JIT), and the music path did not change, so this is one sample under machine load, not a regression.

### Audio pack: Codex round 2 and dispositions (2026-10-31)

Codex (gpt-6-astra) audited b3f7c6f93 read-only and found seven issues (four P2, two P3, plus `--audio-report` creating the debug folder). All are fixed in dddd0ee74, each with a synthetic test (`AudioPackRound2Tests`, 7 tests).

| # | finding | disposition |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **P2, `BufferNeeded` subscriptions accumulated.** `LimitPlaying` drops a replayed sound's list entry without `Stop`, FNA's own `Stop` keeps the event, and `Play` added another subscription each time: N overlapping replays left N, and one cleanup removed one. | **Fixed.** The sound owns its subscription, independent of any list: `SubscribeBufferNeeded` / `UnsubscribeBufferNeeded` keep at most one, on the current instance (a new instance moves it). `Play` subscribes, `Stop` and `Dispose` unsubscribe, all idempotent. Test: ten overlapping replays through the limiter leave exactly one subscription, one cleanup leaves none, and an instance swap moves it (an FNA instance without a native voice, read through the event's field). |
| 2 | **P2, reads before the size check.** Verify asked the frozen loader (unbounded `ReadAllBytes`) about a loose WAV before checking its size, and its later `FileInfo.Length` threw for a file that had vanished. Music import and verify read whole MP3s before Mp3Validator's size check. | **Fixed.** `ExpectedClientSound` first opens the loose file and checks that handle's length. A file over the cap, gone or locked goes to the archive, and the frozen loader is never asked. An `IOException` from the frozen loader (the file vanished after the check) also falls back. `AudioConst.ReadFileBounded` (one handle, length checked before any allocation) is used for music import and music verify, so an MP3 over 32 MiB is refused unread. Tests: an oversized, a missing and a locked loose file never reach the loader, and a loader that throws `FileNotFoundException` falls back. A 32 MiB + 1 MP3 is refused with under 1 MiB allocated by the read and under 8 MiB by `WriteMusic`. |
| 3 | **P2, a refused loose sound was reread on every request.** A loose source reported size -1, so its WAV and PCM (up to ~128 MiB of allocation) were read before the budget check, on the main thread, each time. An invalid override that fell back to a pack record skipped the pre-read budget check too. | **Fixed.** `TryGetSoundSource` probes a loose WAV's headers (`AudioConst.ProbeWaveFile`: one handle, the length cap, the chunk walk, a playable length; no payload) and remembers the PCM length. The read updates it if the file changed. A loose file the probe refuses is dropped there, so the pack record is named instead, with its size, and budgeted before it is read. In the cache, a refusal no longer evicts anything: `Fits` first checks whether evicting every idle id would make room. A refused sound is therefore remembered as its size, and each later request costs that scan and nothing else. It plays as soon as capacity changes (playing sounds finish), with exactly one payload read. Test: a 512 KiB loose sound and an invalid override over a 512 KiB pack record are refused 20 times each, under 64 KiB allocated per attempt, with no eviction. Once the playing sound stops, both play from one read each, and the override's id plays the pack's PCM. |
| 4 | **P2, inaudible sounds took voices.** A sound beyond the view range (volume 0) still went through the limiter and could stop the oldest audible sound, or several through the byte cap. | **Fixed.** `PlaySoundWithDistance` no longer submits a sound from beyond the view range. ClassicUO played it at volume 0, and its distance factor is the whole volume anyway, so nothing audible is lost. It is not read either. The one difference: ClassicUO's silent play started that id's replay delay, so the same id from within range in the next half-length was dropped, and now it plays. Sounds that are silent for other reasons (sound off, window in the background without background sound) still play as before. `UpdateCurrentSoundsVolume` can make them audible when sound is switched back on, so they are kept. But they never stop another sound: `LimitPlaying(audible: false)` returns -1 when there is no room, leaves the list untouched, and the caller skips the play. Audible sounds stop silent ones first (oldest first), then the oldest audible ones. Test: a full list of two audible and two silent sounds. A silent newcomer is refused and changes nothing, and a silent replay is admitted. An audible newcomer stops the oldest silent sound, not the oldest sound. Under the byte cap, a large silent sound evicts nothing and a large audible one takes silent sounds first. |
| 5 | **P2, the converter kept a PCM copy per alias.** The first pass read every id's archive entry, and only the second pass deduplicated. One 64 MiB entry with 128 aliases held 8 GiB during conversion. | **Fixed.** The first pass resolves each id's loose override (`TryGetLoose`), then its archive entry without reading it (`TryGetArchiveEntry`). An entry is read once (`ReadArchive`) and its PCM held once, whatever its alias count. The second pass writes records in the same order as before, so the pack bytes are unchanged. Test: a 4 MiB entry with 128 Sound.def aliases is read once (`ArchiveReads` 1) with under 32 MiB allocated in all (129 copies would be over 1 GiB). The result is one record, 129 ids and 128 aliases, and the client reads ids 0 and 128 byte-exact. |
| 6 | **P3, reload dropped playing sounds from the accounting.** `Clear` kept playing sounds alive but zeroed `Bytes`, so the new cache could fill its whole budget beside them. | **Fixed: they stay counted until they finish.** I chose this over stopping them on reload because a reload (the options gump) cutting off a sound would be heard, and a slightly smaller cache for a second is not. `Clear` disposes idle sounds and moves playing ones to a retired list that stays in `Bytes` and the id count. Each `Get` sweeps the list, disposing finished sounds and releasing their arrays. Test: a sound playing across `Clear` keeps its 256 KiB counted. With the budget full of playing sounds, a new one is refused. Once the survivor finishes, the new one fits without an eviction. |
| 7 | **P3, a check/read race on the WAV size.** `FileInfo.Length` was taken from the path, then `ReadAllBytes` opened the file again. | **Fixed.** `ReadWaveFile` opens one handle, checks its length, walks the chunk headers by positional reads (the same `WalkWave` that `ParseWave` runs on bytes in memory), and then reads exactly the PCM from that handle. A file that shrinks mid-read is an error, not an exception. A new `maxPcmBytes` refuses from the header before reading. Test: seven WAV shapes give the same result through the handle and in memory: good, odd, empty, wrong rate, too short, a padded odd-size LIST chunk, and a data size clamped at the end. A 4 MiB WAV over `maxPcmBytes` is refused with under 64 KiB allocated, and missing and locked files give errors. |
| - | **`--audio-report` created the debug folder** (`Program.cs:143`). | **Fixed.** The folder is not created for `--audio-report`. Checked: with `--debug <new folder>` and `--out <empty folder>`, the report ran and neither folder gained anything. |

**The playing limit: 32 raised to 256, and why.** The old client had no limit, so the cap is a guard against pathological shards, not a mixing policy, and it must not cut sounds in ordinary crowded play.
- **What it counts.** Each id is one `UOSound` with one FAudio voice, and a replay waits half the sound's length, so the cap counts *distinct ids sounding at once*, not packets.
- **What a crowd sends.** In ModernUO, every swing sends two sounds (`BaseWeapon`: the attacker's hit or miss sound and the defender's hurt sound, which differ per weapon and creature type). Spells add cast and effect sounds, and creatures add idle, anger and death sounds. Footsteps come from the client, but only four ids (0x129-0x12C).
- **How many overlap.** The median stock sound lasts 1.25 s (55 KB at 44.1 KB/s). A large fight or a champion spawn can plausibly have 30-60 distinct ids sounding at once, so 32 could audibly cut sounds there, as Codex suspected.
- **What a voice costs.** Neither FNA nor FAudio limits voices: FNA never throws `InstancePlayLimitException`, and FAudio keeps source voices in a list, with no cap. A voice costs its native PCM copy, which the unchanged 64 MiB byte cap bounds, plus mixing time.
- **Why 256.** It is far above a crowded scene, so ordinary and crowded play sound as before, and it still bounds the mixer's work. The cache's 1,024 ids bound it as well.
- **Not measured.** No crowded-combat client run measured the distinct-id overlap. A DevBench count of `_currentSounds` in the TestScene would confirm it.

**Memory and the trade-off** (the owner's rule):

| item | cost per client | benefit |
|---|---|---|
| loose-WAV size memo | one int per loose file probed (0 on a stock install, which has no loose WAVs) | a sound the cache cannot hold yet is refused without file I/O |
| retired playing sounds | after a reload, the PCM of sounds still playing, until they finish, within the same 64 MiB budget (no new memory: the cap now holds) | a reload never cuts a sound off |
| playing count cap 256 (was 32) | no fixed cost. Up to 256 FAudio voices could exist at once; their native PCM stays within the unchanged 64 MiB cap | no audible cut-off in a crowded fight; see above |
| converter | one PCM copy per archive entry instead of one per id (stock: 1 alias, so about 0 MiB saved) | conversion memory stays bounded by distinct entries |

**Pack bytes:** unchanged. `--only sounds,music` on 7.0.103 rewrote `audio/sounds.bin` (sha256 f41571ce...) and `audio/music.bin` (8085e9e0...) byte-identical. `--verify-only --only sounds,music`: sounds 1,656 ids EXACT, music 102 ids EXACT, all checks passed.

**Verification.** Client Release and `-p:CuoDevTools=false` builds: 0 errors. Uo.Converter: 0 errors. `dotnet test tests/ClassicUO.UnitTests -c Release`: 1,100 passed, 1 skipped (pre-existing), 0 failed (`AudioPackTests`: 32, of which 7 are new). Client check: **bench-000052** (`listen-round2`) runs the bench-000051 plan on a Release JIT build of dddd0ee74. Result: status ok, 249.7 s, and the whole plan ran (Britain, Minoc, Cove, walk; `[bench] plan done`). Six sound ids were each read once, then served from the cache (feet12a 2.7 ms on the first read, the others 0.025-0.090 ms). The log has no errors, no "do not fit" warning, and no UOP or MP3 file opened. Music: Britainpos 72.1 ms (JIT), Minocpos 1.7 ms, Cove 0.6 ms to the first buffer. Britainpos and Cove looped. LoginLoop took 415.3 ms to its first buffer (open 5.2 ms), against about 121 ms in bench-000050/51. That is one cold run at login, where nothing in round 2 touches music, so I read it as noise, not a regression.

### Audio pack: Codex round 3 and dispositions (2026-10-31)

Codex (gpt-6-astra) audited 1cb398ccb read-only and found five issues: three P2 and two P3. All five are fixed in 7aefe30d2, each with a test in `AudioPackRound3Tests`.

| # | Finding | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **P2, cache admission ran before the limiter.** Both `AudioManager` paths called `GetSound` before `LimitPlaying`. Silent sounds played in the background could hold the whole 64 MiB cache budget, so an audible newcomer was refused by the cache, and the limiter, which would have stopped the silent sounds, never ran. | **Fixed.** `Sound.GetSoundToPlay` replaces `GetSound` in both paths. When the cache refuses an audible request, it first asks `SoundCache.CouldAdmit`, which uses the source's size from `TryGetSoundSource` and reads and evicts nothing. If stopping every silent playing sound would make room, it stops silent sounds oldest first, removing each from the list, until the id fits, then asks the cache again. If not, nothing is stopped. A silent request never stops anything. Test: a 1 MiB budget is full of two silent and two audible sounds. A silent request is refused and changes nothing. An audible 256 KiB request stops only the oldest silent sound and plays. A 512 KiB request, which the one remaining silent sound could not make room for, stops nothing. |
| 2 | **P2, verify opened the file a second time.** `LooseWithinCap` closed its checked handle, and then the frozen loader opened the path again with `File.ReadAllBytes`, so a file enlarged in between was read whole. | **Fixed.** The frozen loader's `ReadWave` now reads through one handle and checks that handle's length against the client's cap (`MaxWaveFileBytes`, repeated because the project does not reference Uo.Pack; a test compares the two) before allocating. The change is marked "Not verbatim". Its chunk parsing is unchanged. An enlarged file is refused, and the frozen `TryGetSound` falls back to the archive, as before. Test: a loose WAV passes the size check and then grows to 65 MiB + 1 before the frozen loader is asked. Verify gets the archive's sound, with under 8 MiB allocated. |
| 3 | **P2, a loose source that grew between probe and read was read before it was budgeted.** The first `Trim` evicted idle sounds for the probed size. The read then allocated the file's new size, and only the second `Trim` refused it. A pack record answering for an override that had become unreadable followed the same order. | **Fixed.** Admission is now decided from the size alone (`CanTrim`, which evicts nothing). The read is capped at the admitted size: `TryGetSound(id, maxPcmBytes, ..., out changed)` passes the cap to `ReadWaveFile`, which refuses from the header. A grown file is refused with `changed` set. Nothing beyond the cap is allocated, and the remembered size is refreshed so the next request is budgeted at the new size. The pack fallback's size comes from its table and is checked against the cap before it is read. `changed` is false for an invalid or absent sound. Idle sounds are evicted only after a successful read, so a refused request evicts nothing. The cost is that the new PCM, at most its admitted size, briefly sits beside the idle sounds that are about to be evicted. Test: a 2 MiB budget holds 1 MiB playing and 960 KiB idle. A loose WAV probes at 128 KiB and then grows in place to 384 KiB, with the same file length and write time. It is refused, with under 128 KiB allocated, no eviction and `Bytes` unchanged. The next request plays it at its real size and evicts the idle id. An override that becomes unreadable after its 64 KiB probe falls back to a 512 KiB pack record. That record is not read either (under 256 KiB allocated, no eviction), and the next request plays it. |
| 4 | **P3, a stale probe.** After a large loose WAV was probed and refused, its remembered size was used indefinitely, so a file that later shrank or disappeared stayed refused until a reload. | **Fixed.** The memo keeps the file's length and last-write time from when it was probed. `TryGetSoundSource` stats the file first (one `FileInfo`, only on a cache miss) and probes again when either differs. A vanished file is dropped, and the pack's record is named instead. A successful read clears the memo, since the id is now cached. Test: two 1.5 MiB loose files are refused under a 1 MiB budget. One is replaced by a 32 KiB file and then plays. The other is rewritten at the same length with a smaller data chunk and a new write time, and is probed again (32 KiB). Once deleted, it plays the pack's record. |
| 5 | **P3, NaN and extreme arguments (inherited).** `Sound.Play(volume: NaN)` or a NaN distance factor reached FNA's volume setter after the buffer was submitted, and threw. `PlaySoundWithDistance` threw `OverflowException` when a coordinate difference was `int.MinValue`. | **Fixed.** `Sound.Play` and `UOMusic.Play` refuse a non-finite volume or factor before anything else (logged, returns false): no instance is created, nothing is submitted, and the replay delay does not start. Both `AudioManager` paths check the same before asking for the sound. `AudioManager.Distance` computes coordinate differences in `long`. Test: four NaN and infinity combinations leave the sound without an FNA instance and with no replay delay. `UOMusic.Play(NaN)` returns false. `Distance(int.MinValue, ...)` is 2^31 and `Distance(int.MaxValue, ..., int.MinValue, ...)` is 2^32 - 1. |

**Memory and the trade-off** (the owner's rule): the loose-WAV memo grows from an int to an int, a long and a `DateTime` (20 bytes) per loose file probed; a stock install has no loose WAVs, so 0. A cache miss on a loose file costs one stat. Otherwise nothing new is held, and the budgets (64 MiB cache, 1,024 ids, 256 playing, 64 MiB playing) are unchanged.

**Pack bytes:** unchanged. The converter's output code did not change (only the frozen loader that verify uses), so the test pack was not rebuilt. `audio/sounds.bin` is still f41571ce... and `audio/music.bin` 8085e9e0.... `--verify-only --only sounds,music` on the test pack: sounds 1,656 ids EXACT, music 102 ids EXACT, all checks passed.

**Verification.** Client Release and `-p:CuoDevTools=false` builds: 0 errors. Uo.Converter: 0 errors. `dotnet test tests/ClassicUO.UnitTests -c Release`: 1,105 passed, 1 skipped (pre-existing), 0 failed (5 new). Client check: **bench-000053** (`listen-round3`) runs the bench-000052 plan on a Release JIT build of 7aefe30d2. It was queued when this was written; its result is still to be recorded.

## Milestone smoke on classic-1.2 (bench-000054)

End-to-end smoke check of the milestone tip, no code changes. NativeAOT win-x64 publish of 5c90523ca (code = 32ce99b5e), pack CURRENT = classic-1.2, account kbatman4. Three runs: `listen` (Gpu; brit, minoc, cove, walk) and `shots-gpu` / `shots-legacy` (brit, house, `[TestScene go`, large scene at zoom 1 and 2.5). Job ok in 410 s, all three runs `exit: 0`.

- **Errors:** none in any run (no exception, DllNotFound/EntryPointNotFound, `skipped`, incomplete pack). No loose audio or tiledata file opened (no tiledata.mul, sound.mul, soundLegacyMUL, Music\Digital); every run logs `Audio: pack, 1655 sound records, 90 music records` (0.24-0.30 ms) and `[load]` 39-42 ms.
- **Music (listen):** LoginLoop, then Britainpos (first buffer 6.7 ms, looped), Minocpos 1.2 ms, Cove 0.7 ms (looped), Britainpos 1.2 ms (looped); every open 0.2 ms.
- **LoginLoop first buffer:** 28.0 ms (listen), **379.2 ms** (shots-gpu), 25.8 ms (shots-legacy). Two of three are at or below the AOT loose-file figure (34.5 ms, bench-000043). The 379 ms sample is a one-off start-up stall, not the pack path: its open took 0.3 ms like the others, the binary, pack and plan were the same, and the line comes at the same point (right after `Connected!`, before the login burst). It is the only run where the log second ticks between `Connected!` and the first buffer. The figure runs from stream creation to the first buffer the main thread submits in `UOMusic.Update`, so it includes decode-worker scheduling and the main thread's frames during login; the log has no frame times before the world, so the two can't be told apart from this run.

The house-window counters match bench-000045's base run exactly: foliage 1, cap_statics 2, pick_tests 36.7, override_calls 28 (bench-000046: 0, 0, 24, 14); hidden_tiles 80 in both. ## Roof over the player after a teleport: max-Z decision latched before the chunk loads (2026-10-31, `poc/roof-race`)

Known issue "Gpu world renderer: the roof over the player is sometimes drawn" (bench-000045 base arm, bench-000054: 2 of 15 Gpu house shots at 1427,1691 drew the roof, the bottom-left building's chimneys and a tree for the whole window). Base 602354ecc, branch `poc/roof-race`, fix ff2628c74.

**How each renderer decides.** Both renderers use the same decision: `GameScene.UpdateMaxDrawZ` (`GameSceneDrawingSorting.cs:60` at 602354ecc), called from `GetViewPort` (`:1523`) at the start of `FillGameObjectList` (`GameScene.cs:628`), on the main thread, in the draw. It reads the statics on the player's tile and on the diagonal tile (x+1, y+1), only from loaded chunks (`GetChunk(.., load: false)`, `:83` and `:148`), and sets `_maxZ`, `_maxGroundZ` and `_noDrawRoofs`. Legacy's walk hides by them (ProcessAlpha, `obj.Z >= _maxZ`, roofs); the Gpu path passes them to the shader (`gpu.SetZHiding`, `GameSceneGpuWorld.cs`), rebuilds its skip masks when they change (`GpuPrepareBegin`), and its walk runs the same foliage test (`obj.Z < _maxZ && IsFoliage`, which is the `foliage` counter; `cap_statics` counts statics the walk captures for the Gpu pass, here the chimneys above the real max Z). Nothing is baked into a chunk mesh, nothing runs on a worker: the only cached state is the decision itself.

**Root cause** (`GameSceneDrawingSorting.cs:66-75` at 602354ecc): the decision is recomputed only when the player's x, y or z changes (or on a forced call: a house multi arriving, the DrawRoofs option). That was upstream's rule when every chunk loaded the moment it was first asked for. Since incremental chunk loading, the chunk under a teleported player is loaded by `Map.UpdateLoading` (`World.cs:337`, `Map.cs:309`) only once its regions are decoded (`Map.cs:551`) and its art is in the atlases (`Map.cs:559`, decoded on worker threads); until then the player is parked (`Map.Park`, `Map.cs:257`). If the arrival frame's draw comes before that, the decision reads no chunk, keeps max Z 127 and roofs drawn, and records the new position, so no later frame recomputes it until the player moves. Whether the chunk is in by the first draw depends on the region decode and the first-sight art workers, hence the intermittence. The Legacy path has the same race; it has simply not been seen there: only 3 Legacy house shots exist (bench-000045 and 000054), and in both jobs each Legacy run came right after a Gpu run of the same binary, with the OS file cache warm.

The window counters fit: drawn = `foliage 1` (the tree is below max Z 127, so the walk tests it) and `cap_statics 2` (the chimneys), against 0 and 0 when max Z is the roof's; Legacy's full walk also counts foliage 0.

**Fix** (`MaxDrawZLatch.cs`, `UpdateMaxDrawZ`): the decision also records whether both chunks it reads were loaded. A decision made with a chunk missing is not kept: it runs again next frame (two `GetChunk(.., false)` lookups while the chunk is missing; nothing at all once both are there), and the first complete one sticks until the position changes, as before. The cost does not scale with the view. At the map edge (the diagonal chunk outside the map) it recomputes every frame, which is two tile lists. Each recovery logs `[maxz] the player's chunks loaded N frame(s) after the position changed: max Z a -> b, roofs ...` (Trace). No memory held.

**Reproduction.** Deterministic: `MaxDrawZLatchTests.Teleport_Before_The_Chunk_Loads_Recomputes_Once_It_Is_There` replays the failing order (Britain with chunks loaded, a teleport whose first decision has the chunk missing, the chunk arriving later) and checks the decision runs again until a complete one; under the old rule (position only) the second `NeedsUpdate` was false. In the client: **bench-000055** (`job-roof.sh`): Gpu, NativeAOT, pack classic-1.2, 5 sessions per arm interleaved base (602354ecc code) / new (ff2628c74), each `brit -> house1 -> minoc -> house2`, so 10 house arrivals per arm (5 of them a session's first visit, the case that failed before). Each house window is classified drawn (foliage or cap_statics > 0) or hidden; the new arm's `[maxz]` lines show which arrivals needed the recompute.

**Result bench-000055** (ok, 690 s, all 10 runs exit 0): base 10/10 house windows hidden, new 10/10 hidden, so in this sample the race did not show on base (it was 2 of 15 before): the job shows no regression, not the fix. The `[maxz]` lines show where the race happens. Every new session logged three recoveries: at login (`max Z 127 -> 20, roofs hidden`, 2 frames after the position was set; the character logs in at the house, where the previous session ended), after the teleport to Britain (127 -> 127, 1 to 3 frames) and after the teleport to Minoc (127 -> 127, 5 to 12 frames). The house arrivals themselves logged none: the house chunks were still loaded from the login about 30 and 60 s earlier, so the first decision there was already complete. Base got lucky the same way: its login decision at the house kept the roof drawn, but the first measured window comes after the teleport to Britain, which moved the player and recomputed; at house1 and house2 the chunks were already in. So the race happens on every session start, and this plan never measured that moment. The round 2 job measures it (`house0`, the login spot, before the first teleport).

**Verification.** `dotnet test tests/ClassicUO.UnitTests -c Release`: 1,146 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed (4 new). One earlier full run failed `TileDataAuditTests.A_Multi_Component_Takes_The_Draw_Flags_Of_Its_Season_Graphic` once; it passed alone and in the re-run (no code of this branch near it; noted as possibly order-dependent). Builds: NativeAOT publish (dev flavour) and `-p:CuoDevTools=false` Release: 0 errors. No ECS write sites changed.

**Verification round 2** (7289d751f): `dotnet test tests/ClassicUO.UnitTests -c Release` twice: 1,150 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed both times (4 latch tests removed, 8 decision tests added; the season test did not flake, see "Flaky test found"). Builds: Release and `-p:CuoDevTools=false` Release 0 errors; NativeAOT publish 0 errors. No ECS write sites changed (write-site budget test passes unchanged).

### Codex audit and dispositions (2026-10-31, round 2: 7289d751f)

Codex (gpt-6-astra, read-only) audited ff2628c74: the arrival race is real and the patch fixes that sequence, but "both chunks loaded" is not the decision's whole input set. All findings fixed; findings 2-6 were pre-existing.

**Design.** `MaxDrawZState` (replaces `MaxDrawZLatch`) holds the decision, moved verbatim out of `UpdateMaxDrawZ` except for its chunk lookups. It is kept while all its inputs are unchanged: the player's x/y/z, `DrawRoofs`, the Map instance (`Map.Id`, unique per instance) and the content of the chunks it looked up (`Map.DecisionDirty`). Each decision records the box of chunks it looked up (`ChunkReach`), including the recursive roof search's and the ones it found not loaded. `Chunk.OnTileContentChanged` (every non-mobile object joining or leaving a tile list: placement, move, removal, Destroy, re-placement after a graphic change), a chunk load (`Map.LoadChunk`, also for an empty block) and a chunk destroy (`Chunk.Destroy`, eviction) note their chunk; one inside the box sets the dirty flag (four compares). The next `UpdateMaxDrawZ` (once per frame, in `GetViewPort`, before the draw) recomputes once however many changes came in. Nothing runs per frame beyond the key comparison: no retry while incomplete, no work that scales with the view. Memory: 6 ints and a bool per Map, one reference per Chunk; no pool or cache.

| # | Finding | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | P2: the recursive roof search (`Map.CalculateNearZ`) reads further chunks and silently stops at unloaded ones, so a completed decision can keep a too-high roof cutoff | Fixed. `CalculateNearZ` looks up through `Map.GetChunkForDecision`: an in-map chunk that is not loaded counts as missing, goes into the reach and is requested (sticky, so it loads even off screen); its load sets the dirty flag. Chose bump-on-load over retry-while-incomplete: zero per-frame cost, and no endless retry. Out of map is known empty. |
| 2 | P2: a facet change at the same x/y/z keeps the old facet's answer (`World.cs:233` replaces the Map) | Fixed. `Map.Id` is part of the validity. |
| 3 | P2: placed, removed or moved items and statics, house deletion (`HouseManager.cs:109`), local customisation (`HouseCustomizationManager.cs:551`, `:693`), and a player just outside a house whose diagonal tile is inside, don't recompute | Fixed at the central mutation point, not at the call sites: all of these go through `Chunk.AddGameObject` / `GameObject.RemoveFromTile` (`House.ClearComponents` -> `Multi.Destroy` -> `RemoveFromTile`; customisation `place.Destroy()` and `house.Add`; items are re-placed by `SetInWorldTile` after every graphic or position update), so `OnTileContentChanged` covers them, filtered by the decision's reach, whether or not the player is inside the house bounds. The forced calls (Item.cs:336, PacketHandlers) stay. |
| 4 | P2: `World.ChangeSeason` changes graphics (and so the tiledata flags read) in place | Fixed. `ChangeSeason` calls `Map.InvalidateDecision()` after the graphics swap. (Parked components take their season on load, through `AddGameObject`, so they are covered by 3.) |
| 5 | P2: the ToggleDrawRoofs macro (`MacroManager.cs:1767`) bypasses the forced update | Fixed. It calls `UpdateMaxDrawZ(true)` like the Options dialog; `DrawRoofs` is also part of the key, so any other path that changes it is covered. |
| 6 | P2: south edge: `GetChunk2` checked only the flattened index, so chunk (cx, BlocksY) aliased (cx + 1, 0) | Fixed in `GetChunk2` for every caller: both coordinates are checked (`IsInMap`), so out of map returns null, and a negative chunk coordinate no longer indexes outside the array. The Map keeps its size in chunks (`BlocksX`/`BlocksY`, read once at creation; MapLoader never changes it after load) instead of reading `MapBlocksSize` per lookup. Callers checked: `GetChunk`/`GetTile`/`GetMapZ` (null already handled; an object placed outside the map is no longer put into an aliased chunk), `BareWalk` (FrameStats; null skipped), `GetChunkForDraw`/`Park`/`UpdateLoading`/`TryLoadQueued` (already checked both), MiniMapGump (`GetChunk(int block)` after `TryGetBlock`, which checks both). |
| 7 | P3: the four latch tests feed `complete` by hand; none runs the decision | Replaced by `MaxDrawZDecisionTests` (8): `MaxDrawZState.Update`, the code `UpdateMaxDrawZ` runs, on a real `Map` (test-seam size, no map files) with real `Chunk`s filled through `AddGameObject`. Missing chunk -> roof loads -> recomputed once at the same position (and not recomputed while nothing changes); the audit's recursive example (roof at (7,7,30) continuing at (8,7,24) in a chunk that loads later: 30 -> 24); facet change at the same x/y/z; a house roof component placed on, then removed from, the diagonal tile of a player outside; changes outside the reach don't recompute; in-place graphic change recomputes after `InvalidateDecision` (what `ChangeSeason` calls); `DrawRoofs`; the south edge (no aliasing, `GetChunk2(0, 2, load: true)` creates nothing, out of map is complete and not queued, no retry). Not covered by a unit test: `ChangeSeason` itself (it plays music through `Client.Game`), and `GameScene` copying the result into its fields. |

**Known limit** (as first written; fixed in Codex round 2 below, finding 1). An evicted chunk in the reach makes the next decision incomplete for the frames until the sticky request reloads it. The eviction timeout is 3 s (`CLEAR_TEXTURES_DELAY`), not minutes, so an off-screen roof chain would cycle.

**Trace line** (kept for comparison with bench-000055): `[maxz] the chunks the decision reads loaded N ms after it first ran without them: max Z a -> b, roofs hidden|drawn`, once per incomplete-then-complete transition (milliseconds now, since recomputes are no longer per frame).

**Flaky test found.** `TileDataAuditTests.A_Multi_Component_Takes_The_Draw_Flags_Of_Its_Season_Graphic` depends on test order on a fresh test output folder: `SeasonManager`'s static constructor writes the default `Data/Client/seasons.txt` under the test binary folder but does not create the directory (`SeasonManager.CreateDefaultSeasonsFile`), so it throws `TypeInitializationException` (`DirectoryNotFoundException`) unless a test that builds `containers.txt` (`ContainerManager.BuildContainerFile` creates the folder) ran first. Reproduced: deleting `tests/ClassicUO.UnitTests/bin/Release/net10.0/Data` and running the test alone fails; the previous agent's first run on a new worktree fails the same way (its `containers.txt` is 74 s older than `seasons.txt`). Not this branch's code; not fixed (fix: `Directory.CreateDirectory` in `CreateDefaultSeasonsFile`, or the test creating the folder).

**Client check round 2: bench-000056** (`job-roof2.sh`, queued): Gpu, NativeAOT, pack CURRENT, 5 sessions per arm interleaved base (602354ecc code) / new2 (7289d751f), plan `house0 -> brit -> house1 -> minoc -> house2` (house0 is the login spot, measured before the first teleport: the moment bench-000055 showed the race on every session; house2 is the revisit), plus one Legacy session of new2. Expect base drawn at house0 in most sessions (the login answer kept until the first move), new2 hidden in all 15 house windows with one `[maxz] ... 127 -> 20, roofs hidden` per session.

Result (ok, 932.8 s; `~/.claude/rf-agent/jobs/bench/done/bench-000056/summary.txt`):
- **base house0 (login spot, before any teleport): drawn in 5 of 5 sessions**, with the counters of the bad shots in bench-000045/54 (foliage 1, cap_statics 2, pick_tests 36-38, override_calls 28). The login race is deterministic on base; the earlier "2 of 15" were the shots that happened to measure a session's first decision.
- base house1 and house2 (after teleports): hidden 10 of 10.
- **new2: hidden in all 15 Gpu house windows**, house0 included.
- Legacy new2: hidden in 3 of 3 windows (its FRAMESTATS lacks some counters); its `[maxz]` line: "loaded 77 ms after it first ran without them: max Z 127 -> 20, roofs hidden".
- 0 errors, 0 exceptions.

The round-2 fixes below change only the decision's dependencies (pinning, request survival, sync mode, the graphic notify), not this path, so bench-000056 still covers the arrival race; no new job.

### Codex round 2 (audit of 7289d751f) and dispositions

Codex (gpt-6-astra, read-only) found the round-1 fixes 1 and 3 incomplete on four paths. All fixed, each with a test (`MaxDrawZDecisionTests`, now 13).

| # | Finding | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | P2: off-screen dependencies cycle: a roof chain's chunk outside the draw walk gets no access-time refresh, is evicted after 3 s, which dirties the decision; the recompute requests it again (a load, a mesh build and a cutoff change every ~3-3.5 s while standing still) | Fixed. `Map.ClearUnusedBlocks` keeps a chunk in the current decision's reach (`Map.InDecisionReach`); a new decision replaces the box, which releases the old one's chunks to the normal sweep. Bounded: a reach wider or taller than `MaxPinnedReach` (8 chunks, 64 tiles; a house roof spans 2-3) pins nothing and ages out as before (it still invalidates). Memory: none new (the box is the existing 4 ints); at most 64 chunks held, in practice the 1-4 the decision read. Tests: a dependency outside the view with an expired access time survives the sweep while the decision stands (no recompute), and is evicted by the sweep after the player moves 40 tiles away (without dirtying the new decision); a large reach is not pinned. |
| 2 | P2: parked-object cleanup (`TryLoadQueued`) drops the shared request when the chunk's parked mobiles left before it loaded, cancelling a decision dependency for good | Fixed. The cleanup (`Map.DropStaleParked`) still forgets the stale parked objects, but drops the request only when the chunk is outside the decision's reach; otherwise the load goes ahead. Test: a decision request on a chunk whose parked mobile leaves before the load stays queued; a parked-only chunk outside the reach is still dropped. |
| 3 | P2: `CUO_CHUNK_SYNC=1`: the decision looked up with `load: false` and requested only when incremental, so a missing off-screen dependency was never loaded | Fixed: `GetChunkForDecision` passes `load: !Incremental` (sync mode loads it on the spot, as every chunk did before incremental loading). Test coverage: the mode is a `static readonly` read from the environment at type init, so one test process cannot switch it, and a missing chunk cannot load in the tests (no map files). The unit tests run incremental mode; the sync branch is the one-argument change, covered by review. The parked test returns early under `CUO_CHUNK_SYNC=1` (nothing is parked there). |
| 4 | P2: `0xBF/0x1B` (spellbook content) sets a ground item's `Graphic` in place with no tile-list change, so the decision misses a roof/exclusion flag change | Fixed centrally in the `GameObject.Graphic` setter: a changed value on a placed non-mobile (`TileChunk != null`) notes its chunk (`OwnerMap.NoteContentChanged`: four compares against the reach, nothing outside it). That covers every in-place graphic change of a placed object: the spellbook packet, `Static.SetGraphic`/`RestoreOriginalGraphic`, the season swaps (`Static`/`Multi`/`Land.UpdateGraphicBySeason`, also invalidated by `ChangeSeason`), and the DevBench chair command. Other `Graphic =` writes on items (`WorldWriter` 349/355/569, `PacketHandlers` 1743/1935/3025) are followed by re-placement or touch unplaced or contained items; covered either way. Mobiles are skipped (not an input). Write-site budget: the setter is no longer the scanner's one-line form, so its `_graphic` write counts as direct: allowlist regenerated, one pair added (`GameObject.cs|_graphic|1`, the setter's own write after its `FunnelCheck.Write`); no other change. Test: an item on the diagonal tile changing graphic Plain -> Roof dirties and recomputes (hidden); an unchanged value and a mobile's body change don't. |
| tests | the facet test started with `DecisionDirty=true`, so it did not prove the `Map.Id` check alone | The new Map's reach is set (empty) first, so `DecisionDirty` is false and only `Map.Id` triggers the recompute. The season test is now `InvalidateDecision_Recomputes` (the graphic part moved into finding 4's test). |

Verification: `dotnet test tests/ClassicUO.UnitTests -c Release` 1154 passed, 2 skipped; client builds Release and Release `-p:CuoDevTools=false` 0 errors.

## tiledata: standardized counts, legacy statics padded (2026-10-31, `poc/tiledata-pad`)

Owner decision: the pack's tiledata is a standardized format. Every pack has exactly 0x4000 land and 0x10000 static entries, whatever the source install, so a server-sent u16 graphic always indexes inside `TileData.StaticData`. This replaces guarding the ~35 unchecked client sites listed under "StaticData bounds" in the legacy-import entry. Base 203428eab.

**Changes.**
- `PackConst.LandTileCount` (0x4000) and the new `PackConst.StaticTileCount` (0x10000) are the one place the counts live; `TileDataFile.MaxStatics` is gone.
- Converter (`TableConvert.TileData`): `PadSource` pads the source land/static arrays with default (empty) entries up to the counts before the names, fields and `TileRules` are applied, so a padded entry gets exactly the `packFlags` a modern install's genuinely empty entry gets (0, except the ids the rules name: 0xA1FE-0xA201 and 0x63D3 `NoDraw`; 0x9E4C/0x9E64/0x9E65/0x9E7D drawn since they have neither Background nor Surface). Before, `TileRules.Static` gave an id past the source `NoDraw`, but such an id had no entry in the file at all. A source with more entries than the format holds throws ("Refusing to truncate"). Checked installs under `D:/Ultima Online Installations` and `C:/Ultima Online Classic`: UOAOS, UOLBR, UOML, UOML Felladrin, UOSE have 0x4000 statics (1,036,288 B, old layout); 7.0.15.1, Classic, Classic - New Legacy have exactly 0x10000 (3,188,736 B); Enhanced has no tiledata.mul. None has more.
- Writer and reader: `TileDataFile.Write` throws `ArgumentException` for other counts; `TileDataFile.Read` rejects `staticCount` != 0x10000 as malformed (`InvalidDataException`, like its other untrusted-pack checks; it was 1..0x10000). A legacy pack converted before this change (0x4000 statics) no longer loads: re-run `--only tiledata`.
- Verify compares the pack against the source padded the same way, so every padded entry must be all zero (fields, name) and its draw flags must match the rules and the verbatim oracle; the summary says how many entries are padded.
- Client: `CombatBookGump` skipped ability items whose id was past `StaticData.Length`; with padding those ids are in range with an empty name, so it now also skips an empty name (otherwise a legacy pack would show blank rows for out-of-era weapons). `AnimatedStaticsManager` loops over `StaticData.Length`: padded entries have no `Animation` flag, so it registers the same set (at first by inspection only: `LegacyPackLoadTests` did not run the manager; a test now does, see "Codex audit fixes" below). The other `Length` loops (`GpuWorldRenderer.BuildNoCotTable`, `TargetManager`, `FirstSightArt`) are bounds checks that now always pass or tables a 7.x pack already sizes this way. No client run: the only client change is that gump guard.

**Memory** (legacy packs only; 7.x packs already have 0x10000): `tiledata.bin` grows by 49,152 × 32 B = 1.5 MB (UOML: 2,451,634 B). Per client: `StaticTiles[]` grows by 49,152 entries (~40 B each, ~1.9 MB) plus the renderer's compact copy (12 B each, 0.6 MB): about 2.5 MB per legacy client, the same as a 7.x client. Benefit: no out-of-range index from a server graphic at any site.

**Verification.**
- Modern output unchanged: `Uo.Converter --uo "C:/Ultima Online Classic" --only tiledata` (7.0.103.0, the source named in classic-1.2's manifest) into scratch: `tiledata.bin` 2,503,351 B, sha256 995bc805...bed6, `cmp` identical to `uo-packs/classic-1.2/tiledata.bin` and to its manifest hash.
- UOML (4.0.11c): `--only tiledata`: "16384 land, 65536 statics (16384 from the source, 49152 padded empty)"; verify: oracle 212,992 decisions, 0 mismatches, every field and name EXACT. Full conversion (23 s) then `--verify-only`: all checks passed (tiledata, atlases, maps block-exact as before; NoDraw statics 23).
- Tests: `tests/Uo.Converter.Tests` 35 passed, 1 skipped (new: padded legacy entries are byte-identical to a 7.0.9 source's empty entries from 0x4000 up; a 0x10020-static source is refused and no file is written; the old/new layout theory asserts 0x10000 and empty padding). `tests/ClassicUO.UnitTests` 1154 passed, 2 skipped in both `CuoDevTools` variants (reader rejects 0x4000, 0xFFFF, 0x10001 and 16 statics; writer refuses wrong counts); with `CUO_LEGACY_PACK`/`CUO_LEGACY_UO` set to the UOML pack: 1155 passed, 1 skipped (`LegacyPackLoadTests` now expects 0x10000 statics, empty padding). Builds: ClassicUO.sln Release and `-p:CuoDevTools=false` 0 errors; Uo.Client, Uo.Render.App, Uo.Converter.Tests 0 errors.

### Tiledata standardized counts: Codex audit fixes (2026-10-31, `poc/tiledata-pad`)

Codex audit of 42e84f4a6 (three findings). Base 42e84f4a6.

1. **P2, `PlayerMobile.UpdateAbilities` indexed `StaticData[Graphic + 1]`**, which is 0x10000 for a weapon with graphic 0xFFFF whose previous entry has a different `AnimID` (possible on a modern or custom pack; padded legacy tails have `AnimID` 0 on both). Fixed: the neighbour lookup moved to `PlayerMobile.FindAnimNeighbour(statics, graphic, animId)`, which bounds-checks both neighbours and otherwise behaves as before (previous entry first, then next, else 0). New `AbilityNeighbourTests` (5): 0xFFFF with differing tail `AnimID`s returns 0 without throwing; 0xFFFF still matches 0xFFFE; previous wins over next; next when previous differs; graphic 0. Other `+/- 1` neighbour indexing into `StaticData`/`LandData`: none found (grep over `src` and `poc`; `Item.DisplayedGraphic`'s coin `+1/+2` is an art id cast to `ushort`, the other `+ 1` sites are gump ids).
2. **P2, empty entries (no art, zero flags) still count for the roof cut-off and light occlusion.** Deferred by the coordinator: not a regression (modern packs' empty entries behave the same; legacy ids used to throw). Recorded in known-issues.md ("Empty tiledata entries still occlude roofs and lights") with the proposed fix and the parity check it needs.
3. **P3, the claim that `LegacyPackLoadTests` checks `AnimatedStaticsManager` registration was wrong** (`UOFileManager.Load` does not run it). Fixed with a test: `AnimatedStaticsManager.Initialize` now delegates to an internal `Initialize(StaticTiles[], AnimDataLoader)` (same loop), and `LegacyPackLoadTests` runs it on the loaded UOML pack and asserts the registered ids are non-empty, all below 0x4000, and equal to the set the unpadded 0x4000 entries register. The earlier entry's wording is corrected.

No client run: the only behaviour change is the 0xFFFF bounds check. No memory change.

**Verification.** ClassicUO.sln Release and `-p:CuoDevTools=false`: 0 errors. `tests/ClassicUO.UnitTests`: with `CUO_LEGACY_PACK` (the padded UOML pack in the tiledata-pad scratch) and `CUO_LEGACY_UO` (`D:/Ultima Online Installations/UOML`): 1160 passed, 1 skipped (the legacy test ran and passed); `-p:CuoDevTools=false` without the legacy variables: 1159 passed, 2 skipped. `tests/Uo.Converter.Tests` with `CUO_LEGACY_UO`: 36 passed. Write-site budget unchanged.

## T1 funnel, part 2: the bulk clear and 0x27's other deny branches (2026-10-31, `bg/ecs-t1-funnel-2`)

Base `poc/modern-client` 55e115570 (T1 round 3 + containers merged in 2e0659dc9; E4 `world_update_mobile_system` on by default). Commits 48d2b3ff1 (scanner), c253631b7 (clear), c34cc1d14 (deny). Plan: ecs-transition-plan.md, T1. Same operation pattern as slice 1 (admission → resolve → compute → ECS commit → cache from the values → derived helpers → links).

- **Codex round-5 scanner gaps (test code only), fixed in 48d2b3ff1.** (1) Conditional compilation: `UnguardedFallbackUses` parses `WorldWriter.cs` with no symbols and with `CUO_DEVTOOLS` (the two build variants), so a fallback call under `#if CUO_DEVTOOLS` or under its `#else` is judged in the parse that enables it; a fallback named in text both parses disable (another symbol) is a use. (2) The walk queue: a checked method's second statement must be exactly one queue mutator (`AddToBack`, `RemoveFromFront`, `Clear`, or an indexer assignment) whose receiver is the bare `_walkSteps` token (not `target._walkSteps`), naming `_walkSteps` once and with no lambda, so neither another mobile's queue nor an alias or callback argument passes. (3) Jumps: "a `Reject` before the call" was textual order, so an operation body with any `goto` or label now has no guarded fallback call at all. Fixtures: `A_Fallback_Use_Under_Conditional_Compilation_Or_A_Jump_Is_Found` (Codex's `#if` and `goto skip` shapes, a `#else` call, another symbol, a guarded call under `#if CUO_DEVTOOLS` that still counts) and five new lines in `The_Walk_Queue_Changes_Only_Through_The_Checked_Methods` (another mobile's queue, `Keep(_walkSteps)`, `_walkSteps.ForEach(Keep)`, `_walkSteps[i] = _walkSteps[0]`, `_saved = _walkSteps`). No real code changed; budget unchanged.
- **`WorldWriter.ClearContainer(containerSerial, keepEquipped)` (c253631b7).** `ClearContainerAndRemoveItems` (0x3C's clear before its first item, and 0x24 OpenContainer of a non-corpse) moves into the writer as a removal operation: admission, then the container by serial (`World.Get`; null or empty: nothing), the removed children's outstanding placements cancelled, one scope whose subject is the container and which owns every removed child's subtree for `CUO_FUNNEL_CHECK`; then the old loop unchanged (each removal through `World.RemoveItem`, a corpse's equipment kept in its child-list order, the head set to the first kept item). It writes no value of its own: the removals' Syncs and `Destroy` run unfolded as in `RemoveWorldItem`, so the active-items order is unchanged. The old helper wrote links only, so the budget is unchanged; what changes is the funnel check: the `Container` writes at `World.RemoveItemFromContainer` from this caller are funnel writes now. The handler helper is deleted (0x3C passes the serial it already resolved; 0x24 passes the item's serial). No release fallback: taking a serial, the operation has no foreign-instance violation, and a nesting is rejected like the others.
- **`WorldWriter.ReturnHeldItem` (c34cc1d14): 0x27's other deny branches.** The held item that does not go back through `PlaceInContainer` (it has a Layer, or its container is not valid): admission, then the item (`GetOrCreateItem`, its creation Sync skipped) and the container (`World.Get`) in the old order; the outcome is decided before any write (`HeldItemReturn.Paperdoll` for a mobile, `Removed` for another item, `Terrain` for none). Values: graphic, the hue as given (the old branch did not FixHue), amount, flags, layer, x/y/z, the old direction and IsMulti, and a corpse's state from the old direction (`Item.CorpseState`, as `CheckGraphicChange` computed it after the graphic write). Commit 1 is the detached state (Container 0xFFFFFFFF: the old `RemoveItemFromContainer`/`RemoveItem` Sync ran in every branch); then the cache in the old order; `RefreshGraphicState` where `CheckGraphicChange` ran; then the links: paperdoll = unlink, `PushToBack`, commit 2 with the wearer, then the cache's Container (the old path's second Sync: the item moves to the end of the mirror's equipment index, as before); removed = `World.RemoveItem` (owns the subtree; the corpse queueing happened at commit 1, where the old removal's Sync did it); terrain = unlink, Container written when it changed, `SetInWorldTile` (its Sync folded). The handler keeps the console lines and the paperdoll refresh. No release fallback (no violation other than nesting). Budget 306 → 297: `PacketHandlers.cs` Amount 4 → 3, Container 6 → 5, Flags 10 → 9, Graphic 11 → 10, Hue 1 → 0, Layer 4 → 3, X/Y/Z 4 → 3. `FunnelOperations` gains `ClearContainer` and `ReturnHeldItem` (pinned in `Only_The_Funnel_Operations_Are_Exempt`).
- **Tests** (old-vs-new on two Worlds as before): `ClearContainer_Equals_The_Old_Path` (5 starts × the bag, the wearer, a corpse holding equipment around a plain item, ITEM, an unknown serial × keep or clear: 50 cases; the kept children in order, both Worlds equal), `ClearContainer_Cancels_The_Removed_Items_Placements`, `ClearContainer_Inside_An_Operation_Is_Rejected` (throw and release); `ReturnHeldItem_Equals_The_Old_Path` (5 starts × 6 held packets: wearer, a bag (removed), ground, a gone container, a corpse graphic to the ground and onto the wearer; each followed by a resend; the outcome, destruction, mirror records, entity ids, indexes, active items), `ReturnHeldItem_Computes_Its_Values_Before_The_Writes` (each commit sees the getters on the previous values, the detached commit then the wearer), `ReturnHeldItem_Inside_An_Operation_Is_Rejected`, `The_Clear_And_Deny_Operations_Make_No_Direct_Writes` (funnel check: the clear, all three deny branches). 1245 pass, 2 skipped, in both `CuoDevTools` variants (base 1159 + 86); both client builds 0 errors.
- **Not converted here (next):** equipment (0x2E, and the equipment parts of 0x78/0x1D), mobiles (0x20, 0x77, 0x78, 0xD3), status and hits, animation, misc. No E2 bench rows for the two new operations: the clear's per-item cost is the old removal plus one scope, and 0x27 is a UI-rate packet; the bench job re-runs the existing funnel rows paired with base.
- **Gates (jobs on c34cc1d14):** `bench-000059` (client gate: `ls_parity` with `CUO_ECS_PARITY=1`, `CUO_FUNNEL_CHECK=1` over `ls_parity`, `w5items`, `w5push`, `-ecscheck 120`, defaults) and `bench-000060` (E2 bench, base 55e115570 and new interleaved, 3 runs each, TC=0). Client gate (`bench-000059`, pack classic-1.2): `ls_parity` with `CUO_ECS_PARITY=1`: `[ECS] check` mismatches 0; items 1,318,307 checked, 0 mismatched, 0 drawn- or lights-mismatched; mobiles 10,466,533 checked, 0 mismatched, 0 not mirrored. `CUO_FUNNEL_CHECK=1`: `[ECS] check` mismatches 0 on all three; no `WorldWriter` line and no pre-T1 line in any log. Direct writes (last 5-s line): ls_parity 4,189,758 (117 sites), w5items 814,871 (89), w5push 334,275 (93); still dominated by the unconverted mobile paths (animation, steps: w5push OffsetX/Y/Z 97,494 each). Sites by caller over the three runs: `Mobile.ProcessSteps` 31, `CharacterStatus` 30, `UpdateObject` 28, `UpdateGameObject` 25 (all in its mobile branch, PacketHandlers.cs 6351–6395), `SetAnimation` 15, then 12 or fewer each; `EquipItem` 4 (the next group). No site from `ClearContainer`, `ReturnHeldItem`, `DenyMoveItem`, `OpenContainer`, `UpdateContainedItems`, `UpdateGameObject`'s item branch, `DeleteObject` or `AddItemToContainer`; `Container` at `World.RemoveItemFromContainer` and `World.RemoveItem` (1 site each, the stack walk does not name their caller) come from the unconverted removers (equipment, 0x78, the range sweep). E2 bench (`bench-000060`: `EcsPacketCostBench`, base 55e115570 and new c34cc1d14 interleaved, 3 runs each, `DOTNET_TieredCompilation=0`, dev builds; median µs/packet at 500 / 2000 / 8000 mobiles, new): gate (each funnel row ≤ its paired old-path row + 0.1 µs, same bytes) **passes**. 0x1A new ground item: old path 0.157 / 0.159 / 0.175, funnel 0.128 / 0.135 / 0.140; 0x1A update: old 0.111 / 0.111 / 0.109, funnel 0.111 / 0.111 / 0.107; 0x25 new item into the backpack: old 0.227 / 0.250 / 0.246, funnel 0.135 / 0.146 / 0.132; 0x25 update: old 0.076 / 0.074 / 0.074, funnel 0.082 / 0.084 / 0.083 (+0.006 to +0.010, as in round 3). Bytes equal (140 / 0 / 236). Base vs new on the same rows (this branch changes none of these paths): within ±0.01 except single noisy rows (8000 mobile graphic change 0.061 → 0.071, new spread 0.013; 8000 ground item add 0.170 → 0.180, spreads 0.006; 8000 mirror-only UpsertMobile 0.121 → 0.101, spread 0.022). Spreads (max − min over 3 runs) mostly ≤ 0.01; outliers to 0.068 (base serial reuse at 8000).
