- **Codex audit of 55e115570..e1e825d8d (gpt-6-astra, read-only; 2 P2, 3 P3; all fixed in ef82c9c13).** Dispositions:
  1. *P2, 0x24 cleared a different object.* `OpenContainer` found its item with `World.Items.Get`, but `ClearContainer` looked it up again with `World.Get`, which prefers a mobile; with an item under a live mobile's serial (the unconverted `EquipItem` path can make one) the new handler removed the mobile's equipment. Fixed: `ClearContainer(serial, keepEquipped, itemOnly)`; 0x24 passes `itemOnly: true` (`World.Items.Get`, the old lookup), 0x3C `itemOnly: false` (`World.Get`, unchanged). Fixture `ClearContainer_Of_0x24_Clears_The_Item_Under_A_Mobiles_Serial`: the old 0x24 lookup (`OldClear(world.Items.Get(MOB))`) vs the new call on two Worlds; the item's contents go, the mobile keeps its equipment; the same fixture through `World.Get` removes the mobile's equipment (so it tells the lookups apart).
  2. *P2 (T1/T4 invariant), the deny removal reread `item.Container`.* After the detached commit, `World.RemoveItem` → `RemoveItemFromContainer` read the Container again; with T4's ECS-backed getter that is the committed 0xFFFFFFFF, and the old parent's unlink and gump refresh would be skipped. Fixed: the removal branch unlinks from the captured `oldContainer`, writes the detached Container from `v`, then `World.RemoveDetachedItem` (new, internal: the contents, OPL, Destroy; `World.RemoveItem` now calls the same tail). Same behaviour with today's getters (the 60 old-vs-new cases still match). Test `ReturnHeldItem_Removal_Unlinks_From_The_Captured_Parent`: the commit observer sets the cache's Container to the committed value (what T4's getter returns); the item still leaves BAG's child list with its contents. It fails with the old branch (checked by reverting the branch).
  3. *P3, removed descendants kept their placement tokens.* Fixed: `CancelSubtreePlacements` (the item and all its contents, walked before the removal; nothing to walk when no placement is outstanding) in every removal: the clear's removed children, the deny removal, and also 0x1D (`RemoveWorldItem`), the 0x25 replacement (`RemoveForReplacement`) and `RemovePreT1`. The kept corpse equipment and its contents, and a re-equipped or grounded held item's contents, keep theirs. Tests: `ClearContainer_Cancels_The_Removed_Items_Placements` (child, grandchild, great-grandchild), `ClearContainer_Keeps_The_Kept_Equipments_Placements` (two levels under kept equipment stay and are consumed; two levels under the removed plain item are rejected), `ReturnHeldItem_Removal_Cancels_The_Subtrees_Placements` (removal cancels two levels; paperdoll keeps them). In practice a token is consumed by the same handler right after its callbacks, and an upserted item is on the ground (no parent), so no runtime path is known to reach this; it is the token invariant.
  4. *P3, scanner: a guard under another symbol.* Both parses leave `DEBUG` undefined, so `#if !DEBUG` around the `Reject` looked like a guard while a Debug build runs the fallback unguarded. Fixed conservatively: an operation whose body has an `#if`/`#elif` naming any symbol other than `CUO_DEVTOOLS` has no guarded call at all. Fixture `A_Guard_That_Depends_On_An_Unexamined_Symbol_Is_No_Guard` (`#if !DEBUG` removes the Reject; an `#elif TRACE`; a `CUO_DEVTOOLS`-only body still guarded). The round-5 fixture's line 11 (a guarded call in a method that also has `#if SOMETHING_ELSE`) is now a use. The real `WorldWriter.cs` uses only `CUO_DEVTOOLS`.
  5. *P3, two tests could pass without checking.* `ClearContainer_Inside_An_Operation_Is_Rejected` now invokes the nested clear inside the observer in both modes (`Throw<InvalidOperationException>()` / the release call) and asserts there that nothing was removed, plus one violation and the observer ran. `The_Clear_And_Deny_Operations_Make_No_Direct_Writes` asserts the outcome and `FunnelCheck.Total == 0` right after the paperdoll and the terrain branch, before the fixture setup and its Reset. Also from the audit's notes: `ReturnHeldItem_Equals_The_Old_Path` gains a crowded wearer (equipment before and after ITEM in the child list and the equipment index): 30 more cases, and a paperdoll return asserts the siblings' order with ITEM at the end.
- **Release-path nesting is not harmless recovery** (audit note, recorded). If an operation were nested in a release build: 0x24 keeps the gump it already created and opened but skips the clear; a nested 0x3C clear is rejected and its later placements are rejected while the outer scope is open; a nested 0x27 return gets `None` and the handler still clears `ItemHold`. No production nesting entry exists (the operations run only from `ParsePackets`; plugin-injected packets are queued), as in round 4, so the rejection policy stays; a nesting stays a bug that `CUO_DEVTOOLS` builds throw on.
- **Open question decided (coordinator):** keep the paperdoll double commit for now; T3 replaces it with an explicit equipment-order stamp (noted in the plan's T3 section).
- **Also from the audit:** of the 86 tests, 80 are two-world comparisons (50 clear, 30 return) of copied old paths with today's shared helpers; they do not exercise packet dispatch, the UI, ItemHold, maps or multis, and a "resend" calls the writer again (a real repeated 0x27 meets a cleared hold). The client gate bench-000059 covers dispatch.
- **Verification (ef82c9c13):** 1280 pass + 2 skipped in both `CuoDevTools` variants (1245 + 35: 30 crowded return cases, 5 new facts); client build 0 errors. Write-site budget unchanged (297; the new Container write is in the operation). Each new WorldWriter test was checked against the old code (lookup, branch and token cancellation reverted one at a time): each fails there. No client job: the runtime changes are the 0x24 lookup (differs only on a serial collision), the removal's unlink source (the same parent with today's getters) and token cancellation (no known runtime path holds a descendant's token), so bench-000059's gate still covers them.

## T1 funnel, part 3: equipment (2026-10-31, `bg/ecs-t1-funnel-3`)

Base `poc/modern-client` bc9b71f48 (funnel part 2 merged). Commits 29fd1c6d1 (operations, handlers, budget), 528c136ee (tests, E2 rows). Plan: ecs-transition-plan.md, T1. Same operation pattern (admission → resolve with the old lookups → compute → ECS commits → cache from the values → derived helpers → links); the audit rules of parts 1–2 applied from the start.

- **`WorldWriter.Equip` (0x2E).** The item by `World.GetOrCreateItem` (the items only, as before: a mobile-valued serial creates an item), the wearer by `World.Get` (a mobile first; resolved before the writes, which change neither dictionary). An item with a graphic that is not a backpack leaves its old container, and the old path's Sync of that detached state is kept as a commit: it is what moves a re-equipped item to the end of the mirror's equipment index (a single final commit would leave it in place; `Equip_Re_Equips_At_The_End_Of_The_Equipment_Index`). Then graphic, layer, container, FixHue, amount 1, `PushToBack`. No `CheckGraphicChange` (the old handler ran none). The handler takes the gumps' container (`shownContainer`: the old Container when the item did not leave it, else none), the layer and the container from the packet, not read back from the item.
- **`WorldWriter.ClearWornItems` (0x78/0xD3, before the list).** The removal of every child that is neither opened nor the backpack, by serial as before; owns the removed subtrees for `CUO_FUNNEL_CHECK`, cancels their placements at any depth (the kept children's contents keep theirs).
- **`WorldWriter.WearItem` (0x78/0xD3, one entry).** The owner is the handler's `obj` instance, captured once before the list (since f7134d59b; it was looked up again per entry, see the audit below), the item by `GetOrCreateItem`. Commit 1 is the old `RemoveItemFromContainer` Sync (the entry's graphic, FixHue'd hue and amount 1 with the old layer, detached); commit 2 the owner, the entry's layer, or a corpse graphic's state from the old direction (`Item.CorpseState`). The old path's extra Sync from `CheckGraphicChange`'s Direction write (running bit) is not reproduced: by then the item was already re-added at the end of the equipment index and the final commit overwrites every value of it, so no production reader sees the difference (`-ecscheck` observes completed state). It is not invisible to tests: `WorldEcs.ItemMirrorWrites` counts one mirror write fewer per such entry; the old-vs-new tests do not compare that counter. The graphic is written before the unlink (a placed item's tile notes the change, as before); then `RefreshGraphicState`, `PushToBack`.
- **0x1D:** an equipped item's deletion already goes through `RemoveWorldItem` (slice 1); the wearer's removal (`World.RemoveMobile` with its equipment) belongs to the mobiles group.
- **No release fallback:** the three take serials, so nesting is their only violation (rejected; throws in CUO_DEVTOOLS builds).
- **Budget** −8 (allowlist sum 298 → 290): `PacketHandlers.cs` Amount 3 → 1, Container 5 → 3, Graphic 10 → 8, Layer 3 → 1. `FunnelOperations` gains `Equip`, `ClearWornItems`, `WearItem` (pinned in `Only_The_Funnel_Operations_Are_Exempt`).
- **Tests** (old-vs-new on two Worlds; copies `OldEquip`, `OldWear`): `Equip_Equals_The_Old_Path` (5 starts × 7 packets × crowded wearer × ITEM with the backpack layer = 140 cases, each followed by a resend and the next packet; the packets cover the wearer, a backpack layer, an item container, an unknown wearer, a corpse graphic, a new item, a mobile's serial), `WearItem_Equals_The_Old_Path` (5 starts × owner MOB/BAG/unknown × 6 lists × crowded = 180 cases, each resent; lists: an entry, a re-listed equipped item + a corpse graphic with the running bit + a new item, the same item twice, the kept opened container and backpack re-listed, the clear alone, a mobile's serial), `Equip_Re_Equips_At_The_End_Of_The_Equipment_Index`, `Equip_Computes_Its_Values_Before_The_Writes`, `WearItem_Computes_Its_Values_Before_The_Writes`, `ClearWornItems_Cancels_The_Removed_Items_Placements`, `Equip_And_WearItem_Supersede_The_Items_Placement`, `The_Equipment_Operations_Inside_An_Operation_Are_Rejected` (throw and release, asserted inside the outer operation), `The_Equipment_Operations_Make_No_Direct_Writes`. 1607 pass + 2 skipped in both `CuoDevTools` variants (base 1280 + 327); both client builds 0 errors.
- **Each new test fails on a broken version** (corrected after the audit: the saved log of 528c136ee had two passing mutations, and the replacement runs were missing from it). Re-run on f7134d59b with one filter (`Equip|Wear|Worn|Equipment`, 421 tests) and the whole set in one log (`mut_equip3.log` in the queue's scratch): 20 mutations of `WorldWriter.cs`, one at a time, **each fails at least one test**: no detached commit (Equip, WearItem), always unlink, the wearer among the items only, a mobile serial rejected, commit after the cache writes, no supersede (Equip, WearItem), no admission (all three), the corpse state without the running bit, the detached state with the entry layer, the owner looked up again per entry (the audited version), the owner among the mobiles only, no owner validation, the owner validated through `World.Get`, the clear also removing opened containers, no placement cancel (fails `ClearWornItems_Cancels_The_Removed_Items_Placements`; it passed in the first log only because that filter left the test out), no subtree ownership. The proposed `World.Get(serial) as Item ?? GetOrCreateItem` is equivalent to the old lookup for every reachable state and is not in the set.
- **Not converted (next):** mobiles (0x20, 0x77, 0x78/0xD3's mobile part through `UpdateGameObject`'s mobile branch, the 0x1D wearer removal), status and hits, animation, misc. See the handoff `handoffs/t1-funnel-3.md` for the design notes.
- **Gates (jobs on 528c136ee):** `bench-000061` (client gate, pack classic-1.2: `ls_parity` with `CUO_ECS_PARITY=1` and `-ecscheck 120`, then `CUO_FUNNEL_CHECK=1` over `ls_parity`, `w5items`, `w5push`, defaults) and `bench-000062` (E2 bench, base bc9b71f48 and new interleaved, 3 runs each, `DOTNET_TieredCompilation=0`, dev builds). **Both pass.** Client gate: `[ECS] check` mismatches 0 in all four runs; parity items 1,240,753 checked, 0 mismatched, 0 drawn- or lights-mismatched; mobiles 9,792,328 checked, 0 mismatched, 0 not mirrored. No `WorldWriter` line and no pre-T1 line in any log. Direct writes (last 5-s line): ls_parity 4,144,460 (113 sites), w5items 789,016 (85), w5push 209,959 (85), still the unconverted mobile paths. Sites by caller over the three funnel runs: `CharacterStatus` 30, `Mobile.ProcessSteps` 28, `UpdateGameObject` 25, `UpdateObject` 16 (part 2: 28), `UpdateCharacter` 14, `EnqueueStep` 14, then 13 or fewer each. **No `EquipItem` site** (part 2: 4). `UpdateObject`'s remaining sites are player and mobile lines only: `world.Player.Graphic` (2942), `world.Player.Flags` (2945), `mob.NotorietyFlag` (2965), and Graphic/Hue/X/Y/Z/Direction/Flags attributed to the `UpdateGameObject(...)` call line (2950; the same set as part 2's line 2956: its mobile branch, the next group). The equipment list's Graphic/Hue/Amount/Container/Layer sites (part 2: lines 3018-3023) are gone. `Container` at `World.RemoveItemFromContainer` and `World.RemoveItem` (2 sites each) remain (range sweep, `RemoveMobile`). E2 bench (`bench-000062`; median us/packet at 500 / 2000 / 8000 mobiles, new; spread = max - min over 3 runs): the gate (each funnel row <= its paired old-path row + 0.1 us) **passes**. 0x2E re-equip: old 0.341 / 0.346 / 0.357, funnel 0.347 / 0.357 / 0.351 (spreads <= 0.034); 0x78 list (clear + 5 entries): old 3.921 / 3.959 / 4.015, funnel 3.778 / 3.872 / 3.889 (spreads <= 0.16). Both rows exist only in `new`. Bytes: 0x2E 0 / 0; 0x78 old 1504.9, funnel 1400.0 at every size (the funnel allocates 105 B per packet less, never more; the likely source is the old path's creation Sync of each re-created item, which `WearItem` skips; not investigated further). The part 1-2 rows: 0x1A new 0.157 / 0.156 / 0.152 vs funnel 0.128 / 0.131 / 0.133; 0x1A update 0.110 / 0.108 / 0.110 vs 0.108 / 0.108 / 0.108; 0x25 new 0.225 / 0.228 / 0.252 vs 0.135 / 0.138 / 0.134; 0x25 update 0.073 / 0.073 / 0.073 vs 0.080 / 0.080 / 0.080 (+0.007, as before); bytes equal (140 / 0). Base vs new on rows this branch does not change: the T1 rows and most others within +-0.01 (spreads mostly <= 0.01). Not within noise: "item into backpack (0x25) + out" 0.176 / 0.196 / 0.189 -> 0.224 / 0.227 / 0.227 (spreads <= 0.004), "serial reuse" at 500 / 2000 0.233 / 0.231 -> 0.263 / 0.262, and the other way "ground item add" at 2000 / 8000 0.151 / 0.175 -> 0.110 / 0.111. The branch has no code change on these paths. The first two run after the new 0x78 rows, which destroy and re-create 5 x n worn items, so they meet a different world state. Read as a bench-ordering effect, not a regression; a follow-up bench could put the new rows last to confirm.
- **Codex audit of bc9b71f48..274c5fdf0 (gpt-6-astra, read-only; 1 P2 and notes; fixed in f7134d59b).** Dispositions:
  1. *P2, `WearItem` could switch owners midway through a list.* The old loop used the `obj` it captured once; `WearItem` looked the owner up with `World.Get(ownerSerial)` per entry. With a death-rekeyed owner (`0x8000_3000`, not a mobile serial, so `World.Get` tries the items first) and a first entry under that serial, the entry creates an item that later lookups return, and the next entry went into that item instead of the mobile. Fixed: `WearItem(Entity owner, ...)` takes the handler's `obj` and never looks it up. The instance is validated against its own table (`Mobiles` for a mobile, `Items` for an item, and the same World), so a mobile and an item sharing a serial are each recognised. A foreign or stale owner is a `NotHeld` violation: it throws in CUO_DEVTOOLS builds, and in release logs once and is rejected (null, nothing changed). It has no pre-T1 fallback (`Reject` gains `rejected: true` for the log text). The handler passes only the `obj` it just found, and no entry can remove it from its table, so no production path reaches the rejection. `ClearWornItems` keeps its serial: it runs right after the handler's `World.Get`, before any entry. Tests: `WearItem_Keeps_The_Captured_Owner_When_An_Entry_Shares_Its_Serial` (two Worlds, MOB rekeyed as `DisplayDeath` does, entries `0x8000_3000` then NEWITEM: both entries are the mobile's children and the new item has none; then the same packet again, where the handler's own lookup now finds the item, as before T1). It fails with the per-entry lookup and with validation through `World.Get` (mutation log). `WearItem_Rejects_An_Owner_This_World_Does_Not_Hold` (another World's mobile, a stale instance; throw and release).
  2. *Note, "no test can tell it apart"* for the skipped Direction Sync: too strong, since `ItemMirrorWrites` counts it. Reworded above.
  3. *Note, the mutation claim was not supported by the saved log.* Re-run with the whole set in one log; see the corrected bullet above.
  4. *Note, 60 of the 180 Wear cases have no owner* (NOBODY: the handler returns before the list, so they only check that nothing changes). Added a fourth owner, DEAD (MOB rekeyed to `0x8000_3000`), for 60 owner-present cases: `WearItem_Equals_The_Old_Path` is now 5 starts x 4 owners x 6 lists x crowded = 240 cases, 180 of them with an owner (MOB, BAG, DEAD). The DEAD cases do not name the owner's serial as an entry; the collision has its own test.
  5. *Also from the audit (recorded, no change):* the tests compare two Worlds through copied old paths and do not cover packet dispatch, the UI, real tile placement or multis; the client gate covers dispatch. Release nesting is rejection, not atomic recovery, as recorded in part 2.
- **Verification (f7134d59b):** 1669 pass + 2 skipped in both `CuoDevTools` variants (1607 + 62: 60 DEAD cases, 2 facts). One run of the dev variant had an unrelated failure in `ChunkLoadingTests.Drain_Does_Not_Allocate_Per_Frame` (passed alone and in a full re-run: an allocation check under build load). Both client builds succeed. Write-site budget unchanged (290): the fix moves no field write. No new client job: the only runtime change is where `WearItem` gets its owner, which differs from the gated binary only on the serial collision above.

## Body import choices: one body set per pack, chosen at import (2026-10-31, `poc/body-profile`)

Owner decisions of 2026-10-31 (survey `cuo-poc-state/surveys/bodies.md` §6): one pack per shard; the admin picks the body set once, at import; the client does no runtime body remapping. Base 12624ada4.

**Converter.**
- `--body-choices bodies.json` (no file = preset `aos`). `BodyChoices` parses and validates it (unknown keys, bad values, duplicate ids, malformed `from` fail with a message naming the entry); `BodyPlan` resolves Bodyconv.def per body and installs the result in the frozen loader (`AnimationsLoader.SetBodyConv`, `CopyMobType`; `ProcessBodyConvDef` is no longer called). Admin docs: [bodies.md](bodies.md).
- Remodel = own anim.mul art + a conversion (17 on 7.0.103: 9 10 26 28 76 253 318 319 689 704 791 793 794 796 797 798 799); addition = converted, no own art (441). Presets: `t2a`/`uor` every remodel old; `lbr` the column-1 target for column-1 remodels, others old; `aos` the last column (as before). `forceOldAnimations` turns every remodel with a column-1 target old. `remodels` overrides single ids (`new` = last column). `additions: standins` draws the Body.def stand-in only where the preset turns the addition's conversion off; additions without a stand-in keep their art.
- 9/26/28 (7.x all `-1` lines): built-in table `BodyPlan.RevertedLbrRemodels` (9 → anim2 7, 26 → anim2 24, 28 → anim2 5), added only when the install has the all `-1` line and anim2.mul.
- Extras: `{ "id", "from": "anim.mul:76" | "animN.mul:G" }` become a conversion entry for the new id, with the mobtypes entry (kind, flags) of the body the variant belongs to (anim.mul: that body; animN: the lowest body converting to it) and its column's mount height. The id must be free (mobtypes, Bodyconv line, Body/Corpse.def index or stand-in target, own art, UOP, another extra's source); the error says which. The converter prints a ModernUO `Data/bodyTable.cfg` line per extra (the file is `.cfg`, not `.txt`).
- Manifest: `bodies` record (preset, flag, additions, overrides, extras, source path, bodies.json SHA-256). `Verify.CheckAnim` rebuilds the plan from it, so `--verify-only` checks a pack against its own choices. `--only` runs that skip anims keep the previous record.
- **AnimationSequence for converted bodies (coordinator/owner, 2026-10-31):** a converted MUL body's actions follow the converted target's AnimationSequence.uop entry (`BodyMeta.SeqBody`, `AnimConvert.SequenceGroup`). Before, MUL bodies used no sequence at all (as upstream ClassicUO: only UOP bodies). One guard I added: a replacement whose group has no frames in the drawn MUL is not applied, because the entries describe the target's UOP layout (5's list sends walk 0 → 22, past anim2 body 5's 22 groups: giant spider 28 would walk invisibly). Diagnostic `--no-target-sequence` builds the old behaviour for A/B.
- `--compare-bodies <packA> <packB>`: which body entries draw differently (entry fields, per-direction frame counts, centres, sprite geometry; page placement ignored), plus aliases pointing at changed bodies.

**Client.** `BodyConvFlags`, `Animation.UpdateAnimationTable` and the `bcFlags` block in `PacketHandlers.EnableLockedFeatures` are removed; 0xB9 still sets the locked features and chat. Alias lookup stays single hop (`ResolveBody`; the converter stores the final target). No write-site change (no ECS-owned field touched).

**Results (7.0.103, source of classic-1.2; `--only anims` into hard-linked test packs).**
- Default without the sequence rule (`--no-target-sequence`) vs classic-1.2: **exactly 3 entries differ: 9 (anim:9 → anim2:7), 26 (anim:26 → anim2:24), 28 (anim:28 → anim2:5)**; one alias draws changed art: 153 → 26 (Body.def and Corpse.def). The other stand-ins of 9/26/28 (38, 43, 102, 318, 746, 784, 785, 792 → 9; 11, 19, 20, 157, 173 → 28; 310, 316, 747, 748 → 26) are converted bodies under `aos`, so their aliases are not used and their entries are unchanged.
- Default (with the sequence rule) vs classic-1.2: 126 entries differ: 9, 26, 28 and 123 converted bodies whose actions now follow their target's sequence: 10 11 19 20 38 40 43 46 62 67 74 95 102 104 122 124 125 126 128 132 146 148 149 152 157 172 173 176 181 182 187 188 189 191 192 193 194 196 197 198 199 240 241 242 243 244 245 246 249 250 251 252 253 254 256 257 258 259 261 262 263 264 265 266 267 271 273 277 284 300–308 311–319 471 689 704 746 748 752 754–758 763 765 770–776 778 780 782 783 785 787 792 793 794 797 798 804 806 807 808 1261; alias 156 → 95 also draws changed art. 1318 groups are replaced; **614 of them had frames of their own in the MUL, which the rule hides** (e.g. 10 and 9: 6, 12, 13 → 4; 16 → 15; 17–21 → 1/0); 364 replacements to an empty group were not applied. Some bodies gain actions (95: 10 → 13). Anim pages 599.5 MiB vs 623.2 MiB without the rule (the hidden frames are no longer stored).
- `t2a` vs `aos`: exactly the 17 remodels differ (9 10 26 28 76 253 318 319 689 704 791 793 794 796–799), plus alias 153 → 26. The survey's ~210 counted additions going to stand-ins or nothing and equipment; with `additions: newest` none of those change. Anim pages 602.3 MiB (t2a) vs 599.5 MiB (aos): the old art is slightly larger than the anim2 art it replaces, and nothing is dropped. vs classic-1.2: 127 entries (the 123 sequence bodies minus 9/26/28 plus the 17 remodels' own art; 156 → 95 alias).
- `--verify-only` on both packs: all checks passed (anim sample BIT-EXACT vs the ClassicUO loader with the same plan: aos 108,302 of 112,152 frames, the rest absent or on another page; t2a 106,846 of 110,509).
- Conversion time `--only anims`: 63–94 s.

**Memory:** none per client (one resolved set, same format). The test packs are 1.1 GiB each of mostly hard links.

**Tests.** `tests/Uo.Converter.Tests/BodyChoicesTests.cs`: synthetic resolution (presets, standins, overrides, extras with mount height, 18 bad-input cases, 4 bad-id cases, manifest round trip) and, when `C:\Ultima Online Classic` (or `CUO_CLASSIC_UO`) exists, real-data checks of 10, 11, 76, 157, 791, 793, 9, 26, 28, 43 under `aos`, `t2a`, `uor`, `lbr`, `forceOldAnimations`, `standins`, a remodel override and extras; the 9 → 7 sequence (12→4, 13→4, 20→1, not 9's 13→12/20→19; action 13 draws stored group 4); the spider guard; and a small pack conversion (bodies 9, 11, 28, 43 and an extra) checking the entries and that 43's stand-in follows 9's resolved art.

**Client check: bench-000058** (bench-000057 ran while the server was down and never connected; resubmitted unchanged). Release JIT build of be0de57aa, Gpu, the default (`aos`) test pack, kbatman3 at Green Acres: `[set Body 9` / `[set Body 28` on the player, shots standing, walking, and during `[Animate 12 7 3 true false 0` and `[Animate 6 ...`, then `[set Body 400`. Status ok, 41 s, 0 ECS mismatches. **Daemon 9 and giant spider 28 draw the anim2 art** (slim daemon with long thin wings; brown spider without the grey abdomen), matching the right-hand renders of the survey's `daemon.png`/`spider.png`. The `[Animate` shots look like the idle/stand pose, so they don't show whether group 4 replaced 12 or 6: the 0x6E action for a monster body may be remapped by the client first. **Left for the owner's in-game test:** a daemon (body 9 or 10) attacking or casting, where 7's list replaces 6, 12 and 13 with 4.

### Body import choices: audit fixes and the owner's era rules (2026-10-31, `poc/body-profile`)

Codex audit of be0de57aa (seven findings) plus the owner's rules of 2026-10-31 (coordinator messages). Base 83156345b.

| # | Finding | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| 1 (P1) | Remodels were found with today's mobtypes layout; for 253, 689, 704 (and 318, 319, the mounts) it reads other bodies' anim.mul slots. | Fixed. Own art = every stored direction of walk and stand decodes to a non-empty frame in the body's own anim.mul layout (pre-mobtypes, by id). **Remodels on 7.0.103: 9, 10, 26, 28, 76, 95** (was 17). 318 → stand-in 9, 319 → 51, 791 → 220 hue 11, 793 → 200, 794 → 219, 796 → 39, 797 → 12, 798 → 59, 799 → 218: additions with a Body.def stand-in. 253, 689, 704: additions with no older look. New: 95 (turkey; mobtypes says animal, its monster-layout slot holds an older grey creature, same in UOAOS) is a remodel; old 95 is read with an installed monster layout (`BodyPlan.MobTypes`). The converter prints every remodel's old and new source and the misread bodies. |
| 2 | Extras could take equipment AnimIDs. | Fixed: nonzero tiledata AnimIDs and Equipconv.def sources/targets are reserved; the error names the item (`tiledata item 0x108A "…" uses it as its AnimID`) or the Equipconv line. |
| 3 | An explicit MUL extra inherited UseUopAnimation and became a UOP lookup. | Fixed: kind and flags are inherited (from the lowest non-UOP body converting to the art, else a UOP one), UseUopAnimation never; anim.mul sources are read in their own layout. The importer checks the extra resolves to exactly the requested file and body with walk/stand frames. `"mountHeight"` sets an extra's height; default = that same body's column height (0 for anim.mul). |
| 4 | bodies.json was loaded after the previous output was cleared. | Fixed: the file is parsed before the guard/clear step, and the plan is resolved right after the client files load, before `ClearPreviousOutput`. Test runs the converter's entry point with a bad extra and a missing file: rc 1, the previous output file is still there. |
| 5 | No bodies record = today's default (9/26/28 and sequences). | Fixed: no record = **resolver policy 0** (classic-1.2 rules: every column, last wins, no 9/26/28 lines, no sequences). Records carry `policy` (1 now) and `sequences`; a record with policy 0 or above 1 is refused. |
| 6 | `additions: newest` could pick column 1. | Fixed: newest = the last column; the era fallback applies to `standins` only. |
| 7 | Duplicate properties inside an extra overwrote silently. | Fixed: rejected with the extra's position (`extras[1]: "from" is given twice in the same extra`). |

**Owner rules (coordinator, 2026-10-31), each one constant or method so it is easy to flip:**
- Eras: anim.mul T2A/UOR; Bodyconv column 1 LBR, 2 AOS, 3 SE, 4 ML, 5+ later. Presets show up to t2a/uor: T2A, lbr: LBR, aos: everything.
- Remodels count as AOS for the presets whatever their column (`BodyPlan.RemodelEra`): t2a, uor and lbr show every remodel old, aos new. 9/26/28 have era LBR (`RevertedEra`), which only matters if one were an addition.
- `additions` default is now `standins` = the era rule: an addition later than the preset draws its Body.def stand-in (the pre-AOS per-expansion behaviour), else keeps its art; `newest` never falls back. aos: nothing falls back.
- `forceOldAnimations`: every remodel old, additions untouched (`BodyPlan.ForceOldReverts`, under the owner's investigation).
- `sequences`: `"none"` (default, as ClassicUO) or `"target"` (the earlier rule). `--no-target-sequence` is gone.
- Also: a body drawn as its Body.def stand-in stores no frames (the client draws the alias only; for 318, 319 and the mounts the mobtypes-layout index pointed at other bodies' slots, which the pack used to store unused). `--verify-only` checks those entries have an alias and no frames.

**Results (7.0.103, `--only anims` into hard-linked test packs of classic-1.2; `--compare-bodies`).**
- **Default (aos) vs classic-1.2: exactly 9, 26, 28 differ** (anim.mul → anim2 7/24/5), plus alias 153 → 26 (Body.def and Corpse.def). No client job needed.
- **aos + forceOldAnimations vs aos:** 6 entries, the remodels 9 10 26 28 76 95; aliases 153 → 26, 156 → 95.
- **lbr vs aos:** 38 entries = 6 remodels old + 32 AOS-or-later additions as stand-ins (300–319, 747, 930–940); aliases 153, 156. Column-1 additions (11, 43, 157, the mounts…) keep their art.
- **t2a vs aos:** 128 entries = 6 remodels old + 122 additions as stand-ins (incl. 318 → 9, 319 → 51 and the mounts 791 → 220 hue 11 …); aliases 153, 156.
- Anim pages (brotli): aos 623.2 MiB, aos+force 630.3, lbr 616.8, t2a 559.7 (stand-ins store no frames).
- `--verify-only`: aos pack OK (108,430 of 112,267 sampled frames BIT-EXACT, rest absent or on another page), t2a OK (105,233 of 108,607), **classic-1.2 (published, read only; file list, sizes and mtimes compared before/after: unchanged) OK with the legacy policy** (107,647 of 111,610).
- Montages (first walk frame, direction 2): `…/scratchpad/body-profile/fix/remodels.png` (old | new of the 6 remodels) and `…/fix/not-remodels.png` (what the mobtypes layout read | the Body.def stand-in, unhued | the new art) for 253, 318, 319, 689, 704 and the mounts; script `fix/gen.py` + `fix/montage.py` (copied from the survey's render.py).

**Tests.** Converter tests 87 pass, 1 skipped (`BodyChoicesTests`: 52, including a test per finding, a pre-AOS stand-in test per preset, era/forceOld/newest/legacy/policy tests and the entry-point clear-order test). Unit tests both flavours (default and `-p:CuoDevTools=false`): 1159 pass, 2 skipped. No write-site change. Memory: none per client.

**Follow-ups:** the owner's in-game checks (which AnimationSequence list the OSI client uses; forceOldAnimations scope); whether 95 should count as a remodel.

### Body import choices: round-2 audit fixes (2026-10-31, `poc/body-profile`)

Codex round-2 audit of 0f05f3252 (five P2 findings). Base 0f05f3252.

| # | Finding | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Selected mount heights never reach either renderer (t2a 793 drawn as horse 200, rider still at −9). | Fixed. **Not a regression:** upstream ClassicUO stopped reading Bodyconv mount heights in a72e5180a (2025-02-16, "mounts in a different file"): both its MobileView paths use the item-keyed `Mounts` table, and `BodyConvInfo.MountHeight` has been dead data since. classic-1.2's client and the PoC did the same, so this was a pre-existing gap. The table can't simply be replaced by the Bodyconv heights: on the aos pack they disagree (0x3E90 → 276: table 0, Bodyconv −9; unicorn 0x3EB4 → 122: −9 vs 0; every UOP mount: 9/12/18/−10/−4 vs 0). So the converter stores a per-body **`MountShift`** (the former pad byte of `AnimBodyEntry`) = mount height of the art the pack draws (after the Body.def stand-in) − that of the default (aos) art; extras: their own height; legacy packs: 0. Both renderers (`MobileAnimationSystem.Select`, `MobileView` draw and pick) use `AnimationRules.MountOffsetY(item, shift)` = table + shift. Verify recomputes every shift. |
| 2 | Frame-less stand-ins had no corpse target (t2a 191–195). | Fixed: `AnimConvert.Targets` resolves the live and corpse targets independently; a stand-in drops its frames only when both point elsewhere; Corpse.def is honoured, else the corpse is the live stand-in (192's corpse = 228's death frames). Verify checks every stand-in has a corpse target. Only stand-ins (bodies whose frames the converter drops) get the fallback, so aos entries are unchanged. |
| 3 | The probe accepted transparent frames; 95's grey shape isn't an older turkey. | Fixed: `BodyPlan.Visible` requires a non-transparent pixel in every stored walk/stand direction. `BodyPlan.Classification` decides ambiguous art: **95 = not a remodel (owner, final)**. **Remodels on 7.0.103: 9, 10, 26, 28, 76** (the visibility probe alone keeps all six; 95 leaves by the table). A `remodels` override for 95 is refused with the reason. |
| 4 | Unsupported manifest policies were not refused on every path. | Fixed: every run that keeps the previous bodies record (`--only` without anims, `--no-anims`, `--verify-only`) validates it before any output, manifest or debug write and exits 1; a run that rebuilds the anims replaces it. The anim debug PNGs are skipped when the anim checks fail. |
| 5 | Opt-in sequences replaced whole actions on one populated direction. | Fixed: `SequenceGroup(l, m, action, dir)` applies a replacement per stored direction, only where that direction decodes to visible frames; the others keep the action's own group. The report counts partial replacements (`/n`). No stock trigger found (as the auditor). |

**Results (7.0.103, `--only anims` into the hard-linked test packs; converter `fix/bin2`).**
- `--compare-bodies` classic-1.2 vs default (aos): **exactly 9, 26, 28**, alias 153 → 26 (Body.def, Corpse.def). Unchanged.
- vs aos: **t2a 127** entries (5 remodels + 122 stand-ins; was 128 with 95), **lbr 37** (was 38), **force 5** (9 10 26 28 76). Alias 156 → 95 no longer differs.
- `--verify-only`: aos OK (109,488 of 113,619 sampled frames BIT-EXACT; 0 shifted bodies), t2a OK (106,023 of 109,352; 2 shifted bodies: 192, 793, both +9), **classic-1.2 OK with the legacy policy** (109,118 of 113,046; read only, recursive listing with mtimes identical before/after).
- **Riders on the aos pack:** `MountHeightTests` compares old (table) and new (table + shift) offsets for every one of the 65,536 tiledata items taken as a mount item: **0 changed**. On t2a: 5 change, among them 0x3E9B/0x3E9D (192) and 0x3EBB (793), −9 → 0.
- **Client check, bench-000064** (Release JIT of the working tree, Gpu, t2a test pack, kbatman3 at Green Acres; bench-000063 mounted the skeletal mount twice because the second double-click hit it again, so the script was reordered): horse (item 0x3EA1, offset 0) then skeletal mount (0x3EBB, table −9, shift +9, **offset 0**); the driver's `mount` line logs the MobileView value and the ECS `AnimationState.MountOffsetY`, equal in both cases. The skeletal mount draws as hued horse 200, and the rider's pixels are identical in both shots (365 robe pixels, same bounding box 291,160–316,206). 0 ECS mismatches; NPCs wiped.

**Tests.** Converter tests 93 pass, 1 skipped (BodyChoicesTests 58; new: `Mount_Shift_Is_The_Drawn_Height_Minus_The_Default_Art_Height`, `Probe_Requires_Visible_Pixels`, `Mount_Shifts_On_Real_Data`, `Frame_Less_Stand_Ins_Keep_A_Corpse`, `Target_Sequences_Fall_Back_Per_Direction`, `Unsupported_Manifest_Policy_Stops_Every_Path_Before_Writing`, `Turkey_95_Is_Classified_As_An_Addition`). Each fix was reverted once and its tests failed (1: both mount-shift tests; 2: the corpse test; 3: the probe test; 4: the policy test; 5: the per-direction test). Unit tests (`MountHeightTests` new; `CUO_MOUNT_AOS_PACK`/`CUO_MOUNT_T2A_PACK` point at the test packs) both flavours: 1166 pass, 2 skipped. No write-site change. Memory: none (the shift uses the existing pad byte).

**Open:** unicorn 0x3EB4 (body 122) keeps its table offset −9 on t2a, where 122 draws stand-in 228: the table value isn't explained by a Bodyconv height, so the shift treats it as item-specific. If the owner wants t2a unicorns to sit like horses, that needs a per-item rule.


### Body import choices: round-3 audit fixes and stand-in mount offsets (2026-10-31, `poc/body-profile`)

Codex round-3 audit of 631abefb1 (one P1, three P2, two P3) and the owner's decision on stand-in mounts. Base 631abefb1.

| # | Finding | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| 1 (P1) | `--gump-report` skipped policy validation, created the debug folder and ran `ClearPreviousOutput` before returning. | Fixed: `--gump-report` sets `convert = false` like `--audio-report`, and both read-only reports return right after the client files load, before the debug folder, the body plan and any clear. `--filter-ref` now refuses published packs too. Entry paths: see the table below. |
| 2 | Corpse resolution didn't flatten the new fallbacks (`43 {191}` with t2a's frame-less 191 stored 191); self-targets with a hue lost their frames; no cycle check. | Fixed: `AnimConvert.CorpseTarget` stores the effective target: Corpse.def hops while the body is plain anim.mul (as the loader), then through any body that stores no frames to its live stand-in (43 → 191 → 228). `CorpseHop` tells an explicit self-target from an absent line (the loader writes the hue for a self-target and returns false for both); `DropsFrames` keeps a self-targeted body's frames. A cycle throws `BodyChoicesException`; `BodyPlan.Build` resolves every Corpse.def body and stand-in, so a cycle stops the import before anything is cleared. Verify recomputes every alias and corpse target and counts targets without frames (aos, t2a, classic-1.2: 0). |
| 3 | Turkey 95 and alias 156 have death 8 but no 12; the second-death corpse drew nothing. | Fixed in the client: `AnimationsLoader.GetDeathAction` returns the first death action when the drawn body has no frames for the second in any direction (new `HasAction`). Every corpse path goes through it (Gpu `ItemSpriteExtract`, Legacy `ItemView` draw and pick, `Item` corpse tick, 0xAF). **Pre-existing:** classic-1.2's entry for 95 is identical to the default pack's (`--compare-bodies` lists only 9/26/28), and ClassicUO main has no fallback either (`Animations.GetAnimationFrames` returns empty). The rule is general, not a 95 special case; packs are unchanged. |
| 4 | Uo.Client ignored `MountShift`. | Fixed: `AnimMobileSprites.RiderOffset` = table + the original mount body's shift, taken before the alias is followed and used for the body and every equipment layer. Uo.Client's mount body now uses the shared `MountTable.MountBody` (it lacked the ethereal unicorn/kirin cases). |
| 5 | Table + shift saturated at sbyte. | Fixed: `AnimationRules.MountOffsetY(item, shift)` returns int, `MobileView` carries int, `AnimationState.MountOffsetY` is a short (the sum is −256..254). Tiger 18 + 127 = 145. |
| 6 | `MountHeightTests` passed without fixtures (read CURRENT, returned early). | Fixed: `[MountPackFact("CUO_MOUNT_AOS_PACK")]` / `("CUO_MOUNT_T2A_PACK")` skip when the variable is unset (no fallback to CURRENT); `Fixture` checks the manifest's record (policy 1, preset, no overrides/extras/forceOld). Without the variables: 10 pass, 3 skipped; with classic-1.2 / the lbr pack in their place, the 3 fail on the record check. New coverage: `Corpse_Death_Variants_Have_Frames_For_Turkey_95_And_Alias_156` (both death variants of 95 and 156 through the pack loader, all 8 directions) and `Renderers_Use_The_Shared_Rules` (source check of the Gpu, Legacy draw, Legacy pick and Uo.Client rider offsets and of the corpse `GetDeathAction` call sites). |

**Converter entry paths** (`poc/Uo.Converter/Program.cs`):

| Mode | Writes | Retained bodies record | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| full conversion with anims | clears the manifest-listed files, writes the pack | replaced; bodies.json is read and the plan (incl. corpse cycles) built before the clear | `Bad_Choices_Stop_Before_The_Previous_Output_Is_Cleared` |
| full conversion `--no-anims` | clears, writes | validated before any write | `Unsupported_Manifest_Policy_…` |
| `--only` without anims | writes the named sections, manifest | validated before any write | same (`hues`, `tiledata,hues`) |
| `--only anims` / `--anims-only` | rewrites anim/, manifest | replaced; plan built before anim/*.bin is deleted | (rebuild path) |
| `--verify-only` | debug PNGs only | validated before the debug folder | same |
| `--gump-report`, `--audio-report` | nothing | not read; return before folder/clear/plan | same (`--gump-report --no-anims` rc 0, `--audio-report` fails after load; the listed file survives) |
| `--bench-chunked`, `--filter-ref` | their own output folder (published roots refused) | n/a (no pack manifest) | — |
| `--anim-report`, `--compare-bodies`, `--compare-indexed`, `--bench-bc7` | nothing | n/a | — |

The policy test's pack now lists a file in its manifest, so a clear would show; with the round-2 dispatch restored, the `--gump-report` case fails (the file is deleted).

**Owner rule (coordinator, 2026-10-31): stand-in mounts sit as on the stand-in.** `BodyPlan.MountShift` takes the Mounts table offsets per mount body (`BodyPlan.MountOffsets`, from the shared table with the install's tiledata AnimIDs; on 7.0.103 no body's items disagree). A body the plan draws as a Body.def stand-in it doesn't draw by default gets shift = stand-in's offset (its items' table offset, 0 if none) − its own items' offset; other art changes keep the mount-height difference. The table is now one copy, `Uo.Pack.MountTable`, read by the client's `Mounts`, `AnimationRules.MountBody`, Uo.Client and the converter. Mount items whose offset changes: **t2a: 0x3E9B and 0x3E9D (192 → 228), 0x3EB4 unicorn (122 → 228), 0x3EBB (793 → 200), each −9 → 0** (the unicorn is new; the others were already +9 by the height rule). **lbr: none** (its mounts keep their art). aos: all 65,536 items unchanged.

**Results (7.0.103, `--only anims` into the hard-linked test packs; converter `body-profile/fix3/bin`).**
- `--compare-bodies` classic-1.2 vs default (aos): **exactly 9, 26, 28**, alias 153 → 26 (Body.def, Corpse.def). Unchanged.
- vs aos: t2a 127, lbr 37, force 5 entries: the same lists as round 2; the only change in the t2a output is `122 … shift9`. No stock corpse target moved (the flattening only matters for custom Corpse.def data; the real-data test finds no stock chain through a frame-less body).
- `--verify-only`: aos OK (110,388 of 114,454 sampled frames BIT-EXACT; 0 shifted bodies; aliases and corpse targets match; 0 corpse targets without frames), t2a OK (106,316 of 109,796; 3 shifted bodies: 122, 192, 793), **classic-1.2 OK with the legacy policy** (109,204 of 112,948; recursive listing with mtimes identical before/after).

**Tests.** Converter tests from a clean build of e38ad10a0 (bin/obj deleted, `--no-incremental`; the auditor's failure came from a stale binary): **98 pass, 1 skipped** (99; BodyChoicesTests 63). New: `Corpse_Targets_End_At_A_Body_With_Frames`, `Explicit_Corpse_Self_Targets_Keep_Their_Frames`, `Corpse_Target_Cycles_Are_Refused`, `Corpse_Targets_On_Real_Data_Have_Death_Frames` (aos, t2a, lbr, force), `Stand_In_Mounts_Seat_The_Rider_As_On_The_Stand_In`; the policy test covers the report paths. Unit tests, clean builds, both flavours (default and `-p:CuoDevTools=false`) with `CUO_MOUNT_AOS_PACK`/`CUO_MOUNT_T2A_PACK` on the reconverted test packs: **1172 pass, 2 skipped** each. Revert checks (each fix reverted once, then restored): fix 1 → policy test fails (file deleted by the gump report); fix 2 → the three synthetic corpse tests fail; owner rule → stand-in mount test fails (0x3EB4 at −9); fix 3 → death-variant test fails (95, second death group 12, direction 0); fix 4 alone → the renderer test fails on Uo.Client; Legacy pick without the shift → the renderer test fails; fix 5 → the offset theory (145, −138) and the ECS sum test fail. **Not failing on revert:** `Corpse_Targets_On_Real_Data_Have_Death_Frames` passes on the round-2 rule too: stock 7.0.103 has no Corpse.def chain through a frame-less body, so it is a guard for the real data, not a regression test (the synthetic tests are). One stock exception it documents: 786's Corpse.def self-target has no death frames in every direction, in the source as well.

**Client job:** none. The mount change is data only through the code path bench-000064 checked (793 there; the unicorn now gets the same +9). The death fallback is a new client rule for corpses, covered by the loader-level test on the real pack and the call-site check; staging a second-death turkey corpse in game needs the corpse direction bit, which the driver can't set. If the coordinator wants an in-game check, a job killing turkeys until a second-death corpse appears is the way.

**Memory:** none per client (`AnimationState.MountOffsetY` sbyte → short: at most a few bytes per mobile; the Mounts table moved, not duplicated).

**Open:** none new. The unicorn question from round 2 is answered by the owner's rule above.


### Body import choices: round-4 audit fixes (2026-10-31, `poc/body-profile`)

Codex round-4 audit of e1d15b1da (two P2, two P3). Base e1d15b1da.

| # | Finding | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| 1 (P2) | The corpse animation tick (`Item.ProcessAnimation`) resolved the live body: t2a with `Corpse.def 43 {191} 0` stores corpse target 228 (six death frames), the tick clamped against live 9's four and stopped at frame 3. | Fixed: the tick calls `AnimationsLoader.TryCorpseFrame`, which resolves the Corpse.def target (`ResolveBody(…, isCorpse: true)`) before it picks the death action (`GetDeathAction`, with the second-death fallback) and the frame count, as the Gpu extract and ItemView draw and pick do. Test `Corpse_Tick_Advances_To_The_Last_Frame_Of_The_Corpse_Target` (t2a pack): the audit's case set in the loaded table (43 → 228, live 9) plus every stock corpse whose target differs from its live body (14 on t2a, none with different frame counts); both death variants in all 5 stored directions advance to frame 5 (6 frames), not 3. |
| 2 (P2) | Verify rejected every stand-in with frames and every stand-in without a corpse target, so explicit corpse self-targets (frames kept; hue 0 stores no target) failed conversion and `--verify-only`. | Fixed: `Verify.CheckBodyEntries` (the body-table part of the anim check, now callable on its own) follows the recomputed `AnimConvert.Targets(…).DropFrames`: a stand-in that drops its frames must store none and have an alias and a corpse target; one that keeps them only needs its alias (aliases and corpse targets are compared separately, as before). Verification-level test `Verification_Accepts_Stand_Ins_That_Keep_Their_Frames_For_A_Corpse_Self_Target`: a t2a conversion with `318 {318} 65535` and `319 {319} 0` in Corpse.def (318 and 319 have art in their own slots) keeps both bodies' frames, passes `CheckBodyEntries`, and two broken copies (192 without a corpse target, 192 with frames) fail it. |
| 3 (P3) | Stand-in seating was a delta from the listed items' offset: unlisted 0x007A (AnimID 0, falls back to body 122) sat at +9 instead of horse 228's 0. Seven item offsets changed on t2a, only four of them listed. | Fixed with an **absolute seat**: a body drawn as a Body.def stand-in it doesn't draw by default stores the stand-in's own table offset in `MountShift` and sets a pack-only bit in `Flags` (`AnimBodyEntry.MountAbsoluteFlag` = 0x40000000; mobtypes flags never use it, the converter clears it from them and `Animation.GetAnimFlags` masks it). `Uo.Pack.MountSeat(Value, Absolute).RiderOffset(item)` = absolute ? value : table + value, used by every renderer (Gpu `MobileAnimationSystem`, Legacy `MobileView` draw and pick, Uo.Client `RiderOffset`, the driver's `mount` line). Other art changes keep the relative mount-height shift. Same format (no new field), so no memory change. |
| 4 (P3) | `CorpseHop` read hue 0xFFFF as "no line", so `191 {191} 65535` lost its self-target. | Fixed: the tools loader exposes `TryGetCorpseDef` (presence from its table); `CorpseHop` uses it. The converter's anim workers now share the main file manager's override map (`UOFileManager.OverrideMap`), which the tests use to substitute Corpse.def. Test `Corpse_Def_Presence_Is_Explicit_Whatever_The_Hue` goes through `CorpseHop` and `Targets` on the real loader: 191 `{191} 65535` → (191, 0xFFFF), frames kept; 193 `{193} 0` → own frames, no target; 194 `{9} 65535` → (9, 0xFFFF); 192 (no line) → the stand-in. |

**Second-death fallback, accepted timing change (from round 3).** The fallback (`GetDeathAction` plays the first death action when the drawn body has no frames for the second) also applies to the 0xAF temporary corpses. Across the aos, t2a, lbr, force and classic-1.2 fixtures, resolved corpses **95/156, 704 and UOP 1308** are affected: their 0xAF mobiles now play the first death animation before removal instead of vanishing on the next animation tick. That follows from the rule and is accepted (coordinator, 2026-10-31).

**Item offsets over all 65,536 items** (`MountHeightTests` on the reconverted packs, `Stand_In_Mounts_Seat_The_Rider_As_On_The_Stand_In` from the plan, both taking every tiledata item as a mount item): **aos: 0 changed** (every seat relative 0). **t2a: exactly 4 changed, all listed: 0x3E9B and 0x3E9D (body 192 → 228), 0x3EB4 (122 → 228), 0x3EBB (793 → 200), each −9 → 0.** Unlisted items: none change (0x007A → 122, 0x00C0 → 192, 0x0319 → 793 stay at 0; round 3 had moved them to +9). lbr: 0 changed.

**Results (7.0.103, `--only anims` into the hard-linked test packs; converter `body-profile/fix4/bin`).**

**Tests.** Converter tests from a clean build (bin/obj of the converter and its tests deleted, `--no-incremental`): **100 pass, 1 skipped** (101; BodyChoicesTests 65; new: `Corpse_Def_Presence_Is_Explicit_Whatever_The_Hue`, `Verification_Accepts_Stand_Ins_That_Keep_Their_Frames_For_A_Corpse_Self_Target`; `Stand_In_Mounts_Seat_The_Rider_As_On_The_Stand_In` now scans all 65,536 items under aos, t2a and lbr and pins the t2a list). ## T1 funnel, part 4: mobiles (2026-10-31, `bg/ecs-t1-funnel-4`)

Base `poc/modern-client` d7e063cd9 (funnel part 3 merged). Commits 87b560577 (groundwork), 234f906c4 (mobile operations, handlers, tests, E2 rows). Plan: ecs-transition-plan.md, T1. Same operation pattern (admission → resolve with the handler's captured instance → compute → ECS commit → cache from the values → derived state → placement); the audit rules of parts 1–3 applied from the start.

- **Groundwork (87b560577).**
  - *Mobile fold and commit.* `WorldEcs.BeginFold` takes any entity; while a mobile is folded, its hook Syncs (the Direction setter, `AddToTile`/`SetInWorldTile`) and its `PushInputs`/`PushClock` are skipped. `CommitMobile(Mobile, in MobileState)` writes the record (`UpsertMobile`, the same call `Sync`'s mobile branch makes) from the operation's values and returns the entity; `CommitMobileInputs` is the derived-state step (the `MobileInputs` and the clock are computed from the getters, so they are pushed after the cache writes). `MobileCommitObserver` and `MobileMirrorWrites` are the test hooks (like `CommitObserver`/`ItemMirrorWrites`).
  - *`EnqueueStep` split.* `PlanStep` is the pure half (accepted, changes, the walk start with `SetAnimation(0xFF)` when not walking, `LastStepTime`, up to three steps), `ApplyStep` the mutation in the old order; `EnqueueStep` = plan + apply. `PlanStep` takes the queue's end position, so an operation that writes the position first (UpdateGameObject's creation branch) passes the position it computed.
  - *`Mobile.BodyState`*: `CheckGraphicChange`'s sex and race as a pure helper (like `Item.CorpseState`).
  - Placements and scopes hold an `Entity`; `PlaceWorldItem` rejects a mobile's token; `PlacePreT1` places a mobile as UpdateGameObject did.
  - Budget −10 (290 → 280): `Mobile.cs` IsFemale 6 → 1, Race 6 → 1.
- **Mobiles (234f906c4).**
  - *`UpsertMobile` + `PlaceMobile`*: UpdateGameObject's mobile branch, so 0x77 and 0x78/0xD3 for another mobile, 0x1A/0xF3 for a mobile's serial and 0xF6's mobiles. The handler's `obj` (its `World.Get(serial)`, captured once) is passed in and validated against the mobiles table (a null or destroyed one creates the mobile with `GetOrCreateMobile`, whose creation Sync runs as before). Before any write: the creation's values (graphic plus increment, sex and race from the unmasked graphic, direction, position), for a mobile other than the player the step plan or the reset to the packet's position (unplaced marker, or a full queue: `EnqueueStep`'s false), the masked graphic, the FixHue'd hue, the flags. The old `World.Get(mobile) == null` test is always false for a held mobile and is not repeated (comment in the code). The tile comes after the handler's new-mobile SingleClick, through a placement token, as for 0x1A.
  - *`SetNotoriety`* (0x77 on `World.Mobiles.Get`'s mobile, 0x78 on the mobile `World.Get` returned), *`SetMobileBody`* (the player's body: 0x77/0x78 with CheckGraphicChange's sex and race; 0x20 with its direction, whose door check runs inside the operation as the setter did), *`MoveMobile`* (0x20's tile, last, after DenyWalk, the season and CloseRangedGumps, which read the old position as before), *`RemoveMobile`* (0x1D for a mobile with everything it wears or holds: owns the removed subtree, cancels the placements of the mobile and of every removed item, no fold).
  - *Rejections:* a mobile this World does not hold (foreign or stale) is a `NotHeld` violation: it throws in CUO_DEVTOOLS builds and in release is rejected with nothing changed (no pre-T1 path: the handlers pass only what they just looked up). A mobile placement that is not outstanding takes the pre-T1 placement in release (`PlacePreT1`); nesting is rejected.
  - *What the old path published and the funnel does not:* the old path's intermediate Syncs (the Direction setter's, with the old graphic, hue and flags) and its extra input pushes. The final record, tags, inputs and clock are identical (tests); `MobileInputs.Pushes` (a diagnostic counter in the inspector dump) is lower, and the mirror holds the final values already when the SingleClick callback runs (no reader of the mirror runs there).
  - Budget −27 (280 → 253): `PacketHandlers.cs` Direction 6 → 2, Flags 9 → 4, Graphic 8 → 3, IsRunning 2 → 0, NotorietyFlag 3 → 1, X/Y/Z 3 → 0 each. `FunnelOperations` gains `UpsertMobile`, `PlaceMobile`, `SetNotoriety`, `SetMobileBody`, `MoveMobile`, `RemoveMobile`.
- **Tests** (`WorldWriterMobileTests`, two Worlds, old copies `OldUpsertMobile`, `OldEnqueueStep`, `OldCheckGraphicChange`; every pair starts from the same random-generator state and must draw the same number of values, since `SetAnimation` draws the idle delay): `UpsertMobile_Equals_The_Old_Path` (7 starts: none, standing, one queued step, walking, full queue, unplaced, destroyed but held × 8 packets: no-op, a step running, far with a turn, a turn in place, a body change through the increment, a graphic above 0x3FFF, the unplaced marker as position, a new mobile; each followed by a resend, the next packet and one a later frame = 56 cases), `UpsertMobile_The_Callback_Sees_The_Same_Mobile_As_Before_T1`, `UpsertMobile_Computes_Its_Values_Before_The_Writes`, `The_Body_Notoriety_And_Move_Operations_Equal_The_Old_Path` (0x77, 0x78, 0x20 × starts, four bodies each), `SetMobileBody_And_MoveMobile_Compute_Their_Values_Before_The_Writes`, `UpdateCharacter_Keeps_The_Handlers_Lookups_For_A_Rekeyed_Mobile` (a death-rekeyed `0x8000_3000` mobile with a corpse under the same serial: the notoriety goes to the mobile, UpdateGameObject's `World.Get` finds the item first, as before), `PlaceMobile_Needs_An_Outstanding_Mobile_Placement`, `Release_A_Bad_Mobile_Placement_Places_As_Before_T1`, `A_Mobile_Operation_Inside_An_Operation_Is_Rejected_Before_Any_Change` (5 operations × throw/release), `A_Mobile_This_World_Does_Not_Hold_Is_Rejected_Before_Any_Change` (4 × 2, foreign and stale), `RemoveMobile_Equals_The_Old_Path`, `RemoveMobile_Cancels_The_Placements_Of_The_Mobile_And_Its_Subtree`, `RemoveMobile_Rejects_Nesting_And_A_Mobile_This_World_Does_Not_Hold`, `The_Mobile_Fold_Skips_The_Hooks_Of_Its_Instance_Only`, `BodyState_Equals_The_Old_CheckGraphicChange` (graphics 0–0x500), `EnqueueStep_Equals_The_Old_EnqueueStep`, and `MobileFunnelCheckTests.The_Mobile_Operations_Make_No_Direct_Writes`. Compared per mobile: graphic, hue, position, direction, flags, sex, race, running, notoriety, offset, LastStepTime, IsPositionChanged, the walk queue element by element, `UpdateStateHash` (animation state and timers), the child list; per entity: the record, id, equipment-dirty/player/on-ground tags, `MobileInputs` (without `Pushes`) and `MobileClock`. Not covered by unit tests: the player's own branch of UpdateGameObject and the PlayerMobile callbacks (a PlayerMobile needs the UO files); the client gate covers them.
- **Mutations** (`muts_mobile.py`, 33 breakages of WorldWriter.cs, WorldEcs.cs and Mobile.cs, one filter `WorldWriterMobileTests|MobileFunnelCheckTests`). Round 1 on 234f906c4 (`mut_mobile_round1.log`): 28 fail a test, 4 survived and 1 did not compile. Survivors and fixes: a walk start with one queued step (no start had exactly one: added `Start.OneStep`); sex and race for an existing mobile (the mutation was equivalent: the writes sit in the creation block; replaced by one that applies BodyState outside it); SetNotoriety without its push (the body operation's push hid it: the world is now compared after the notoriety alone); SetMobileBody always writing the direction (the test passed direction 0 = the start's North: it now passes the packet's). The compile error (commit moved after the writes) is rebuilt as one block. Round 2 on cb1ba5bf9 (`mut_mobile.log`, rerun in full after the first run was killed mid-way): 32 of 33 fail a test, no compile error; one survived: the walk start with one queued step. Cause: `Start.OneStep` queued a step East from a mobile facing North, which is a turn step plus the move, so the queue held 2 steps and `Steps.Count <= 1` never differed from `== 0`. Fix: the start now queues one step in the facing direction (North to 1000,999) and throws if the queue does not hold exactly one step; with it the mutation fails 9 tests (`mut_mobile_round2b.log`, both `plan:` mutations rerun). All 33 now fail at least one test.
- **Gates (jobs on 234f906c4; the test-only changes after it do not change the binary).** `bench-000065` (client gate, pack classic-1.2: one run per script, `ls_parity`, `w5items`, `w5push`, each with `CUO_ECS_PARITY=1`, `-ecscheck 120`, `CUO_FUNNEL_CHECK=1`, `CUO_MOBILE_UPDATE_CHECK=1`, `CUO_MOBILE_INPUT_CHECK=1`; ModernUO listening on 2593) **passes**: `[ECS] check` mismatches 0 and no mismatch line in all three; parity items 1,755,752 checked (1,433,101 + 292,491 + 30,160), 0 mismatched, 0 drawn- or lights-mismatched; mobiles 13,272,950 (11,399,903 + 836,341 + 1,036,706), 0 mismatched, 0 not mirrored; mobile-update-check: clocks 30.5M checked, 0 different, skipped updates 0 changed, order 0 out of order, table differences 0; mobile-input-check: pushed samples 12.5M checked, 0 different (the folded pushes leave the inputs right). No `WorldWriter` line and no pre-T1 line. Direct writes (end of run): ls_parity 3,432,113, w5items 726,532, w5push 256,040 (63–66 sites each). **No site from `UpdateGameObject`, `UpdateCharacter`, `UpdateObject`, `UpdatePlayer` or `DeleteObject`** (part 3: `UpdateGameObject` 25, `UpdateObject` 16, `UpdateCharacter` 14, `EnqueueStep` 14 sites). What remains by caller over the three logs: `Mobile.ProcessSteps` 36, `CharacterStatus` 30, `Mobile.SetAnimation` 14, `Mobile.ProcessAnimation` 12, `GameObject.Destroy` 11, `Mobile.SetIdleAnimation` 9, `GameObject.SetInWorldTile` 9 (X/Y/Z: EnterWorld's and the walker's `SetInWorldTile`, not 0x20's), `NewHealthbarUpdate`/`MobileAttributes`/`EnterWorld`/`ProcessFootstepsSound` 6 each, `Mobile.CheckGraphicChange` 6 (IsFemale/Race: EnterWorld's 0x1B call, line 999), `CharacterAnimation` 5, `World.RemoveMobile` 4 (Container, Offset, Steps, LastAnimationChangeTime: the range sweep, not 0x1D), then 3 or fewer each (`World.RemoveItemFromContainer`, `PlayerMobile.Walk`, `Warmode`, `ConfirmWalk`, `Mobile.ClearSteps`/`ClearStepQueue`/`RemoveFirstStep`: the walker's DenyWalk, `Entity.Destroy`, `World.RemoveItem`, the stat updates, `DisplayDeath`, `CorpseEquipment`).
  `bench-000066` (E2 bench, base d7e063cd9 and new interleaved, 3 runs each, `DOTNET_TieredCompilation=0`, dev builds; median us/packet at 500 / 2000 / 8000 mobiles). **The ordering question from part 3 is settled:** with the four new rows after every older row, no unchanged row moves by more than twice the larger within-arm spread at any size (largest: 0x78 list rows, whose spreads are 0.18–0.40; `item into backpack (0x25) + out` −0.005 / +0.002 / −0.003 with spreads 0.011–0.021), so part 3's +0.03–0.05 shifts came from inserting rows before them, not from code. New rows (bytes 0 everywhere): 0x77 move of another mobile, old 0.112 / 0.117 / 0.121, funnel 0.170 / 0.174 / 0.173 (+0.052–0.058, within the +0.1 µs gate; spreads ≤ 0.03; the extra cost is the second operation's admission, scope and lookups and the placement token, while the ECS work is lower: one input push fewer); 0x78 player body, old 0.090 / 0.092 / 0.095, funnel 0.079 / 0.083 / 0.084 (faster: one push instead of three). Noise: the first mutation run (test builds under agentnice) was running during both jobs; within-arm spreads are listed above.
- **Verification (final head, after the `Start.OneStep` fix):** 1775 pass + 2 skipped in both `CuoDevTools` variants (1669 + 106 mobile tests). Both client builds succeed (0 errors). Write-site budget 253 (unchanged since 234f906c4). No new client job: the changes after 234f906c4 are tests and docs only, so bench-000065 still covers the binary.

### T1 funnel part 4: Codex audit and dispositions (2026-10-31, audit of bf450e820; fixes 78a85f284)

Codex (gpt-6-astra) found one P2 and two P3, no P0/P1. All three fixed.

- **P2, player placement suppressed callback-triggered movement.** `PlaceMobile` folded the mobile around `SetInWorldTile`, which runs `PlayerMobile.OnPositionChanged`; a plugin's `RequestMove` there runs `Player.Walk` synchronously (step queue, timers, a turn). Its input and clock pushes and the Direction Sync were skipped and nothing published afterwards, so W5 inputs, E4 clocks and the record's facing could stay stale. The same held for `MoveMobile` (0x20): its final `CommitMobileInputs` repaired inputs and clock, but not a turn's facing in the record. **Fix:** both open their scope without a fold (`Open(mobile, null)`), so the callbacks' pushes and Syncs and the tile's own Sync publish as before T1. The operation's own commits stay. Cost: every mobile placement runs the tile's Sync again (one mirror upsert plus the inputs/clock write per 0x77/0x78 placement). That was the pre-T1 cost; the E2 rows of bench-000066 (0x77 funnel +0.05 µs over old) predate this and were not re-measured.
  - *Seam:* `TestPlayer`, a `PlayerMobile` made with `RuntimeHelpers.GetUninitializedObject` and then `Mobile`'s constructor (the PlayerMobile constructor reads the UO files; Skills/Walker/Pathfinder stay unset and are not touched), set as `World.Player` by reflection. Its `OnPositionChanged`/`OnDirectionChanged` are the test's: the real ones call the plugins and read the profile. The callback is a stand-in for `Player.Walk`'s writes (a turn plus a queued step with `LastStepTime`, `SetAnimation` and the push), not the real `Walk` (that needs the walker, the pathfinder and the profile).
  - *Test:* `A_Walk_From_The_Players_Position_Callback_Is_Published_As_Before_T1` (0x78-style `UpsertMobile`+`PlaceMobile` on the player, which is also the first unit coverage of UpdateGameObject's player branch; and 0x20's `SetMobileBody`+`MoveMobile`), compared with the old path on a second World (record, tags, inputs, clock, queue, state hash).
- **P3, `PlaceInContainer` on a mobile serial bypassed the placement cancellation.** It called `World.RemoveMobile` directly, so the tokens of the mobile and its equipment survived. **Fix:** RemoveMobile's body is now `RemoveMobileSubtree` (cancel the subtree's placements, own the subtree, remove), used by both; it runs only for a live held mobile, as `World.RemoveMobile` did. *Test:* `PlaceInContainer_Of_A_Mobile_Serial_Cancels_The_Placements_Of_The_Mobile_And_Its_Subtree` (a retained mobile token and a retained token of an item in its worn backpack; both are rejected afterwards).
- **P3, the detached `World.Player`.** A 0x25 under the player's serial removes the player's mobile while `World.Player` stays; 0x78 and 0x20 in the same burst pass `World.Player` itself, which the operations rejected (dev: throw; release: body and move skipped). **Fix:** `SetMobileBody` and `MoveMobile` accept that exact instance (`IsDetachedPlayer`: `World.Player`, same World, not held) and write it unfolded. Nothing of it reaches the ECS (every commit, Sync and push ignores an instance World does not hold), so this is the pre-T1 path, including the position callbacks; no violation is counted. Admission and the rejection of every other not-held instance stay. *Test:* `The_Detached_World_Player_Is_Written_As_Before_T1` (throw and release modes: 0x78 then 0x20 on the detached player against the old writes; then a stranger instance is still rejected by both operations). 0x77 is unaffected (it looks the mobile up in `World.Mobiles`).
- **Revert check** (`revert.py`, each fix reverted alone, filter `WorldWriterMobile`, dev build): PlaceMobile fold back → `A_Walk…(UpdateObject)` fails; MoveMobile fold back → `A_Walk…(UpdatePlayer)` fails; direct `World.RemoveMobile` back → the PlaceInContainer test fails; `IsDetachedPlayer` → false → both cases of the detached-player test fail.
- **Verification (78a85f284):** 1780 pass + 2 skipped in both `CuoDevTools` variants (1775 + 5 new). Both client builds 0 errors. Write-site budget unchanged (253: no new direct write; the detached-player path reuses the operations' writes).
- **Gate:** `bench-000068` (the bench-000065 job rerun on 78a85f284, dev build, pack classic-1.3 (CURRENT has moved since 000065's classic-1.2); ModernUO listening on 2593) **passes** with the same numbers checked: `[ECS] check` mismatches 0 and no mismatch line in all three scripts; parity items 1,906,389 (1,494,135 + 342,510 + 69,744), 0 mismatched, 0 drawn- or lights-mismatched; mobiles 13,388,482 (10,883,239 + 973,103 + 1,532,140), 0 mismatched, 0 not mirrored; mobile-update-check: clocks 29.4M checked, 0 different, skipped updates 0 changed, order 0 out of order, table differences 0, no warning; mobile-input-check: pushed samples 12.5M checked, 0 different; no `WorldWriter` line and no pre-T1 line. Direct writes 3,317,504 / 750,042 / 237,528 (81 / 65 / 72 sites logged). Still no site from `UpdateGameObject`, `UpdateCharacter`, `UpdateObject`, `UpdatePlayer` or `DeleteObject`; the callers are those of bench-000065 (`World.RemoveMobile` 5 sites, the range sweep's, e.g. AnimIndex at World.cs:1191 in Destroy).

## T1 funnel, part 5: EnterWorld, the walker, the step completion, the range sweep (2026-10-31, `bg/ecs-t1-funnel-5`)

Base `poc/modern-client` 072f9a6f8 (part 4 merged). Commits 4d54543ea (group 1: EnterWorld), faf61d425 (group 2: the walker and the step completion), bc649e272 (group 3: the range sweep). Plan: ecs-transition-plan.md, T1. The audit rules of parts 1–4 applied from the start (admission before side effects; values computed before the first write; no read-back; captured instances; the old lookups; subtree placement cancellation; no fold around callbacks or plugins; documented release behaviour).

- **Group 1, EnterWorld (0x1B), 4d54543ea.** New `SetMobileGraphic` (the body graphic and `CheckGraphicChange`'s sex and race; folded, no callback runs in those setters) and `SetMobileDirection` (the record is committed with the new direction, then the setter runs **unfolded**: the player's door check can send a packet, so plugin send hooks run; then the derived inputs). 0x1B is now `SetMobileGraphic` → (map, prefetch as before) → `MoveMobile` (part 4's, unfolded around the position callbacks) → `SetMobileDirection`. Both accept the detached `World.Player` (written as before T1) and reject every other instance World does not hold (no pre-T1 path). Budget 253 → 251 (`PacketHandlers.cs` Direction 2 → 1, Graphic 3 → 2).
- **Group 2, the walker and the step completion, faf61d425.**
  - `StopMobile`: `WalkerManager.DenyWalk`'s `ClearSteps` (0x21 and 0x20's deny), folded; DenyWalk's move is `MoveMobile`. 0x21's direction is `SetMobileDirection`; 0x22's notoriety is `SetNotoriety`, which now accepts the detached player too. `ConfirmWalk` itself writes no A field (walker state and `RangeSize` only); 0x22's `AddToTile` stays (its Sync publishes the same record).
  - `CompleteStep`: the `removeStep` block of `Mobile.ProcessSteps` (position, direction, run state, the member-wise offset reset, `RemoveFirstStep`, the idle timer; unless a turn in place: `UpdateScreenPosition`, the player's `CloseRangedGumps`, the tile re-add, `LastStepTime`). One record commit first from the step's values, then the cache in the old order, then the inputs. A mobile other than the player is folded (none of its setters or helpers runs a callback): per completed step, the old path's Syncs (Direction, UpdateScreenPosition, AddToTile), two input pushes and a clock push become one commit and one push. The player is **not** folded (door check, the plugins' position callback, `CloseRangedGumps`), and its inputs are also committed before the callbacks, where the old code pushed. ProcessSteps passes its own instance: a stale instance is written as before T1 (unfolded; the ECS ignores it); only another World's mobile is a violation (rejected, the step stays queued). The turn-in-place recursion runs after the operation returns (no nesting). The per-frame offset interpolation (the non-completing branch) and `SetAnimation(0xFF)` stay direct (animation group).
  - Budget 251 → 239 (`Mobile.cs` Direction 1 → 0, IsRunning 1 → 0, LastStepTime 2 → 1, Offset 7 → 4, Steps 5 → 4, X/Y/Z 1 → 0 each; `PacketHandlers.cs` Direction 1 → 0, NotorietyFlag 1 → 0).
- **Group 3, the range sweep, bc649e272.** `SweepMobile`/`SweepItem` replace `World.Update`'s out-of-range `RemoveMobile(mob)`/`RemoveItem(item)` (the legacy mobile loop, the E4 clock path, both item loops; no force, so the destroyed objects stay in their tables until the frame's destroyed lists drop them, as before). Removals like part 4's `RemoveMobile`: own the removed subtree, write no value, no fold, cancel the placements of the object and its whole subtree first. A destroyed held object is a no-op (the old removal returned false) and no violation; a not-held instance is rejected (no pre-T1 path). `Clear`/`InternalMapChangeClear` keep `World.Remove*` (resets, not the sweep). Budget unchanged (239): the removals' writes are in `Destroy`, now owned at run time.
- **Tests** (`WorldWriterMobileTests.Part5.cs`, the part-4 class made partial; old copies `OldEnterWorld`, `OldDenyWalk`, `OldCompleteStep`): `EnterWorld_Equals_The_Old_Path` (3 starts × 4 entries), `EnterWorld_On_The_Player_Publishes_Its_Callbacks_As_Before_T1` (`TestPlayer` gains `OnTurned`, a stand-in for the door check's packet), `SetMobileGraphic_And_SetMobileDirection_Compute_Their_Values_Before_The_Writes`, `SetMobileGraphic_Alone_Leaves_The_Ecs_As_A_Sync_Of_The_Old_Writes`, `DenyWalk_And_ConfirmWalk_Equal_The_Old_Path` (4 starts × 3 denies), `WalkerManager_DenyWalk_Goes_Through_The_Funnel_As_The_Old_Path` (a real `WalkerManager` on the TestPlayer), `CompleteStep_Equals_The_Old_Step_Completion` (3 starts, parked and unparked: these Worlds have no map, so a parked `PendingBlock` stands in for a placement and shows whether `AddToTile` ran), `CompleteStep_Of_The_Player_Publishes_Its_Callbacks_As_Before_T1` (incl. the inputs the position callback sees), `CompleteStep_Computes_Its_Values_Before_The_Writes`, `CompleteStep_Writes_A_Stale_Instance_As_Before_T1_And_Rejects_Another_Worlds`, `A_Step_Completion_Inside_An_Operation_Is_Rejected_Before_Any_Change`, `The_Walker_And_EnterWorld_Operations_Write_The_Detached_Player_As_Before_T1`, `The_Sweep_Removals_Equal_The_Old_Path` (5 starts incl. destroyed-but-held), `The_Sweep_Cancels_The_Placements_Of_The_Removed_Subtrees`, `The_Sweep_Rejects_Nesting_And_An_Object_This_World_Does_Not_Hold`, the part-4 nesting and not-held theories extended to the new operations, and `WalkFunnelCheckTests` (no direct writes under `CUO_FUNNEL_CHECK`). Not unit-tested: the call sites in `ProcessSteps` and `World.Update` (ProcessSteps reads `Client.Game.FrameDelay`; World.Update needs a map and a player); the client gate covers them.
- **Mutations** (scratch `t1-funnel-5`: `muts_part5.py`, `muts_sweep.py`, logs `mut_part5.log`, `mut_part5_round2.log`, `mut_sweep.log`): round 1, 24 breakages of the group 1–2 operations and `WalkerManager`: 21 failed a test, 3 survived: `SetMobileGraphic` without its inputs commit and with a wrong record direction (0x1B's `MoveMobile` commits again right after; fixed by `SetMobileGraphic_Alone_…`, which compares the operation alone with a Sync of the old writes), and the player's mid-step input commit (the callback's own push hid it; fixed by recording the inputs the position callback sees). ## Stress scene: 7,500 Balrons, results (2026-10-31, `poc/balron-stress`)

Measure only, no client code change. Base `poc/modern-client` 072f9a6f8; both arms of ours are the same NativeAOT publish of 072f9a6f8, upstream is ClassicUO main ee79d7ebc (NativeAOT). Method, spawn and wipe: large-scale.md, "Stress scene: 7,500 Balrons". Jobs: bench-000070 (spawn, 7,500 Balrons, AI on, Felucca 5140..5171 × 2214..2245), bench-000071 (gpu-tp1, upstream up-login1, gpu-login1, gpu-walk1), bench-000072 (legacy-login1, legacy-tp1, gpu-tp2, up-login2, legacy-tp2), bench-000073 (wipe). All ok. RTX 3090 Ti, client pinned to the P-cores; ModernUO on the same machine at about one core while a client was among the Balrons.

- **Survival:** every run survived. Ours: 6 of 6 standing runs plus the walk, exit 0, never unresponsive. Upstream: 2 of 2 reached the world within 2 s, answered `WM_NULL` every second for the full 150 s, kept private bytes at 1.4–1.6 GB, and closed cleanly at the cap. **The upstream stall-and-crash was not reproduced** in a login among already-spawned Balrons; it was not tested with upstream present during the spawn itself. No 300 s upstream run is proposed: it was not stalling at the cap.
- **Owner's observation:** no crash; fps dipped to about 39 during the spawn and settled at about 240 within seconds. This matches the logs: login and teleport-in show 60–150 frames over 16 ms in the first 12 s (worst 23–103 ms), then 182–236 fps standing. The network caps stay at their defaults (128 KB / 1,500 packets / 4 ms per frame; owner: hardware-dependent).

**Results** (standing windows `bal`, 12 × 5 s; 2 reps per arm, interleaved; ms per frame):

| run | survives | entry stall (longest frame, ms) | p50 / p95 / p99 | fps | mobiles in range | packets/s | private MB peak | GC by +60 s (gen2), pause | GPU world |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| gpu-tp1 | yes | 44 | 5.07 / 6.76 / 8.65 | 194 | 7,320 | 1,307 | 3,005 (anim layers grown to 128 after the TestScene) | 24 (6), 92 ms | 1,728 baked + 17.8k dynamic, 2 draws |
| gpu-tp2 | yes | 39 | 4.35 / 5.89 / 6.99 | 213 | 6,582 | 1,382 | 2,291 | 30 (8), 122 ms | 1,728 + 16.5k |
| gpu-login1 | yes | 55 | 4.71 / 6.14 / 7.34 | 236 | 5,858 | 1,414 | 2,164 | 22 (8), 80 ms | 1,728 + 14.0k |
| legacy-tp1 | yes | 36 | 4.96 / 6.95 / 8.32 | 192 | 6,666 | 1,366 | 1,746 | 30 (10), 105 ms | – (45 draw calls) |

Packets/s is the client's `net_packets` counter over the windows (about 15 KB/s; the packets phase is 0.05–0.07 ms per frame); the Uo.Net.Cli count failed (the server closed the connection at the server list). Standing: at most one gen0 per 60 s, 400–860 B allocated per frame. Long frames while standing: 439 ms (gpu-login1), 384 and 87 ms (gpu-tp2), 112 ms (legacy-login1); in each the frame's measured work was under 8 ms (`work_max` 7.6–8.0 ms against `cpu_max` = the frame), so the time went outside every instrumented phase. Not renderer work; cause unknown (shared machine, server on the same box). gpu-walk1 (driver walk with `-ecscheck`): 325 fps walking among about 5,000, ECS checks 0 mismatches.

**Noise.** Within-arm spread of frame p50 is 17 % (Gpu tp) and 20 % (Legacy tp), above the 5 % threshold, and the scene drifts: the Balrons wander off (7,320 in range in the first run, 6,357 in the last), so run order is confounded with load. **The data cannot show Legacy faster than Gpu, or the reverse.** Normalised per mobile in range the arms tie: whole frame 0.70–0.72 µs per mobile (Gpu) vs 0.67–0.81 (Legacy); world prepare + world draw 0.42–0.43 µs vs 0.44–0.49.

**Phases per renderer** (window averages, ms per frame; Gpu tp1 / tp2 / login, Legacy tp1 / tp2 / login):

| phase | Gpu | Legacy |
