- **Item cache invalidation from moving mobiles:** none. There are no ground items, `item_cache_builds` is 0 and the phase costs 3 µs.
- **Instance upload vs draw:** not separable with these phases; both are inside Gpu's world draw (0.48–0.58 ms together). About 18k dynamic instances × 72 B ≈ 1.3 MB written per frame.

**Why Gpu does not win here, the opposite of the frozen large scene.** The GPU path wins the frozen scene by baking: land and statics into chunk meshes and 11k+ ground items into the item cache, so most of its 21k objects cost nothing per frame. Here nothing is static: the view is 5,000–7,400 animated, wandering Balrons on bare grass (1,728 baked land instances). Every visible Balron is re-extracted from the ECS each frame (about 0.27 µs each, 3 instances: 1.3–1.7 ms) and uploaded again; Legacy spends the same per-sprite CPU time in its batcher instead (2.3–2.6 ms). The GPU path's other advantage, 2 draw calls instead of 45, buys nothing on this GPU (present 0.17 ms in both). So the two arms do the same O(mobiles) CPU work and tie. If the owner's interactive run saw Legacy ahead, the measured candidates are Gpu's extra per-frame extract plus upload (which grows with fps: about 260 MB/s of instance writes at 200 fps) and a different number of Balrons in view between the two looks; these runs can't tell which.

**Fixes, ranked (not implemented):**
1. **Reuse each mobile's instances between frames (Gpu).** A Balron's animation frame changes about every 100 ms and the client draws every 4–5 ms, so about 95 % of extracts rebuild the same sprites. Keep each mobile's last instances with a key (graphic, frame, direction, hue, flags, z) and on a hit only rewrite the screen offset. Expected: prep_cap_mobile 1.3–1.7 → about 0.3–0.5 ms, roughly 20–25 % of this frame.
2. **Persistent dynamic instance buffer with dirty ranges (Gpu).** Give each mobile a stable slot and upload only changed slots instead of 1.3 MB per frame. Builds on 1; the gain is part of world draw's 0.5 ms plus GPU bandwidth.
3. **`HealthLinesManager.Draw` walks all of `World.Mobiles` every frame** (7,000+ here) and checks whether health lines are enabled only inside the loop. Both arms: part of scene DrawUI's 0.7–1.1 ms. Iterate only the mobiles that can show a line (target and selection, plus those in view when ShowMobilesHP is on).
4. **Text per mobile** (prep_text 0.15–0.24 and world_fx_text 0.17–0.28 ms, both arms): skip mobiles with no text instead of visiting all of them.

**"need more data ID: 78/DC/17" warnings: benign.** Count per run (all IDs; top four): gpu-tp1 589 (C1 117, 78 95, D6 83, DC 80), gpu-tp2 758 (C1 273, 11 125, D6 113, 78 102), gpu-login1 318, gpu-walk1 278, legacy-tp1 722, legacy-tp2 499, legacy-login1 297, wipe 481; upstream up-login1 368, up-login2 249. 78/DC/17 dominate at login (the incoming-mobile burst), then C1/D6/11 (cliloc messages, property lists, status). They come from `PacketHandlers.ParseQueue` (src/ClassicUO.Client/Network/PacketHandlers.cs:152): the buffered stream ends inside a packet (a TCP segment or drain-slice boundary), the loop logs a warning and breaks, and the partial packet stays in the circular buffer until the next read completes it. The 10–41 `Invalid ID: xx | len: -1 | stream.pos: 1–2` lines per run are the same case for a variable-length packet whose 2 length bytes have not arrived yet (`GetPacketInfo` returns false with fewer than 3 bytes buffered). Nothing is dropped: no `Malformed packet`, no protocol error or disconnect in any run, ECS checks 0 mismatches, and upstream has the same code and similar counts. Only the log level is wrong (fix 5).

Same Balrons, interleaved, so the drift cancels. Both need the Balrons again: the scene was wiped, so this means respawning with bench-000070's recipe and wiping afterwards (owner decision). ## Stationary Balron scene: a spawner with CantWalk (2026-10-31, `poc/balron-spawner`)

Owner request: "create a spawner, 7500 balrons, under properties do cantwalk true and homerange of the spawner as 32", later corrected to **HomeRange 16** (33×33, the old footprint). Renderer A/B dropped from this stage (owner); docs only, no client change. Base `poc/modern-client` 3fc8c4e4e. Recipe, location and removal: large-scale.md, "Stationary Balron scene (spawner)".

- **Created** in bench-000076 (ok, 126 s) with `[ImportSpawners temp/balron-spawner.json`. The file is `C:/Repositories/cuo-poc-state/scenes/balron-spawner.json`: Spawner `BalronStressScene`, Felucca 5156 2230 0, count 7,500, entry Balron ×7,500 with properties `CantWalk true`, homeRange 16. It generated 1 spawner in 0.81 s. `[Global Count where Balron` went from 222 to 7,722; `[Area Count where Balron` over 5140..5172 × 2214..2246 went from 0 to 7,500, all with `CantWalk == true`. The client at 5156 2230 counted 7,501 mobiles in range, and again after leaving and returning. It stayed responsive throughout, with private bytes peaking at 2.86 GB. The spawner stays in place.
- **Why the JSON import:** entry Properties are set only by the spawner gump, `[EditSpawner` and the importers. The DevBench driver can't fill gump text fields, and SpawnerEntry has no `[Set`-able properties.
- **ModernUO findings (not changed; the predictions came from the source):**
  1. *CantWalk spawns all land on the spawner's tile.* Confirmed: the 7,500 Balrons stand on the single tile 5156,2230, not spread over the 33×33. `BaseSpawner.Spawn` sets the entry properties before `GetSpawnPosition`. `Map.CanSpawnMobile` grants a land or static surface only when `!cantWalk`. Every try therefore fails as non-transient, the spawner falls back to `Location`, and after 25 misses (`SpawnPositionState.AbandonThreshold`) it marks itself `Abandoned`. That is probably a bug for land mobiles with CantWalk set in an entry, such as stationary NPC spawns: the check looks meant for water mobiles (`isWaterMob = canSwim && cantWalk`). Even without CantWalk, a spawner can't place more than one mobile per tile (mobiles block z ±16), so at most 1,089 fit in 33×33 and the overflow also goes to the spawner's tile.
  2. *`[EditSpawner <type> set <props>` can't work* (predicted, not run). `EditSpawnCommand` takes `props = argSpan[start..^len]` with `len = argSpan.Length` when there's no `where`, which is the range `[start..0]` and throws ArgumentOutOfRange. With `where`, the slice ends at `Length − whereIndex` instead of `whereIndex`. Expected `argSpan[start..len]`.
- **What HomeRange means:** HomeRange *n* gives a (2*n*+1)² square centred on the spawner, ends inclusive: 16 → 33×33, and 32 would have been 65×65. WalkingRange −1 falls back to HomeRange, and each spawned creature gets `RangeHome = WalkingRange` and `Home = spawner location`.
- **CantWalk and motion:** the Balrons never change tile; `Movement.CheckMovement` rejects land for CantWalk. While a player is in range their AI still runs: `BaseAI.DoMoveImpl` sets `Direction` before the failed step, so they turn, send direction updates and animate. That still loads the network, but nothing drifts.
- **Stragglers:** none inside the new square before the spawn. About 184 Balrons from the earlier stress spawn are still alive somewhere (222 world-wide against 38 before it; AI on). Left alone, per the owner.
- **Open for the owner:** the scene as built is a 7,500-Balron *stack* on one tile, stationary and reproducible. To get the old 32×32 spread and keep it stationary, either `[TileXYZ` the 7,500 as before and then `[Area Set CantWalk true` over the square (the result isn't tied to a spawner), or patch ModernUO's `CanSpawnMobile` and still accept one Balron per tile. Not done; the owner decides.

## T1 funnel, part 8: the idle animation, the footstep sound, the corpse frame, the walk queue, logout's removals, the container clamp (2026-10-31, `bg/ecs-t1-funnel-8`)

Base `poc/modern-client` 9ade17d63 (part 7 merged). Commits 12bd71e23 (group 1: idle animation, footstep sound), b5283af68 (group 2: the corpse frame), c6ee84a80 (group 3: a server animation a step ends), 51ae8467d (group 4: the player's walk queue), 8e130aa43 (group 5: logout's removals), 8110727e3 (group 6: the gump-side write), 1bf22f791 (group 5 test follow-up), then these docs. Plan: ecs-transition-plan.md, T1. The audit rules of parts 1–7 applied (admission before side effects, values before writes, old write order, captured instances, no fold around callbacks, the player unfolded). Every new operation is unfolded and commits nothing beyond what the old path pushed.

- **Group 1, the idle animation and the footstep sound (12bd71e23).** `SetIdleAnimation` splits into `Mobile.PlanIdleAnimation` (reads the mobile and the animation data through the new `Mobile.IIdleAnimationData`, a struct-constrained generic so the live adapter does not box; draws the random numbers in the old order: the idle delay, then a gargoyle's flight or the idle pair; writes nothing) and the `IdleAnimation` operation (`Mobile.ApplyIdle`: the idle due time and its clock push, the timer reset, then the group, or `SetAnimation` of the group the mobile had when neither idle action exists, which draws its own idle delay last, as before). The old code wrote the group up to three times before its final value; nothing read the intermediate values, so the plan writes the final one. `ProcessFootstepsSound` computes the sound, the offset and the due time, writes the offset then the due time through `StepSound`, and plays the sound after it returns true (the sound reads neither field; before T1 it played between the two writes; a rejected call plays nothing). Admission for the per-frame operations of part 8 (`PerFrameAdmitted`, as `InterpolateStep`'s): no operation or fold open; a stale instance of this World is written as before T1; another World's is a violation, rejected. Budget 156 → 147 (`Mobile.cs` `_animationGroup` 9 → 2, `LastStepSoundTime`, `StepSoundOffset` 1 → 0).
- **Group 2, a corpse's frame (b5283af68).** `Item.ProcessAnimation` reads the corpse frame from the animation data as before and writes the frame (when there is one) and the next due time through `AdvanceCorpseFrame`, in the old order. Budget 147 → 145 (`Item.cs` AnimIndex 2 → 1, LastAnimationChangeTime 1 → 0; the remaining AnimIndex write is `Item.Destroy`).
- **Group 3, a server animation a step ends (c6ee84a80).** `ProcessSteps`' `SetAnimation(0xFF)` for a mobile whose server animation a queued step ends is `EndServerAnimation` (SetAnimation's own clock push, as before). This was the last unconverted per-frame mobile site part 7 reported. Budget unchanged (a call).
- **Group 4, the player's walk queue (51ae8467d; reworked by the Codex audit fix b816cd849, below).** `PlayerMobile.Walk` computes its queue writes as a `StepPlan` (`PlanWalkStep`: the step; for an empty queue the walk start, with `SetAnimation(0xFF)` if the player is not walking) and writes them through `QueuePlayerStep` (`Mobile.ApplyStep`, the same mutation half `UpsertMobile` uses, in a scope owning the player, unfolded) before the walker records and sends the step: the walker is not world state and neither side reads the other, so moving the step's record after the queue write changes nothing observable; a rejection (not this World's player, nesting) returns false before the walker changes. Since the audit fix `QueuePlayerStep` takes the step and runs admission, then `CloseBank` (the caller's removals, unchanged and unscoped), then the plan and the writes, and the coalesced turn (three unconfirmed requests) is `TurnPlayer` (SetMobileDirection's writes with the walk's admission) through `PlayerMobile.CoalescedTurn`, which returns false without the cooldown when it is rejected. Budget 145 → 142 (`PlayerMobile.cs` Direction, LastStepTime, Steps 1 → 0).
- **Group 5, logout's removals (8e130aa43).** `World.Clear`'s two loops (every mobile, then every item, removed and destroyed without force) are `ClearWorld`: the outstanding placements cancelled, then the old loops in a scope that owns every object of this World (`Owns` is true for any entity while it is open; reset when the scope closes). The rest of `Clear` is unchanged. A nested call is rejected (nothing removed; Clear then empties the tables and `OnWorldCleared` resets the mirror). Budget unchanged (calls).

  - *P2 #1, a walk from the player's callbacks was rejected.* Confirmed: `SetInWorldTile`/`UpdateScreenPosition` → `PlayerMobile.OnPositionChanged` → `Plugin.UpdatePlayerPosition` → a plugin → `Plugin.RequestMove` → `Player.Walk` runs synchronously inside `MoveMobile`, `PlaceMobile` (the player), `CompleteStep` (the player) and `MoveBoatPassenger`, and the door check (`OnDirectionChanged` → `TryOpenDoors` → `GameActions.OpenDoor`, the plugins' send hooks) inside `SetMobileDirection`. Part 8 made Walk call `QueuePlayerStep` and `SetMobileDirection`, which nested (dev: throw; release: rejected, the movement lost; the coalesced turn still returned true with its cooldown; `CloseBank` ran before the rejection). **Fix (b816cd849): a narrowly scoped, documented allowance**, not the split the audit suggested. `WorldWriter.AdmittedPlayerWalk`, used only by `QueuePlayerStep` and the new `TurnPlayer` (the coalesced turn), lets the walk join the open operation when that operation's subject is this exact instance and nothing is folded; the caller's player check (this World's `World.Player`) follows, still before any side effect; anything else nests and is rejected as before. A joined walk opens no scope of its own, so the outer scope, its ownership (the walk's writes are its funnel writes) and its deferred boat clears stay as they are. *Why not the split:* each callback sits inside a `GameObject` method between writes of the same operation (`SetInWorldTile`: X, Y, Z, callback, `AddToTile`; `UpdateScreenPosition`: the flag, callback, Sync; the Direction setter: the field, callback, Sync), so running it with no scope open would split `GameObject`'s position and direction primitives into three parts in five operations, or change the order the plugins observe; the continuation after the callback would be a separately admitted operation built from values computed before the callback, which is exactly what the old code did and what the joined walk reproduces. The allowance keeps the pre-T1 order exactly (the walk writes at the moment the old Walk wrote, with the same pushes and Syncs) and is local to one call chain on one object. What it relies on, checked for the four operations and `SetMobileDirection`: after their callback they commit only from the getters (`CommitMobileInputs`) and through the hook Syncs (from the cache), never values computed before the callback, so a T4 move of the getters keeps them right; the operations that fold the player run no callback. This reverses part 4's disposition only in admission: the operations stay unfolded around the callbacks as part 4 decided. `QueuePlayerStep` now takes the step: admission and the player check, then `CloseBank` (unscoped, the caller's removals as before), then `PlanWalkStep` and `ApplyStep`; Walk's coalesced turn is `CoalescedTurn` (`TurnPlayer`, then the cooldown; false and no cooldown when rejected). `TurnPlayer` commits the record with the new direction, then runs the setter unfolded, whose Sync writes the inputs, the old turn's one push (711f350b7 removed a second inputs commit that the old path never made; its mutant had survived).

Walk itself (the walker, the pathfinder, the network) stays client-gate only; no gate script has a plugin that walks from a callback.

## T1 funnel, part 9: the value-taking re-key, the last removal sites, -ecscheck v2, the child-order stamps, uistate.txt (2026-10-31, `bg/ecs-t1-funnel-9`)

Base `poc/modern-client` 9b071c834 (part 8 merged). Commits 6e1bb0e56 (group 1: the value-taking re-key), 0c9040739 (group 2: the removal sites), 5d029ac99 (groups 3 and 4 in one commit, their code is intertwined: -ecscheck v2 and the child-order stamps), f4fd87538 (groups 3/4 test follow-up), 243e7b089 (group 5: uistate.txt and its driver commands) and these docs. Plan: ecs-transition-plan.md, T1. The audit rules of parts 1–8 applied (admission before side effects, values before writes, the old write order, captured instances, no fold around callbacks, the player unfolded).

- **Group 1, the value-taking re-key (6e1bb0e56).** `RekeyDeadMobile` now commits the ECS first, from values, as every other operation: the record under the new serial (`MobileState` from the getters with `Serial = serial | 0x80000000`) through the new `WorldEcs.CommitRekey` (the hold check under the old serial; the old record removed; the record written; the persistent mirror bit carried over; a destroyed held mobile only loses its old record, as Sync skipped it), then each child's `CommitItem` with the new Container; then the cache writes in the old order (out of the table, each child's Container, into the table, the Serial); then the derived inputs and clock from the getters (`CommitMobileInputs(mobile, e)`, what `OnSerialChanged`'s Sync pushed). Nothing reads the serial, the table or a Container back. `OnSerialChanged` stays only for the tests' old-path copies. T4's open question from part 7 is closed. Budget unchanged (the writes are the operation's).
- **Group 2, the removal sites outside the converted callers (0c9040739).** Part 8's gate traced its only direct writes (Item.Destroy's Graphic, Hue, Offset, AnimIndex, LastAnimationChangeTime) to `World.RemoveItem` from callers its two-level trace cut off. The funnel check's caller now goes past the removal plumbing (`Destroy` on any GameObject, `World.RemoveItem`/`RemoveMobile`/`RemoveContentsAndDestroy`/`RemoveDetachedItem`/`RemoveItemFromContainer`) and names the method that asked for the removal: `[funnel] direct write <field> at <writer> via <caller> from <origin>`. The four production callers (DevBench's chair aside) are operations: `RemoveBankContents` (`PlayerMobile.CloseBank`, from 0x20 and from the walk: admission as the walk's, so a walk from the player's position callback that closes the bank joins the open operation on the player, as `QueuePlayerStep` does; the player check; the bank's subtree owned; a rejection removes nothing and `CloseBank` then leaves the bank open), `RemovePickedUpItem` (`World.Update`'s `ObjectToRemove`, the item `GameActions.PickUp` lifted), `ClearForMapChange` (`World.InternalMapChangeClear`, the old body as `World.MapChangeRemovals` in a scope that owns the World, as `ClearWorld`; its `Player.Destroy` branch is unreachable, the only caller passes `noplayer: true`, but it runs inside the scope too) and `ClearForLogin` (`LoginScene`'s reset between login steps). Each cancels the removed objects' placements (the map change only those of what it destroyed; the player's kept items keep theirs). Budget unchanged (the Destroy writes are in GameObject/Entity/Item, unchanged; the converted callers wrote no field themselves).
- **Groups 3 and 4, -ecscheck v2 and the child-order stamps (5d029ac99, f4fd87538).** New mirror components (ClassicUO.Ecs): `EntityName`, `Vitals` (Hits, HitsMax), `MobileNotoriety`, `ItemPrice`, `ItemLayer` (every item, from every item commit; `EquippedOn.Layer` stays the worn layer) and `ChildOrder` (a monotonic stamp). The first four are added on the first non-default write (absent = the GameObject default), so most records do not change archetype. The funnel commits them from its values before its cache writes: `SetName` and `SetStatus` the name, `SetHits` and `SetStatus` the vitals, `SetNotoriety` the notoriety, `SetPrice` the price, every item commit the layer; each ignores an entity World does not hold (the detached player) or without a record. The child-order stamp: after each `PushToBack` of a held item (`PlaceInContainer`, `ReturnHeldItem`'s paperdoll branch, `Equip`, `WearItem`, `PlaceCorpseEquipment`; `FillSpellbook`'s spell items are detached and get none) the item takes the next stamp, so a parent's mirror children (worn and contained) sorted by stamp are the GameObject child list (arrival order, a re-push to the back). The death re-key carries the name, hits and notoriety (the operation and the old `OnSerialChanged`). `-ecscheck` compares, per check: every item's layer, name, hits and price; every mobile's name, hits and notoriety; every parent's held children in list order against the mirror's by stamp (children World does not hold are skipped). Memory: the new components exist only on records that have the value; ItemLayer is 1 byte per item record (25k items: about 25 KB plus Friflo's per-archetype column, well under 1 MB per client); the check's two lists are reused.
- **Group 5, uistate.txt (243e7b089).** The plan's T1 gate script, `tools/ecs-parity/uistate.txt` (main client, kbatman3, at 5445 1153) with `uistate_partner.txt` (a second client on kbatman2, one tile east, under a `kbatman2.lock` in the session scratchpad; skipped when the lock is held or `kbatman2.owner-hold` exists). New driver commands: `pick pack|bank <graphic> [amount]`, `pick layer <n>`, `drop bank|container <graphic>|mobile <dx> <dy>`, `use near <graphic>`, `target pack|near|mine <graphic>`, `target named <text>`, `contents`, `find`, `worn`, `buy`, `named`, `status`, `rename`, `trade accept|log` (all `[ECS] ui ...` lines). After the fixes (warmup one full pass in both arms; the base test binary built from 9b071c834 with the same warmup patch, uncommitted in the base worktree), `bench-000099` (base 9b071c834 vs new dea7562a9, 3 runs each interleaved, TieredCompilation=0, pinned): all 111 rows within +0.1 µs (largest +0.138 µs on the *old-path* 0x78 row at 8,000, inside its 2× spread of 11 %; funnel 0x78 rows +0.015/+0.026/+0.057 µs), allocated bytes equal on all 111 rows. Beyond 2× the within-arm spread: `SetHits` +0.012 µs (+50 %, the Vitals commit: one table check, one lookup, one write) and 0x77 at 500 mobiles +0.015 µs (the notoriety commit); both are the v2 commits' cost and inside the gate. `bench-000098` (cc016b1fa) agreed: funnel 0x78 +0.06/+0.07/+0.075 µs. Noise: within-arm spreads 2–20 % (one 91 % outlier on a 0.024 µs row).
- **FrameStats:** not run: no per-frame code changed (the check runs only under `-ecscheck`; the commits are in packet operations; `World.Update`'s picked-up removal runs once per pick-up). The owner runs the T1 final series on a quiet machine.
- **Memory:** `ItemData` (Stamp 8 B, Amount 2 B, Layer 1 B: a 16-byte column) replaces `Amount` (2 B): +14 B per item record, about 0.35 MB per client at the large scene's 25k items; the cold components (name, vitals, notoriety, price) only where set; the check's two lists and the vendor sort's list are reused. No pool or cache added.
- **Codex audit** (gpt-6-astra, read-only, after bench-000095; `astra-t1p9/out.md` in the session scratchpad). Dispositions, commits fd39f45f9, 92b2bfb8e, 291da6a1b, cc016b1fa, d78d708b0, b21d9e2b8, dea7562a9, 4bdee3906, a738a7c6d:
  - *Gate crash and the runner's exit code.* P1 (fixed): `EcsSchema.CreateSchema` registered none of the six new components, so NativeAOT's schema (which the client uses, JIT or not) threw at the first commit. The unit tests never saw it: a test process can build Friflo's reflection schema before `WorldMirror` registers, and that schema has every type. The schema now registers EntityName, Vitals, MobileNotoriety, ItemPrice and ItemData and lists what it registered (`EcsSchema.RegisteredTypes`); a test compares the list with every IComponent/ITag type of ClassicUO.Ecs. The job exited 0 because job-gate.sh ended with `exit 0` and `run_parity.py` returned 0 whatever the client did: run_parity now exits 1 on an abnormal client exit and 2 on a timeout, and the job verifies every client log (run_parity exit, no exception line, login reached, the script's `quit` reached, an `[ECS] check` ran, 0 ECS/parity/mobile-check mismatches, no WorldWriter or pre-T1 line), printing a `FAIL <script>: <why>` line per failure and ending `GATE FAIL` with exit 1 (dry-run on bench-000095's logs: 5 FAIL lines per script). The job also prints the uistate step evidence as `UISTATE FAIL <step>` lines and a `UISTATE PASS|FAIL n` verdict, apart from the checkers' verdict.
  - *Vendor sort.* P2 (fixed): 0x74 `BuyList` sorted a 0x2AF8 shop container's list by X outside the funnel. `WorldWriter.SortShopContents` computes the stable order by X first (insertion sort: equal X keep their list order, as the merge sort), re-stamps each held child in it, then sorts the list as before (admission and nesting as every operation). A search for other reorders of a world object's child list (`SortContents`, `Insert`, `MoveToFront`, `MoveToBack`, `Clear`, `Remove`/`Unlink`) found only macros and gumps besides this, `World.UnlinkFromContainer` (every caller changes the Container, see below) and the spellbook's `Clear`. Tests: arrival order differs from X (and equal X), an unstamped sort is a mismatch, a nested sort is rejected.
  - *Attachment vs Container.* P2 (fixed): the mirror represents attachment as `ItemData.Stamp` (0 = in no parent's child list). `UpsertItem` takes `attach` (the operation's PushToBack: the next stamp in the same write); a change of parent without it detaches; the same parent keeps its place. So an item equipped before its wearer exists is an orphan (Container set, stamp 0) and stays one when the wearer is created (legacy unchanged: ClassicUO never adopts it); the spellbook's clear detaches the held children it drops (`WorldEcs.CommitDetach`, before the clear); both re-keys re-stamp the children in list order; removal deletes the record. `-ecscheck` v2 compares a parent's list with its attached children only. Tests: orphan equip then re-attach, an attached item re-equipped onto a wearer that does not exist yet, moves to the ground, between containers and between wearers without a push, the spellbook clear then re-attach.
  - *Equipment-list cost.* P2 (fixed): profiling by elimination, not a profiler: making the stamp part of the item commit (no first-stamp archetype move, no second lookup) did not move the 0x78 rows (bench-000096: still +0.25–0.42 µs, and the *old-path* row too), so the cost was the extra column every item record carried (ItemLayer, then ItemSlot) through its create, its move to the wearer and its delete, five times per packet. `ItemData { Stamp, Amount, Layer }` replaces `Amount`, so an item's archetype has the base's width again; the commit writes the three fields with the one lookup the Amount write had, and a new record is created with them (bench-000097, bench-000098, bench-000099: within the gate, above). Warmup: one full pass.
  - *Stamp wrap.* P3 (fixed): the counter is 64-bit (never wraps: 584 years at a billion stamps a second); `WorldMirror.Clear` resets it (no record, so no live stamp, is left). Test: three stamps across the old 32-bit boundary keep their order; Clear resets.
  - *ECS-first operations are not transactional.* Disposition: kept as is, no transactions. The admission and the hold checks run before the first commit, and no later rejection exists in the re-key or the Set* operations. What can still throw after the first commit is `Entity.Hits`/`HitsMax`'s `RefreshHitsPercentage` (`RenderedText.Create` of "[n%]": a pooled object and a string; it throws only on out-of-memory) and the re-key's table writes (Dictionary remove/insert, field writes; out-of-memory only). And no exception on the packet path is caught: bench-000095 shows one ends the client (`Unhandled exception`, exit 0xE0434352), so a partial state is never observed by a running client.
  - *Also found by the gate:* the map change (0xBF.08 at the partner's login, `World.MapIndex`) wrote the player's X, Y, Z, Steps and Offset directly (`SetInWorldTile`, `ClearSteps`): now `MoveMobile` and `StopMobile` after `ClearForMapChange`'s scope (b21d9e2b8; budget unchanged, the writes are in GameObject/Mobile). The uistate script and driver: the partner stood on Trammel (both now `[self set Map Felucca`), the trainer must be adjacent (ModernUO's VendorAI answers "vendor buy" within 1 tile under AOS), coins dropped into a bank box become account balance (the split uses arrows), "T1Pet" is not an acceptable name (Funnelpet), the trainer's Name has no title (removed by place), and the driver's `FindMine` compared a serial by reference, so `target mine` never matched (fixed; an unmatched target now warns and cancels the cursor).
  - *Mutations of the fixes* (`muts_audit.py`, `muts_audit2.py`, logs `mut_audit.log`, `mut_audit2.log` in scratch `t1-funnel-9`): 31 on cc016b1fa (schema 4, vendor sort 5, attachment and its commits 19, wrap and Clear 2, checker 1): 29 failed a test at first; "SetParent: a container change is not a move" and "a wearer change is not a move" survived (every test move passed through a ground state); d78d708b0's straight moves fail both: 31 of 31. The run_parity/job hardening, the map change and the driver are not unit-testable (Client.Game); the gate covers them.
- **Codex audit, round 2** (gpt-6-astra, read-only, of the fixes 883f7c8c4..e5e807811; `astra-t1p9b/out.md`): no production regression; schema, attachment, the vendor sort (stable, the same comparer as `SortContents<Item>`), the counter reset, the `ItemData` merge and the map change checked and fine. P2 (fixed by the coordinator in the scratch job scripts `job-gate2.sh`/`job-gate3.sh`): the verifier missed checker warnings (the logger writes `Warning`, not `WARN`), the parity view-effect counters on continuation lines, and a non-zero `run_parity` exit code on its own. It now fails on any `Warning` line from `[mobile-update-check]`, `[mobile-input-check]`, `[PARITY]`, `[ECS]` (driver lines excepted) or `[funnel]`, on `(mirror|frameinfo|lights)-mismatched=` or `mismatching` above 0, and on rc != 0. Re-run over bench-000101's six logs: 0 FAILs; each injected case gives 1 FAIL. P3 (fixed): the driver's `find` printed `mine=False` always (`ReferenceEquals` of a serial with the player); now `RootContainer == player.Serial`.
- **Left:** the quiet-machine FrameStats series (owner); the two appearance gumps (not reachable by the driver); the test character's leftovers from earlier runs (a bag, a cap and w5boat's spellbooks in kbatman3's pack: the cleanup removes one of each graphic it added, so the count stays constant; a one-off `[remove` job can clear them).

## T2: container contents owned by the ECS (2026-10-31, `bg/ecs-t2-contents`)

Base `poc/modern-client` bfe7e4bc7 (T1 part 9 merged). Commits 739f51d05 (step 1: `WorldState.Contents`), 48ccfed4c (step 2: `CUO_CONTENTS_CHECK`), efaf976c2 (step 3: the readers behind `ecs_read_contents`), 15db78c98 (step 4: the two-way reader tests), 0024007b0 (gate tooling), da1b07e7f (the release variant compiles the tests), the Codex audit round 1887f50bc (fixes), 51ec4fb5f (gate tooling), 3287f9530 and e073c756c (tests), and these docs. Plan: ecs-transition-plan.md, T2. `ecs_read_contents` stays **off** by default (the coordinator flips it).

- **Step 1, `WorldState.Contents(parent)` (739f51d05).** `World.State` (new, `Game/Ecs/WorldState.cs`) reads the world state the ECS owns. `Contents(parent)` is the parent's attached children (`ItemData.Stamp != 0`, worn or contained: both indexes, as -ecscheck v2) in stamp order, i.e. the `LinkedObject` list (arrival order, a re-push to the back; orphans and the spellbook's detached entries are not in it). Friflo's index order is not stable across removes, so `WorldMirror` keeps a per-parent sorted `uint[]` (a slot: array, count, valid), built on the first read after a change (the index's attached children into a reused `(stamp, serial)` scratch, sorted by stamp; stamps are unique) and invalidated by every change of attachment: `UpsertItem` (attach, detach, a move: old and new parent, compared by stamp), `StampChild` (the vendor sort's re-stamp), `DetachChild` (the spellbook's clear), `Remove` (the parent of an attached child; a removed parent's own slot is released), `Clear` (all). Nothing is tracked until the first read: with no cached parent the writes skip the invalidation (one `Count` test). A cached read is a dictionary lookup and a span, no allocation (test: 1,000 reads, 0 bytes). Released slots keep their arrays (up to 64 free slots). New component `SpellbookContent { ulong Spells }` (registered in the NativeAOT schema): 0xBF.1B's spell set.
- **Step 2, `CUO_CONTENTS_CHECK=1` (48ccfed4c; CUO_DEVTOOLS builds only).** At every `Contents`/`Children`/`HasChildren` read, and every frame for each open `ContainerGump`, `GridLootGump`, `SpellbookGump` and both boxes of a `TradingGump` (`WorldEcs.Update` → `WorldState.CheckOpenContainers`), the ECS enumeration (the spellbook's entries for its set, then `Contents`) must equal the World child list, serials and order: a difference logs `[contents] mismatch (<where>) children of <parent>: World ... | ECS ...` (Warning, 25 logged) and every 5 s while the counts change `[contents] checks reads=… gumps=… mismatches=… | read_contents=on|off cached parents=… builds=… invalidations=… cache bytes=…`. The spellbook's spell entries are ClassicUO's detached items (serial and amount = spell number, graphic 0x1F2E) at the front of the book's list; the funnel now commits their set: `FillSpellbook` (`CommitSpellbook` before its cache writes) and `ClearContainer` (a clear drops them: the set goes to 0, committed first).
- **Step 3, the readers (efaf976c2).** `WorldState.Children(parent)` returns a `ref struct` for a foreach: with `ecs_read_contents` on, the spell entries then `Contents` looked up in `World.Items`; off, the `LinkedObject` list walked as the old loops did (the next link read after the body). `HasChildren` replaces `!IsEmpty`. The spell entries: `FillSpellbook` hands the entries it creates to `WorldState` with the set they stand for; `SpellEntries(book)` returns them only while the mirror's set is that set (a clear, a refill or the book's removal makes them stale; never returned). The setting: `ecs_read_contents` (settings.json, default false); `CUO_ECS_READ_CONTENTS=1|0` overrides it in CUO_DEVTOOLS builds (the gate); driver `readcontents on|off`. Reader inventory (every walk of a container's child list in the client; branch line numbers):
  - *Converted* (15 readers, 26 sites): `ContainerGump.ItemsOnAdded` (IsEmpty 543, the item loop 549) and `Dispose` (the child gumps, 720); `GridLootGump` (216, both display groups); `ItemGump`'s double-click loot (`IsEmpty`, 277); `SpellbookGump` (204: the entries then the book's items); `TradingGump` (164, 219: both boxes); the shop lists: 0x24's vendor branch 0x30 (`PacketHandlers` 1465, reversed unless 0x2AF8) and 0x74 `BuyList` (2833–2851, after `SortShopContents`, whose re-stamp invalidates the shop's slot); `Entity.FindItem` (236, 263: the counters, `FindBandage`), `Entity.GetItemByGraphic` (289, 297–299, with its legacy quirk: the deep search walks the entity's own children again); `Item.GetTotalAmount` (575); `Mobile.GetSecureTradeBox` (310: the trade box on the player); `PlayerMobile.FindItemInContainerRecursive`/`FindItemByClilocInContainerRecursive` (175–214: `FindItemByGraphic`, `FindItemByCliloc`, `FindPreferredItemByCliloc`: the macros' potions, bandages, trap boxes) and `GetTotalAmountOfItem` (251, 257: the counters); `Profile.SaveItemsGumpRecursive` (453: the open container gumps saved at logout); the driver's `contents` (448, so uistate's evidence is the reader path).
  - *Not converted, why:* `Entity.FindItemByLayer` (318) and `MobileView`'s `IsEmpty` (338, 1106, 1176): equipment, T3 (`ecs_read_equipment`), and per-frame hot paths. The writers of the list and the funnel's own resolution (`WorldWriter` 713–771 ClearContainer, 1040–1070 ClearWornItems, 2350 FillSpellbook, 2415 SortShopContents, 2671–2682 the re-key, 3130 RemoveBankContents, 3407/3463 subtree collection; `World` 1137–1186 the removal plumbing; `PlayerMobile.CloseBank` 411/419; `PacketHandlers` 1480 and 2834–2836, the switch-off branches): the list is maintained (dual) until T9, and these read it to maintain it. The checkers (`WorldEcs` 672 the old re-key path, 947 -ecscheck v2; `WorldState`'s comparison). Dev tools (`DevBench` 515/1085/2011, `EcsSessionDriver` 173/478/907/935/1024–1028 `FindChild`/`FindWorn`/`FindInBackpack`/`worn`, `EcsInspector` 84): they pick targets or dump state for scripts; `contents` was converted because the gate's uistate evidence uses it.
  - Orphans (an item equipped or contained before its parent existed: Container set, stamp 0) are in no list and in no `Contents`; corpses (their equipment layered by `PlaceCorpseEquipment`, the loot by 0x3C), trade boxes (contained in the player at layer 0), the bank box (`RemoveBankContents` removes its records, so its slot empties) and the vendor's shop containers (re-stamped by the sort) go through the same stamps.
- **Step 4, tests (15db78c98; `WorldStateContentsTests`, `WorldStateCheckTests`, `WorldStateReaderTests`, 69 new).** Contents: a funnel world (pack with a re-push, worn items, a 0x78 wear, a returned held item, a corpse with laid equipment, a bag, a shop, a spellbook) read for every parent, then 20 kinds of change with every parent cached (a push, a re-push, a new child, a move between containers, to the ground, a removal, a container's removal, an equip, a re-equip, an unequip, an orphan then its attachment, the spellbook clear, the vendor sort, a clear, a corpse clear keeping its equipment, the re-key old and new, a mobile's removal, the mirror's clear, a removal in the middle then two pushes): each parent's contents equal its held child list, read twice; a change elsewhere or of another field (name, price) builds nothing. Check: every one of those changes checks clean; seven deliberate divergences (the list's order, a stray child, a missing child, a mirror-only detach, a mirror-only re-stamp, a spell set, the entries dropped) are each reported at a read and at the gump check; off, nothing is compared. Readers: every testable reader gives the same result with the switch off and on (`FindItem` least hue and a hue, including the legacy quirk that finds a spell entry for 0x1F2E; `FindBandage`; `GetItemByGraphic` with and without the deep search; `GetTotalAmount`; `GetSecureTradeBox`; `FindItemByGraphic`, `FindItemByCliloc`, `FindPreferredItemByCliloc`; `HasChildren`; `Children` for every parent as the same objects in the same order, the book's entries included); on a world whose list was changed behind the funnel, ten readers follow the ECS with the switch on and the list with it off; the spell entries go stale with their set; a walk allocates nothing either way. The gumps, the shop handlers, Profile's save and `GetTotalAmountOfItem` need the UI or the tile data and are covered by the gate.
- **Mutations** (scratch `t2-contents`: `muts_t2.py`, `mut_t2.log`): 45 deliberate breakages (the mirror's cache maintenance, the switch, `Children`/`HasChildren`, the checker's comparisons, the spell entries' staleness and hand-over, the off walk's next-link timing, every converted reader made to ignore the switch, and the audit fixes: the leaf guard both ways, the displaced re-key detach, the eager spell-entry drops at destruction, at a set commit and for an empty set, the unconditional mirror clear, the spell-storage accounting), run with `mutate.py` on the T2 filter (150 then 154 tests): every one fails a test. The first run (51ec4fb5f) left three survivors, closed by tests in 3287f9530 and re-run: a direct `Mirror.Remove` of an attached child (the funnel always detaches first, so only a mirror-level test sees it), a removed parent's own slot (memory only), and the recursive finders' `HasChildren` (a bag whose list was emptied behind the funnel; the cliloc twin added as a 45th mutant). The old "next read before the body" mutant skipped nodes; it is now a real read-ahead (`_ahead`), killed by a test whose body pushes a child while the last one is visited. `A_Walk_Allocates_Nothing_Both_Ways` failed as a bystander in 15 of 45 runs (the tiered JIT allocating on the thread): it now takes the least of three rounds after a warm-up (e073c756c).
- **Verification:** 2,253 passed + 6 skipped in both variants (CuoDevTools true and false) at 51ec4fb5f; at e073c756c 2,257 passed + 6 skipped in both variants. The player-world T2 tests run in the non-parallel collection: they set the static `Time.Ticks` and `RandomHelper` seed, and once made `The_Boat_Steps_Equal_The_Old_Path` flake. Both client builds (CuoDevTools true and false) succeed at 51ec4fb5f (the client code is unchanged after it). Write-site budget 138 → 138 (regenerated with `CUO_WRITE_BUDGET_REGEN=1`: no pair changed; the spell entries' writes stay in `FillSpellbook`'s body, `WorldState` writes no A field).
- **Gate:** the hardened recipe (ls_parity on the large scene, w5items, w5push, w5boat, uistate + the kbatman2 partner; every checker plus `CUO_CONTENTS_CHECK=1`) at 51ec4fb5f (bin-new, CuoDevTools=true; the later commits change tests only). **Off** (`CUO_ECS_READ_CONTENTS=0`): bench-000104 GATE PASS, UISTATE PASS. **On** (`=1`): bench-000106 GATE PASS, UISTATE PASS, E2 GATE PASS, E2 T2 ROWS PASS. (bench-000105, the first on run, failed on the environment: ls_parity's login was refused 4 s after the previous job's logout, and uistate's horse died between the rename and its target; neither involves a reader, and the rerun passed.) Both: 0 `[contents] mismatch`, 0 `[ECS] mismatch`, every summary `mismatches=0` (on: uistate reads=61 and 655,767 per-frame gump comparisons, w5boat 519,360; ls_parity at 25,134 items / 1,985 mobiles with -ecscheck clean).
- **Screenshots:** bench-000104 (`t2shots.txt`: the backpack, 27 items, and an orc's corpse, 5 items, opened with the switch off and shot, closed, reopened with it on and shot; since 51ec4fb5f the containers are placed at fixed positions with the driver's new `place` and the scripted cursor parked with `mouse 600 300` before each shot, after the kill message has faded). UI layer 640x480: 108 differing pixels, all in (370,92)-(415,111): the corpse gump's skull eyes, which animate (yellow in one shot, red in the other); screen 960x720: 392 pixels at the same spot, scaled. The containers and their contents are pixel-identical. (bench-000102, before the placement: 55k differing pixels, all from the reopened gumps' cascade position, the tooltip under the cursor and the fading kill message.)
- **E2:** bench-000106, 3x3 interleaved, TieredCompilation=0, base bfe7e4bc7 vs new 51ec4fb5f: E2 GATE PASS (every paired row within +0.1 us or 2x its spread, bytes equal). The T2 rows, cached against their nothing-cached control in the same run (sizes 500/2000/8000): 0x25 new + delete -0.03 to -0.00 us, 0x25 update +0.02 us, 0x2E re-equip +0.01 us, 0x78 list +0.03 to +0.20 us (+0.9 to +5.2 %, within 2x spread of 6-10 %; its bytes are 1,400 against the control's 1,819, the second-run effect above), all 0 B except the 0x25 new item's 140 B in both; the read row (an update plus a build of the 6-item backpack) +0.04 us over the cached update, 0 B. E2 T2 ROWS PASS.
- **FrameStats:** not run. No per-frame path changes with the checker off: the readers run on events (a container's item added, a gump built, a counter's timer, a macro); the per-frame open-container comparison runs only under `CUO_CONTENTS_CHECK`. With the switch on, a counter's periodic walk reads cached spans instead of following links (cheaper or equal).
- **Memory** (the deliberate-tradeoffs convention), layout-based accounting (computed from the 64-bit object layouts and capacities, not measured with a heap tool; corrected in the Codex audit round 2, below): `ContentsCacheBytes` and `WorldState.SpellEntriesBytes` now count by the 64-bit layout with every capacity (the dictionaries' buckets and entries per slot of capacity, the slots and their arrays, cached and free, the free-slot stack, the sort scratch; the spell storage's sets and `Item[64]` arrays), and the 5 s summary logs both. On the large scene (ls_parity, 25,134 items and 1,985 mobiles in view) the contents cache holds **3,220 B** and the spell storage **80 B**, with the switch off and on: nothing there reads a container, so only the empty structures exist (the dictionary's 64-entry capacity, the 1 KB scratch). The most any gate script reached is **3,812 B** (uistate, switch on: three cached parents after a backpack, a bank, a corpse, a spellbook, a trade and a vendor) and 3,708 B on the partner. Only parents a reader read are cached (open containers and what counters and macros walk); a parent's slot goes with its record, and a book's spell entries go with its record or its set (also at the bank's, a map change's and login's removals): the spell storage was back to 80 B at every script's end. `SpellbookContent` is 8 B on a book's record. The entries' `Item` objects are not counted: the book's child list holds the same objects until T9. Benefit: a cached read is a span (no link chasing); cost: a dictionary lookup per change of attachment while any parent is cached (E2: +0.00 to +0.03 us per packet on the 0x25/0x2E rows, 0 B).
- **Codex audit** (gpt-6-astra, `bfe7e4bc7..0024007b0`; each finding and its disposition): (1) P1, a spellbook's detached spell entries (serial 1-64) aliased a real mobile of that serial, so a recursive reader could find another mobile's items or loop (player at serial 1 -> pack -> book -> spell 1 -> player): **fixed** (1887f50bc): `Children` treats an instance World does not hold for its serial as a leaf with the switch on (its own list, unchecked, with it off); tests with the player at serial 1 and with another mobile at serial 1, both ways, checker on, plus a replaced instance. (2) P2, a re-key onto an occupied dead serial left the displaced mobile's attachments in the mirror (switch on: the new dead mobile showed the old one's equipment): **fixed**: `RekeyDeadMobile` detaches the displaced children (`CommitDetach`) before attaching the incoming list; tested cold and warm, with and without incoming equipment, the displaced mobile equipped. (3) P2, removed books kept their spell materialisations until logout: **fixed**: dropped at the record's destruction (`OnDestroyed`: a removal, a container's removal, the bank's, a map change's, login's) and at every set commit (a clear, a refill; an empty set is not stored); tested for each without another read; the storage and the dictionary capacities are in the memory log, measured on the gates (above). Also from its notes: `World.Clear` now always clears the contents cache (slots of parents without a record survived when the mirror was already empty). (4) P2, the release tests did not compile: already fixed in da1b07e7f; both variants build and pass (above). (5) P2, the gate's E2 T2 check did not gate: **fixed** in the scratch tooling: `e2t2.py` requires every row and size, fails a cached row over +0.1 us beyond 2x the spread (the E2 gate's rule) and any row that allocates more, exits 1, and the job turns that into FAIL. The pair is now a "T2 control" row run just before the cache is warmed (51ec4fb5f), because a repeated row differs from its first run without any cache (the 0x78 list: 1,400 B/packet on its first run, 1,819 on its second, measured with nothing cached; against the earlier T1 sibling the new check failed bench-000103 for a reason that is not T2). The job also fails on a failed uistate step now (bench-000103 printed GATE PASS with UISTATE FAIL 4). (6) P3, divergences were only checked through `Contents`/`CheckParent`: **fixed**: each of the seven divergences is reported through `Children` and `HasChildren` with the switch off and on; the "next read before body" mutant is now a real read-ahead, killed by a test of the link-read timing. The pre-fix gates (bench-000102 off, bench-000103 on, at 0024007b0) had 0 `[contents] mismatch` and 0 `[ECS]` mismatches in every script; 000103's uistate failed the trade steps because the partner character was a ghost (`uistate_partner.txt` now starts with `[self res`).
- **Recommendation:** flip `ecs_read_contents` to **on** by default: both gates pass with it on and off with zero contents and ECS mismatches, the shots match except the animated skull, E2's cached rows are within the gate with no added allocation, and the audit's three correctness findings are fixed and tested. The coordinator decides; it is not flipped here.
- **Left:** the default flip (coordinator); T3 (the equipment readers: `FindItemByLayer`, `MobileView`); T9 deletes the container half of the list (and with it the spell entries' hand-over). The 0x78 row's 1,400/1,819 B alternation between runs is pre-existing (nothing cached) and not investigated.
- **Codex audit, round 2** (gpt-6-astra, read-only, of `da1b07e7f..aace052fa`; `astra-t2b/out.md`): no correctness defect left in the round-1 fixes (identity, re-key, spell entries, `World.Clear`, the switch-off walk). Three findings, fixed in d995a847f, 316f60917 and 291ce3f1a:
  - **P2, the driver's `mouse` override could outlive the script** (a script ending without `mouse off`, or a disconnect, left `Input.Mouse.Override` set for the rest of the dev process). **Fixed** (d995a847f): the driver owns its override (`OwnsMouse`) and releases it at the end of the script (EOF), at `quit` and `logout`, when its gump is disposed, when the world is no longer in game (disconnect), and when a line throws (`Step` catches, releases and rethrows); an override the driver did not set (DevBench's) is left alone. `EcsSessionDriverMouseTests` (4 tests, by reflection: the driver is CUO_DEVTOOLS only and the tests are compiled without the define; in the dev variant they assert the type exists, so they cannot pass vacuously there) drives `Step` over in-memory lines: EOF, `mouse off`, a throwing line, the detach path and the not-owned case. The gump's `Dispose` and the not-in-game branch only call `ReleaseMouse` (they need a running UI and are covered by reading, not by a test).
  - **P2, the 0x78 E2 control did not prove "no added allocation"** (control and cached ran back to back on one mutated scene: 1,819 B vs 1,400 B per packet, so +256 B in the cached path would have passed). **Fixed** (316f60917, `e2t2.py` in the scratch): the T2 funnel rows now run on three freshly built scenes with the same preparation and the same rows in the same order, `T2 control` (nothing cached), `T2 cached` (the backpack and every mobile cached before the warm-up) and `T2 control2` (nothing cached), the controls bracketing the cached scene. `e2t2.py` fails when the two controls allocate differently (BASELINE) and when a cached row allocates more than the control (BYTES); self-test with synthetic inputs: equal rows PASS, cached 0x78 at 1,656 B FAIL BYTES, control2 at 1,819.4 B FAIL BASELINE. **bench-000107** (E2 only, base bfe7e4bc7 vs 291ce3f1a, 3x3 interleaved, TieredCompilation=0): E2 GATE PASS (every paired row within the gate, bytes equal) and E2 T2 ROWS PASS. On the fresh scenes the two controls and the cached row allocate the same at every size (0x25 new: 140 B; 0x25 update and 0x2E: 0 B; 0x78: 1,504.9 B), so cached <= control now holds on equal scenes. Time, cached vs control: 0x25 new -0.003 / -0.002 / +0.010 us (500 / 2,000 / 8,000 mobiles), 0x25 update +0.023 / +0.017 / +0.014, 0x2E +0.027 / +0.027 / +0.027, 0x78 -0.374 / -0.447 / -0.380 (all within +0.1 us); the second control is up to 0.7 us faster than the first on 0x78 (the first fresh scene's run pays a time-order effect), so the cached rows are timed against the slower, earlier control; within-arm spreads (2x) 1-25 %. Open item, not investigated (predates T2): the 0x78 list allocates 1,400 B/packet on its first run on the main scene, 1,819 B on a repeat there and 1,504.9 B on a fresh scene.
  - **P3, the memory accounting** omitted the buckets' alignment, the `ValueCollection` that `.Values` creates once and the dictionary keeps (24 B each), and WorldWriter's permanent spell-entry scratch list (List 32 B + `Item[64]` 536 B = 568 B). **Fixed** (291ce3f1a): `WorldMirror.DictionaryBytes` (object 80 B, buckets 24 B + 4 B per slot 8-aligned, entries 24 B + 24 B per slot, the ValueCollection 24 B) serves both formulas, `SpellEntriesBytes` adds `WorldState.SpellScratchBytes` (568 B; a book has at most 64 spells, so the list never grows), and both are documented as layout-based accounting. Corrected by the layout (not re-measured on the client this round): the empty spell storage is 672 B, not 80 B; the contents cache grows by 24 B (+4 B at an odd bucket capacity), so the large scene's 3,220 B is about 3,248 B and uistate's 3,812 B about 3,840 B. Test `The_Layout_Accounting_Counts_Alignment_The_ValueCollection_And_The_Spell_Scratch` pins the numbers.
  - **Note, the walk-allocation test** (`A_Walk_Allocates_Nothing_Both_Ways`): the least of three rounds proved one allocation-free round of 200 walks, not that every round is clean, so an intermittent allocation could pass. A first stricter try (every round in which this thread compiled nothing, `JitInfo.GetCompiledMethodCount(currentThread: true)`, must allocate 0) failed in the full suite with 7,520 B in a round with no method compiled on the thread, so the JIT counter cannot excuse the test host's noise, and tiering cannot be switched off for one test inside the shared host. Now (291ce3f1a): a warm-up round, then six judged rounds; the least must be 0 and at most ONE round may allocate. An allocation at least once per 600 walks lands in two or more of the six rounds and fails; the trade-off left: a rarer one (less than once per 600 walks) can still hide in the one tolerated round. Three full dev-variant runs and eight isolated runs passed.
  - **Verification:** tests 2262 pass + 6 skipped in both CuoDevTools variants (2257 + the 4 driver tests + the layout test; the driver tests pass trivially in the release variant, which has no driver). Mutations (`muts_r2.py`, `mut_r2.log`), 7 of 7 fail a test: no release at EOF, no release when a line throws, release clearing an override the driver does not own (2 tests), no ValueCollection, unaligned buckets, no spell scratch, and `FindItem` allocating once per 500 calls (fails the walk test; the least-of-three version, rounds of walks 200-799, sees it in one round only and passes, by the arithmetic above). The E2 gate change has no unit test (a bench); its check was mutated through `e2t2.py`'s synthetic inputs (above). Budget unchanged (138).
- **Merged and default on** (coordinator, 2026-11-01): merged as 751c016f1; `ecs_read_contents` defaults to on (the off/on gates bench-000104/106, the screenshots, E2 bench-000106/107, two Codex audits). The off path and `CUO_CONTENTS_CHECK` stay for one phase (T9 deletes the container half of the linked list). Two tests changed with the default: `The_Switch_Is_On_By_Default`, and `GetSecuredTradeBox`'s three legacy tests pin the switch off, because their mobile is built outside every World table and so reads as a leaf with the switch on (the P1 rule); `WorldStateReaderTests` covers `GetSecureTradeBox` both ways on a World that holds its objects.

## T3a: equipment owned by the ECS (2026-11-01, `bg/ecs-t3-equipment`)

Base `poc/modern-client` 064f8f735 (T2 merged, `ecs_read_contents` on). Plan: ecs-transition-plan.md, T3 (state and readers only; the layering rules as data are T3b). Commits bb85edd26 (step 1), 8e372d76e (step 2), 26fb523d4 (step 3), 281d1438d and 84f6d7692 (step 4), a68633620 (step 5 tests), 663c20a61, d018a2477 and 5b443e3d2 (gate tooling), 9ec5c87e2, ce34c22ab and e0d2e046b (the E2 rounds), b4b197409 (the mutation survivors' tests), and these docs. `ecs_read_equipment` stays **off** by default.

- **Parked (the park rule): the funnel's WornLayers maintenance on 0x78 is over the E2 gate.** Before: 064f8f735. After: bb85edd26 (the maintenance), tuned in 9ec5c87e2, ce34c22ab, e0d2e046b. bench-000114 (3x3 interleaved, TC=0, base 064f8f735 vs e0d2e046b): the 0x78 equipment-list rows (ClearWornItems + 5 WearItem) +0.11 to +0.36 us per packet (+3.5 to +9.8 %, within-arm 2x spreads 2-9 %), OVER on 7 of 12 rows (T1 funnel at 8000 mobiles +0.357 us; the T2 control/cached/control2 scenes +0.11 to +0.25 us); 0x2E re-equip +0.03 to +0.04 us (beyond the spread, under +0.1 us); the serial-reuse row +0.05 us with +4 B per packet (BYTES: the `Mobile.EquipCache` reference, +8 B per Mobile object; a mobile is created every other packet). Profiled with an in-process probe and four E2 rounds: bench-000108 (first version: 0x78 +0.3-0.5 us, every departure rescanned the wearer's index; the read +57 %), bench-000112 (per-layer counts spare the rescans; the read moved to a per-mobile cache: the read now -47 to -53 %; serial reuse +62 %), bench-000113 (no component read-backs in UpsertItem: unchanged), bench-000114 (WornLayers folded into `EquipmentSlots`: an 11th component on the mobile archetype made Friflo's delete + create 6x slower, 0.40 against 0.06 us in populated archetypes; serial reuse back to +0.05 us; and the mirror's last-wearer cache keyed on mobile removals only, so 0x78's item removals keep it). Best hypothesis for what is left: one `GetComponent<EquipmentSlots>` per departure and per arrival (two per worn item per 0x78: the clear removes, the wear adds), ~10-15 ns each, plus the slot bookkeeping; 5 items x 2 x ~25 ns is the measured +0.15-0.35 us. Not contained behind a switch: WornLayers is the state the readers and `EquipmentSlots` (step 2) read, so maintaining it only with the switch on would need the index-order rebuild back for the off path and a full rebuild at every switch flip. The owner decides: accept (about 0.03 us per worn-item change, a few hundred per second in a crowd), or move the bookkeeping into the friflo write the funnel already does (one component access instead of two) in T4.
- **Step 1, `WornLayers` (bb85edd26; folded into `EquipmentSlots.Worn` in e0d2e046b).** Per mobile record, for layers 0x01..0x1D (slot `layer - 1`): the serial of the first item *attached* to the mobile on that layer, i.e. the lowest child-order stamp among the attached items there, which is what `FindItemByLayer` finds first in the child list; a per-layer count of attached items (a departure rescans the wearer's equipment index only when another item is left on the layer); a version (a never-reused value bumped at every slot change). Maintained only by the mirror from attachment (`ItemData.Stamp != 0`): `UpsertItem` (attach, detach, a re-push, a layer or wearer change: leave the old place, enter the new one, with the values it wrote), `Remove` (an attached worn item leaves), `StampChild` (the old re-key's re-stamp; the vendor sort), `DetachChild` (the displaced re-key), and a mobile record created over children still attached under its serial (rebuilt from the index; normally none). Equipment that arrives before its mobile (stamp 0) is never worn, as ClassicUO never links it; that behaviour is unchanged. Layer 0 (the trade boxes) and layers above 0x1D are not tracked (the reader takes the list for them). `WorldMirror.Worn(mobile, layer)`, `WornCount`.
- **Step 2, the equipment-order stamp (8e372d76e).** The order of a wearer's equipment is its child-order stamps: `MobileAnimationSystem.Rebuild` builds `EquipmentSlots` from WornLayers instead of the first item per layer in the order of the mirror's equipment index (so an orphan in the index is no longer drawn by the Gpu world, which the list never drew either), and nothing reads the index's own order any more. `WorldWriter.ReturnHeldItem`'s paperdoll branch commits once, attached (the next stamp: the back of the list), instead of the detached state and then the wearer. The old-path comparisons keep checking the index order for every other operation and its members for ReturnHeldItem. `-ecscheck`'s equipment compare stayed at 0 on every gate script.
- **Step 3, `CUO_EQUIP_READ_CHECK=1` (26fb523d4; CUO_DEVTOOLS builds).** Every `FindItemByLayer` call on a mobile compares the child list's first item on the layer with the ECS's (the serial, 0 for none): `[equip] mismatch (FindItemByLayer) <mobile> layer <L>: World .. | ECS ..` (Warning, 25 logged) and every 5 s `[equip] checks reads=.. mismatches=.. | read_equipment=on|off mobiles=.. worn bytes=.. writes=.. rescans=.. | read caches=.. with items=.. bytes=.. refreshes=.. fills=..`.
- **Step 4, the readers behind `ecs_read_equipment` (281d1438d, 84f6d7692, tuned in 9ec5c87e2).** Settings `ecs_read_equipment` (default false); `CUO_ECS_READ_EQUIPMENT=1|0` overrides it in devtools builds; driver `readequipment on|off`. Every equipment reader goes through `Entity.FindItemByLayer`, which for a mobile with the switch on returns `WorldState.WornItem` (an item's own `FindItemByLayer`, a corpse's laid equipment, is unchanged); MobileView's three `!IsEmpty` guards read `WorldState.HasWornItems`. The read is served from a per-mobile cache (`Mobile.EquipCache`, a `WornCache`: the verified record and the Item objects of its slots; valid for the mirror's epoch, its slot-write count and the mobile's WornLayers version): a hit is three compares and an array load, a bare mobile's guard a null test. Identity (T2's rule, adapted): an instance World does not hold for its serial (the appearance gumps' detached preview mobile at serial 1, a replaced or destroyed mobile) reads its own list, never that serial's record; for equipment the own list rather than a leaf, because the preview's clothes are its only truth and a leaf would empty the creation paperdoll. Reader inventory (branch line numbers; full list in the handoff):
  - *Per frame, all drawn mobiles:* `MobileView` 152 (mount), 338-350 (the guard, `PaperdollOrder.BuildInWorld`, one `FindItemByLayer` per layer), 1025 and 1106-1110 (the pick), 1176-1419 (`IsCovered`'s ~20 reads); `Mobile.IsMounted`/`IsDrivingBoat` (206-229; used per frame by the animation update, overhead texts, name plates, health lines, `MobileAnimationSystem.IsMounted`); `MobileAnimation.GetAnimGroupInput`'s hands (60-81); `PaperdollOrder.GraphicsFromEntity` (182, behind `Build`/`BuildInWorld`); `PaperDollInteractable` 162/193/265 and `PaperdollGump` 431/477/567/759 while open.
  - *Events:* `PlayerMobile.UpdateAbilities` (307-311), the backpack/bank lookups (`PlayerMobile` 133/146/158/407, `GameActions` 235/824, `ContainerManager` 180, `ContainerGump` 47, `ItemGump` 279, `OptionsGump` 4447, `CounterBarGump` 157/162), `MacroManager` 848/1002/1010/1099/1106 (arm/disarm, bandages), `PacketHandlers` 1459 (the vendor's shop layers), `Pathfinder` 390, the character-creation preview (`OutgoingPackets` 380-420, `CreateCharAppearanceGump` 626/630/956: not held, so its own list).
  - *Not converted:* `ItemView` 276/628 and `ItemSpriteExtract` 271 (a corpse's laid equipment is an item's list, not a mobile's); the funnel's list walks and World's removal plumbing (maintained until T9); `-ecscheck`'s equipment compare (`WorldEcs` 1121/1150: it compares the reader with `EquipmentSlots`, so with the switch on it checks the ECS against the ECS's slots); dev tools (DevBench, EcsSessionDriver, EcsInspector).
  - *T2-owned (equipment scans already behind `ecs_read_contents` via `WorldState.Children`, not layer reads; T2's switch decides them):* `PlayerMobile.GetTotalAmountOfItem` (251), `Entity.FindItem` and `Entity.GetItemByGraphic` (Entity.cs 227/286, also on a mobile's children), `Mobile.GetSecureTradeBox` (Mobile.cs 310).
- **Step 5, tests (a68633620, b4b197409; `WornLayersTests`, `WorldStateEquipmentCheckTests`, `WorldStateEquipmentReaderTests`, plus `MobileRebuildTests`/`WorldWriterTests` additions).** WornLayers equals the lists' first item and count per layer for every mobile after each of T2's 20 kinds of change, two or three items on a layer (re-equip, removal, a move), a layer change, a move to another wearer, an orphan then its attachment, the returned held item, a record rebuilt over attached children and a direct removal of a still-attached first item, an orphan never chosen as the next. Checker: clean over the 20 changes both ways; six divergences (a list re-order, a layer in the cache only, a mirror-only detach, a mirror-only removal, a list-only unlink, a mirror-only re-stamp) each reported once, both ways, and the switch picks the source returned. Readers: every layer's item (the same object), the guard, `IsMounted`, `IsDrivingBoat` and the system's `IsMounted` are equal with the switch off and on after each of the 20 changes; mount, dismount and a tiller agree with `EquipmentSlots.Mounted`; the preview outside the World (serial 1, also a real mobile wearing a helmet) and a replaced mobile read their own lists, also after a cached read; a bare mobile removed with no slot write; an orphan is worn by neither; the re-key onto an occupied death serial wears only the incoming items (warm and cold, with and without one); untracked layers read the list; a slot change elsewhere refreshes without refilling; a read allocates nothing either way. `GetAnimGroupInput`, `UpdateAbilities`, `GraphicsFromEntity` and the paperdoll read the tile data, which the tests do not load: they are covered through `FindItemByLayer` here and by the gates (the checker, `-ecscheck`'s hands and mount compare, the shots).
- **Mutations** (`muts_t3.py`, `mut_t3.log`, `mut_t3_rerun.log` in the scratch): 39 deliberate breakages (the mirror's leave/enter/rescan/counts/rebuild/version/wearer cache, the slots' rebuild keeping WornLayers, ReturnHeldItem's single commit, the read cache's epoch/writes/version/identity, the not-held paths of the read and the guard, the switch in the reader and the guard, the checker's three ways to go blind): the first run left five survivors (the rescan's exclusion and attachment filter, the rebuild's counts, the version, the cache's epoch), closed by the tests in b4b197409 and re-run: **39 of 39 fail a test.**

Both: 0 `[equip] mismatch`, 0 `[contents] mismatch`, 0 `[ECS] mismatch`, every summary `mismatches=0`; the equipment compares per script (off / on): ls_parity 277.3M / 227.6M at 25,134 items and 1,985 mobiles, w5push 108.4M / 125.0M, w5items 37.8M / 41.2M, w5boat 13.7M / 14.5M, uistate 41.2M / 37.4M, partner 5.1M / 3.8M; parity on (ls_parity): 5.2M mobile and 1.38M item comparisons, 0 mismatched; rescans 0 everywhere (the counts). The scene shots cannot be pixel-identical while the scene animates; the equality evidence for the per-frame readers is the checker (227.6M per-call compares on the large scene with the switch on, 0 mismatches, every reader returning the ECS's item) and the parity compare.
- **E2:** bench-000114 (3x3, TC=0, base 064f8f735 vs e0d2e046b). So about 0.3 MB per client off and 0.86 MB on the large scene. Benefit: MobileView's per-mobile equipment reads half the list walk's time (E2), every frame for every drawn mobile.

(1, P2) `StampChild`/`DetachChild` changed WornLayers without marking the wearer `EquipmentDirty`, so a built, clean record kept stale slots, hands and mount (the re-key onto an occupied death serial, the old re-key, the vendor sort): both now dirty the wearer; tested through the normal dirty dispatch (`TakeDirty`, then a rebuild only when dirty). (2, P2) **Behaviour fix, changes the off path:** 0x2E keeps a backpack's link (no unlink for `Layer.Backpack`, as upstream ClassicUO's `PacketHandlers.EquipItem` and the base 064f8f735 both do), and the new wearer's `PushToBack` unlinks it only through its neighbours, so a backpack that was its old wearer's *first* child stayed that wearer's list head (cutting off the old wearer's other children) while the mirror moved it: `WorldWriter.Equip` now removes the kept link from its old parent's list (own commit f72c2fcac; the old-path reference `OldEquip` models the fix; tests: the lists and the reads both ways, the backpack first and not first). (3, P2) The per-layer byte count wrapped at 256: it saturates at 255 (255 or more) and a departure from a saturated layer rescans the wearer once for the exact count and the first item; the rebuild over attached children saturates too; tests at 255/256/257 attaches and departures, with and without reconstruction. (4, P3) A cached `NoRecord` never recovered when the record was created again without an epoch change: NoRecord is looked up again at every refresh; tests with the intervening read (with children, and bare then equipped). (5, P3) The checker compares the object as well as the serial, and checks `HasWornItems` against the list's tracked live equipment (held, not destroyed, layers 0x01..0x1D), not `!IsEmpty` (untracked-only children are legitimate): tests for another instance under the same serial, a guard divergence, and untracked-only checking clean. (6, P3) The version was the write counter truncated to 32 bits: `ulong` end to end (WornLayers 152 → 160 B, +8 B per mobile record, +15.9 KB on the large scene; `WornCache` stays 72 B, measured); tests past 2^32 in the mirror and through the reader. Also: the T2-owned equipment scans added to the reader inventory; the untracked-layer reader test now attaches items on layers 0 and 0x1E through the funnel. Each new test fails with its fix reverted (8 mutants, 8 killed). Tests 2,398 + 6 skipped in both variants; both client builds. Gates at e8fa275a5 (all checkers, `CUO_CONTENTS_CHECK=1`, `CUO_EQUIP_READ_CHECK=1`): off bench-000118 GATE PASS + UISTATE PASS, on bench-000119 GATE PASS + UISTATE PASS, 0 mismatches. E2 bench-000120 (base 064f8f735 vs e8fa275a5): E2 T2 ROWS PASS, E2 T3 ROWS PASS (MobileView reads -45 to -58 %); E2 GATE FAIL 4 on the parked rows only, unchanged in kind from bench-000114: the funnel's 0x78 +0.11 to +0.30 µs (one row OVER), 0x2E re-equip +0.03 µs (beyond spread, under +0.1 µs), serial reuse +0.04-0.06 µs and 236 -> 240 B (the `Mobile.EquipCache` reference), worn-item Sync +0.005-0.009 µs. No round-2 Codex audit (its weekly window was at 96 %); the coordinator reviewed the fix diff instead.
- **Recommendation:** the readers are correct both ways (both gates, 0 mismatches over ~0.9 billion per-call compares, the paperdoll shots identical up to the reopen and the animated rider) and the read is faster than the list walk; flip `ecs_read_equipment` to on once the owner accepts or resolves the parked 0x78 maintenance cost (it is paid with the switch off as well). The coordinator decides; not flipped here.

## T3b: equipment layering rules as data (2026-11-01, `bg/ecs-t3-layering`)

- **What:** ClassicUO's hard-coded layering rules as a pack data file, `layerrules.bin` (magic `LAYR`, pack-format.md "layerrules.bin"), and a data-driven evaluator behind the new setting `ecs_layer_rules` (default **off**; env `CUO_ECS_LAYER_RULES=1|0`, driver `layerrules on|off`). The hard-coded rules stay.
- **Rule inventory** (file:line table in cuo-poc-state handoffs/t3-layering.md): the base tables T1/T2/T3 and their selection (arms AnimIDs, torso 0x21A, the chest-under torso for women and gargoyles), eight reorders (pants/shirt/shoes, the surcoat tunic over the robe, the quiver cloak, helmet/neck, the 0x5E9 helmet over the robe), the world's cloak-by-direction move, `IsCovered`'s rules for shoes, pants, tunic, torso, arms, necklace, bracelet, hair and helmet (the hoods: 0x204E-F, 0x2683-7, 0x2FB9, 0x3173 on every body; 0x4B9D, 0x7816, 0xA0AB-F, 0xB2B7 on every body except gargoyles), skirt; the gargoyle draw remaps. Paperdoll and world run the same order and covering; the world adds the direction move and the remaps. No elf-specific rule exists (elves differ only in their paperdoll body gumps).
- **Format:** body groups (human, elf, gargoyle, male/female, other) from a body table; base tables; rules (select, reorder, cover, dirmove, remap) per set (paperdoll, world) with AND-ed conditions (present, graphic or AnimID in ranges, female / gargoyle-draw flags, body group). First match for select, cover and remap; every match in order for reorder and dirmove. Default file 3,023 B: 91 rules, 128 conditions, 186 ranges.
- **One source:** `Uo.Pack.LayerRulesDefault.Create()`. The converter writes it (`--only layers`; verify reports EXACT), and a client whose pack has no `layerrules.bin` uses the same `Create()`. **Pack change needed** (coordinator): publish the next version with `layerrules.bin` (`cp -al` CURRENT + `Uo.Converter --only layers --out <pack>`; the test pack is `<scratch>/t3-layering/pack-t3b`). Without it the client is unchanged (built-in rules).

The data path gathers a mobile's 24 layers once (FindItemByLayer) instead of IsCovered's repeated lookups.

The gate scripts' verify fails on any mismatch or warning line.
